The excerpted content does not provide all per-benchmark numbers, so the tables and appendices should be checked for exact deltas.4f:T6c7,The paper has two parts: diagnosing the phenomenon and then intervening on training. For diagnosis, the authors build a synthetic task called Spaced Retrieval, designed to isolate retrieval ability from the messiness of natural language. The task uses controllable source-target gaps, with training and evaluation using t=5 and gaps of 64 and 8192 to represent short- and long-range retrieval. They then introduce a layer-wise contribution attribution method to quantify how much each layer contributes to retrieval over the course of training. The purpose is to track who learns retrieval first and who gets suppressed later. On top of that, they run freezing and unfreezing interventions. When recurrent layers are allowed to train normally, they acquire retrieval behavior earlier. When their retrieval learning is manually blocked, attention layers begin learning retrieval almost immediately. This is strong evidence that attention is not inherently incapable; it is being outcompeted. The paper further shows that the winner depends on data distribution: natural language contains many more short-range than long-range patterns, and recurrent layers learn those short-range patterns faster, which gives them an early optimization advantage that spills over into retrieval. To address this, the authors propose Better Layer Division (BLD), a training pipeline that adds a preliminary stage before standard pretraining. During this stage, selected components are frozen so that full-attention layers get an early window to learn retrieval first. Standard pretraining then resumes, but from a more favorable specialization trajectory. The key idea is not extra capacity, but changing the order in which modules are allowed to learn.50:T54a,The experiments include both mechanism studies and end-to-end pretraining results. On the synthetic Spaced Retrieval task, the paper provides three kinds of evidence. First, layer-attribution trajectories show that recurrent/KDA layers take over retrieval earlier than attention. Second, freezing and later unfreezing gives a more causal result: once recurrent learning is stopped, attention’s retrieval contribution rises quickly. Third, changing the ratio of short- and long-distance patterns changes which mixer wins the competition, showing that the outcome is jointly determined by data distribution and learning speed. For realistic language modeling, the authors apply BLD to Kimi Delta Attention based hybrid LLMs at multiple scales and report gains over vanilla pretraining on training loss and several benchmarks, including commonsense reasoning, recall-intensive tasks, RULER, and LongPPL. The abstract does not expose all numbers, but the full paper argues that the gains are consistent across scales and not limited to one recurrent architecture. An important nuance is that the paper is not arguing recurrent layers should never do retrieval. The claim is that, under standard training, they learn it too early and too broadly, preventing attention from developing the specialization that would lead to a better overall division of labor.51:T449,Read the introduction first and keep the target claim in mind: desirable specialization in hybrid models does not emerge automatically. Then spend most of the time on Section 3. Section 3.1 matters because the synthetic task is what makes the mechanism analysis credible. Section 3.2 is worth reading carefully to understand how retrieval contribution is attributed layer by layer. Sections 3.3.1 to 3.3.3 are the core of the paper: they provide observational evidence, causal evidence through freezing, and evidence that the short-vs-long pattern distribution determines the winner of the competition. After that, move to the BLD training pipeline. The important point is not implementation detail, but why an early freeze-unfreeze schedule changes specialization trajectories. In the empirical section, prioritize the training-loss curves, long-range or retrieval-heavy benchmarks, and consistency across model scales and recurrent backbones. If you work on hybrid pretraining, SSM-plus-attention, linear-attention hybrids, or module specialization more broadly, this paper is worth a full read.52:T446,The method introduces per-position latent auxiliary variables. At inference time, auxiliaries are sampled from a prior and a parallel decoder maps them to a block of tokens in one model call. The dependencies among predicted tokens are routed through the auxiliary variables rather than through left-to-right token generation. Direct likelihood training is intractable because it requires marginalizing over auxiliaries; random auxiliary samples would almost never decode to a given training sequence. The paper therefore trains an autoregressive encoder q_theta(u_i | x_<=i) that proposes auxiliaries for observed sequences and optimizes an ELBO. Operationally, this gives a self-distillation-style objective with an autoregressive language modeling component and a parallel decoding component. The distinction from PTP is important: PLMs are trained from raw sequence data, not distilled from an existing AR model. The distinction from discrete diffusion is also clear: consistency is handled through latent variables in a single or few decoding calls rather than through iterative denoising.53:T425,DFM adds two components to a frozen LLM: a causal chunk-level memory predictor and memory cross-attention modules inserted into selected decoder layers. Training sequences are divided into non-overlapping chunks. For a target chunk, the previous chunk is encoded and used to retrieve top-K neighboring chunks from a corpus datastore. A frozen text encoder converts those retrieved chunks into dense embeddings, ordered by retrieval rank, forming the target memory matrix. During training, the predictor generates memory slots from prior context, and the same predicted memory is shared by all token predictions within the chunk. The fusion module uses cross-attention to inject the predicted memory into hidden states. The added modules are trained jointly with a language-modeling loss and a memory-prediction loss, while the backbone remains frozen. Compared with token-level parametric memories such as MLP Memory and Memory Decoder, the design reduces offline target construction cost and replaces shallow logit-level interpolation with hidden-state fusion.54:T7e1,作者选取两个 diffusion LM：DiffusionGemma-26B-A4B-it，一个 26B 的 MoE 模型，采用 uniform diffusion、256-token block 生成；DreamReasoner-8B，一个 8B dense masked diffusion 模型，32-token block 生成。两者都属于 semi-autoregressive block diffusion，并通过置信度阈值动态提交 token，因此步数不是固定的。论文用一个统一指标衡量解码 effort：每 100 个输出 token 需要多少次 forward pass。这个定义比常见的 tokens per forward 更适合做跨模型、跨 block size 比较，因为它按真实生成 token 数归一化，而不是按 block 容量。

任务设计是全文的关键。作者把任务按输出约束程度分成三类。Reproducing 类，如 grammar correction 和 extractive summarization，答案大部分来自输入，模型主要做复制和局部修正。Chained 类，如 code editing、code generation、competition math，后续 token 受前面生成内容强约束。Open-ended 类，如 WildBench v2 用户查询和 story generation，输出空间更大，约束更弱。除此之外，还加入 translation、clinical note generation、abstractive chapter summary 这类 rewriting 任务，用来区分“依赖输入信息”与“直接复制输入”之间的差别。

分析上，作者不是只报任务均值，而是进一步把成本与两个输出属性关联起来：一是输出相对输入有多少新内容，二是输出词在该任务分布里有多稀有。直觉上，越接近复制、越高频、越可预测的内容，越容易在较少 refinement 步中被 commit；越开放、越低频、越需要真正选择的内容，越需要更多步数。文中还把单个回答拆成 reasoning trace 和 final answer，考察成本在回答内部如何分布；并分析数学题中正确答案与错误答案的 effort 差异。最后，作者把 effort 用作推理时的额外信号：在多样本解题投票时，用“解得更快”的答案赋予更高权重，而不是简单多数票。55:T762,The study evaluates two diffusion LMs: DiffusionGemma-26B-A4B-it, a 26B MoE model with uniform diffusion and 256-token blocks, and DreamReasoner-8B, an 8B dense masked-diffusion model with 32-token blocks. Both use semi-autoregressive block diffusion and adaptive token commitment based on confidence thresholds, so the number of denoising steps is input- and output-dependent. The core metric is forward passes per 100 generated tokens. This choice is important: it normalizes by actual generated tokens up to EOS rather than by block capacity, making comparisons across models and block sizes more meaningful.

The task suite is structured around how constrained the output is. Reproducing tasks, such as grammar correction and extractive summarization, mostly copy from the input with light edits. Chained tasks, such as code editing, code generation, and competition math, have strong dependence on earlier generated content. Open-ended tasks, such as WildBench v2 queries and story generation, leave much more of the output underdetermined. The paper also adds rewriting tasks like translation, clinical note generation, and abstractive summarization to separate 'uses input information' from 'mostly copies input'.

The analysis then relates decoding effort to two output properties: novelty relative to the input and lexical rarity within the task. The hypothesis is straightforward and well supported by the experiments: text that is more constrained, more repetitive, or more frequent can be committed earlier, while text that is more novel or lower-frequency requires more refinement steps. The paper also decomposes responses into reasoning traces and final answers, and tests whether effort correlates with correctness in math. Finally, it uses effort as an inference-time signal by weighting votes from faster-decoded answers more heavily in self-consistency-style aggregation.56:T6fd,The empirical pattern is consistent across 10 tasks. First, task type strongly affects cost. Input-constrained and lightly edited outputs are much cheaper than open-ended generation. A representative number from the paper is that, in DiffusionGemma, story writing requires more than 3x as many forward passes per token as grammar correction. This shows that diffusion speedups are not a fixed property of the model; they depend heavily on task structure. Second, rewriting tasks typically sit between pure reproduction and open-ended generation, which supports the paper’s interpretation that the key variable is not whether there is an input, but how much of the output remains genuinely undecided.

Third, novelty and rarity explain a substantial share of the variation. Outputs that introduce more new content relative to the input, or use rarer words within the task, require more passes per token. This relationship appears not only across tasks but also within a single response. Fourth, in math, incorrect solutions are more expensive than correct ones even after controlling for problem difficulty and output length, suggesting that effort is not just a length proxy. Fifth, when responses are split into reasoning traces and final answers, final answers are often cheaper, especially when they mostly restate information already established in the reasoning trace. Sixth, multilingual experiments show a compounded efficiency penalty: some languages require more tokens and also more diffusion passes per token, creating a double multilingual tax. Seventh, effort is useful operationally: in math answer aggregation, weighting votes by decoding speed improves accuracy over plain majority vote by 4.2 points with two samples and 2.3 points with five, at no extra inference cost.57:T404,Start with the setup and metric definition. The choice of forward passes per 100 output tokens is central, and the paper explains why it is preferable to raw tokens-per-forward or block-capacity normalization. Then read the main task-level results to get the overall shape of cost variation. After that, focus on two analyses: the link between effort and output novelty/rarity, and the decomposition into reasoning traces versus final answers plus correct versus incorrect math solutions. Those sections contain the most useful mechanistic insight. Finish with the multilingual section and the speed-weighted voting experiment, which show that effort is not only descriptive but also actionable at inference time. A solid skim takes about 20–30 minutes. If you work on diffusion LM design, any-order LM, or unified multimodal generation, the appendix details on block size, commitment thresholds, and model-specific settings are worth checking to judge how much of the pattern is paradigm-level versus implementation-specific.58:T89a,论文提出 Lineage-Preserving SMC，简称 LP-SMC。核心思路是同时处理 resampling 事件前后的两个问题。

第一个问题发生在 resampling 之前：在 block-wise masked diffusion decoding 里，一个粒子的权重通常是当前 block 上多个已提交 token 的 reward 乘积，因此随着 block 变长，不同粒子权重会迅速拉开。某条 lineage 可能还没来得及证明自己，就已经因为权重太低而几乎不可能在下一次 resampling 中存活。为此，作者引入 weight floor，把每个粒子的权重下界限制在相对当前最大权重的某个比例之上。这样做不是为了让所有粒子一样重要，而是避免某些 lineage 在 resampling 前就被数值上“判死刑”。论文还分析了这个 floor 何时会生效、会引入什么偏差，以及触发条件。

第二个问题发生在 resampling 本身：标准 multinomial resampling 会把连续权重离散化成后代个数，导致高权重粒子被大量复制、低权重粒子直接消失。作者改用 Chopthin resampling。它不是把 resampling 后的粒子权重全部拉平，而是约束返回权重之间的比值，并把不相等的权重继续带到后续步骤。这样做的好处是，既能控制权重退化，又不必像 multinomial 那样通过激进复制来换取 ESS 的表面恢复。论文还给出了基于 ratio bound 的 ESS 下界，并声称相对 Gandy & Lau 2016 的结果把常数项收紧了一步。

这两个部件组合起来形成 LP-SMC：weight floor 负责防止 lineage 在 resampling 前塌缩，Chopthin with carried weights 负责在 resampling 时减少随机淘汰和过度复制。值得注意的是，作者没有改 proposal，也没有额外增加模型评估次数，重点是把已有 SMC 框架中的 population management 做对。实验同时覆盖两类 guidance：一种是 SR-SMC 那种 internal self-reward，即模型对已提交前缀的自身置信度；另一种是 external process reward model。作者还专门区分了 oracle coverage 和 final accuracy，强调“生成群体里是否存在正确答案”和“最后能否选中它”是两件不同的事，这个拆分很合理。59:T7f8,The method is Lineage-Preserving SMC, or LP-SMC. It addresses two complementary failure modes around each resampling event.

Before resampling, weights can collapse too aggressively. In block-wise masked diffusion decoding, a particle’s weight is typically a product over multiple committed tokens in the current block, so moderate differences compound quickly. A lineage may become numerically negligible before it has any real chance to prove itself. To mitigate this, the paper introduces a weight floor that lower-bounds each particle’s weight relative to the current maximum. The goal is not to equalize particles, but to prevent potentially useful lineages from becoming effectively unsalvageable before resampling. The paper also analyzes when this floor is activated and what bias it introduces.

At the resampling step itself, the paper replaces multinomial resampling with Chopthin resampling. Instead of forcing all post-resampling particles to have equal weights, Chopthin bounds the ratio among returned weights and carries those unequal weights forward. This reduces the need for aggressive duplication of top particles and lowers the chance that moderate-weight lineages disappear purely due to resampling stochasticity. The paper derives an ESS lower bound implied by the ratio constraint and states that this tightens the earlier bound from Gandy and Lau by a constant factor.

Together, the weight floor and Chopthin-with-carried-weights form LP-SMC. Importantly, the proposal distribution is unchanged and no extra model evaluations are required. The contribution is therefore about population management rather than a new reward or proposal mechanism. The paper evaluates LP-SMC under both internal guidance, namely self-reward as in SR-SMC, and external guidance from a process reward model. It also explicitly separates oracle coverage from final accuracy, which is a strong design choice because constructing a population that contains a correct answer is not the same problem as selecting that answer at the end.5a:T6eb,The experiments cover two base diffusion LMs, four benchmarks, and twelve model-guidance-benchmark settings. The headline result is on oracle coverage: the fraction of problems for which at least one of the N particles is correct. LP-SMC improves oracle coverage in all twelve settings, which is the clearest evidence that it preserves useful search branches better than standard resampling.

The internal-guidance ablations are especially informative. On GSM8K with LLaDA-1.5, the number of surviving lineages out of 16 particles rises from 5.2 to 10.0. That is close to a twofold increase and directly supports the paper’s central claim that the gain comes from preserving lineage diversity rather than merely replicating the same high-scoring trajectory more often. The paper also reports increases in distinct outputs, which is consistent with the lineage statistics.

A key nuance is that better coverage does not automatically translate into the same gain in final accuracy. The conversion depends on the selection rule used at the end. The paper therefore uses a common reward-model selector for the main comparison and separately analyzes how different selectors affect the coverage-to-accuracy conversion. That separation is methodologically important because it avoids conflating population construction with answer selection.

The paper also evaluates both internal self-reward and external PRM guidance, and the gains are not limited to one reward source. Even without every final accuracy number in the abstract, the full paper’s most convincing evidence comes from the alignment between theory and intermediate diagnostics: surviving lineages, distinct outputs, and oracle coverage all move in the direction predicted by the proposed resampling changes.5b:T48e,Although labeled skim, this is worth reading a bit more carefully if you care about diffusion LMs or any population-based decoding method. Start with the introduction and background to understand block-wise masked diffusion decoding, when resampling happens, and how SR-SMC works. Then go straight to Section 3, which is the conceptual center of the paper: the mismatch between ESS and lineage diversity. After that, read Section 4 for the actual method, focusing on how the weight floor, Chopthin, and carried weights interact, and on the theoretical discussion of the ESS bound and floor-induced bias. In the experiments, prioritize the tables that report surviving lineages, distinct outputs, and oracle coverage, not just final accuracy.

If time is limited, about 45 minutes should be enough to capture the main thread. If you want to dig deeper, three questions are worth keeping in mind: whether the bias from the weight floor grows with longer blocks or stronger reward models, whether Chopthin’s benefit depends on relatively small particle counts, and whether the same ideas can transfer to AR tree search, particle decoding, or verifier-guided sampling.5c:T5bd,SFPRM re-implements FPRM’s damped fixed-point solver on the unit sphere used by normalized Transformers (nGPT).
- State geometry: every token hidden vector is constrained to \(\mathbb{S}^{d-1}\), preventing norm blow-up.
- Input injection: instead of Euclidean mixing, the input is re-injected via geodesic movement toward an input anchor, parameterized by an injection strength \(\lambda\), implemented with spherical linear interpolation (Slerp).
- Damping: the Euclidean convex-combination update is replaced by a spherical interpolation step with coefficient \(\eta_i\), now interpretable as an angular step size. The same patience-based decay schedule is used, but without the need for FPRM’s coupled residual-rescaling coefficients.
- Halting: the stopping residual is defined as an angular discrepancy (worst-token angle between the current iterate and its proposal), which is naturally scale-invariant—removing the need for relative-norm residual normalization.
- Guarantees: fixed-point existence follows from continuity plus injection; local convergence is characterized via the tangent-space Jacobian with an explicit step-size window; sufficiently strong injection yields a unique global attractor.
- Training: follows the practical FPRM approach (truncated BPTT with windows, deep supervision, detach between windows) rather than implicit differentiation; the novelty is primarily in the spherical control/halting design and the resulting decoupling.5d:T4e9,OrderGPT builds on Any-Order GPT, which separates the decoder-only computation graph from the left-to-right factorization. Variables have fixed identities, while causal attention follows a supplied reveal permutation. The method adds a lightweight OrderMLP that predicts continuous priorities for variables; sorting these priorities gives the generation order. The order is not found by combinatorial search. The model first observes predictions under randomly sampled reveal prefixes. Recurring attention patterns are aggregated into a reciprocal dependency graph. A Spectral Teacher applies a graph-Laplacian construction to recover a continuous axis that places strongly related variables close to each other. Directed attention is then used to orient the axis, preferring variables that are often attended as context to appear before their prediction targets. These continuous priorities supervise OrderMLP. During training, random orders are gradually replaced by the learned order, and the final order is frozen for standard autoregressive likelihood evaluation and generation. Compared with masked diffusion, the model does not average over many orders at convergence. Compared with ordinary GPT, it does not require a hand-specified canonical order.5e:T438,UpLoop uses layer-wise local recurrence. Each selected Transformer layer executes multiple local rounds before passing the hidden state to the next layer. This preserves the pretrained depth hierarchy and avoids the mismatch induced by whole-model or block-level looping.

The second component is gated residual writing. The first round is identical to the original pretrained forward pass. Extra rounds apply hidden-wise gates to the attention and MLP residual branches. These gates are specific to the layer, loop index, and residual branch. Parameters are still shared across loop executions of the same layer, but each refinement step can write with a different strength across hidden channels.

The third component is a depth-aware training objective. Intermediate supervision keeps each recurrent depth decodable, while an improvement objective encourages later rounds to refine earlier ones instead of drifting. This matters because recurrent hidden trajectories can otherwise become poorly controlled, especially when the model is evaluated at a different number of loops.5f:T43f,The evaluation covers several settings. Parallel Needle-in-a-Haystack tests whether a stream without local evidence can retrieve information from another stream. TinyStories pretraining and FineWeb-Edu LoRA continued pretraining test language-modeling behavior and masked-token recovery. PQA and PMHQA probe factual transfer across streams. parallel-WikiHop tests a multi-hop setting. Cooperative MARL evaluates whether the same communication primitive supports coordination.

The results are mixed. BatchParScale can learn controlled cross-stream retrieval, improves small-scale sequence modeling comparisons against ParScale, and improves masked-token recovery when neighboring streams contain redundant context. It can also be added to a pretrained Transformer via LoRA continued pretraining. However, on PNIAH and PMHQA, both pretrained and finetuned models remain close to random, even though the task is solvable when the evidence stays within a single stream. parallel-WikiHop is meaningfully above random, and MARL results are competitive on several coordination-sensitive tasks.60:T88d,The core idea is native latent tokens plus a unified diffusion sequence. Each modality is represented in its own latent token space rather than being projected into a shared cross-modal embedding space. For a given generation task, the source-condition tokens and target tokens are assembled into a single sequence and processed by one denoiser. To make this sequence unambiguous, each token carries an attribute tuple that includes at least modality, role (source or target), and noise level. This lets the same model handle text→image, audio→text, image+text→audio, and related tasks without architectural branching.

A second key component is role-based positional embedding. Since the sequence layout changes across tasks, naive concatenation with a standard positional scheme can damage the internal structure of image patches, audio frames, or text tokens. The role-aware positional design is meant to preserve within-modality structure while still allowing a unified transformer to process variable layouts and lengths.

For multi-condition generation, the paper proposes two mechanisms. The first is inference-time score composition, essentially a product-of-experts style combination of single-condition predictions. Its advantage is that it requires no extra training, which is attractive when training data only contains paired examples. Its weakness is that interactions among conditions are only approximated through score fusion. The second is caption-based adaptation: express the joint semantics of multiple conditions in language, construct a compact adaptation set from existing paired data, and lightly finetune the model. This gives up some zero-training purity but models condition interactions more faithfully.

Methodologically, Modaliff is best viewed as token-based multimodal diffusion rather than shared-latent alignment. Relative to UniDiffuser or OmniFlow, it removes the need for fully aligned multimodal tuples. Relative to CoDi or FlowBind, it avoids collapsing all modalities into one common representation. The trade-off is explicit: the model has to manage token attributes and sequence layout carefully, but it preserves modality-native structure.61:T6d5,The experiments cover generation across text, image, and audio, with comparisons against any-to-any baselines such as OmniFlow and CoDi. The paper makes two main empirical claims: first, Modaliff achieves the best fidelity on most generation tasks; second, it does so with much smaller model and data budgets. The headline scale numbers in the abstract are that it uses roughly 6–8× fewer parameters and about 5% of OmniFlow’s training data while remaining competitive.

From the full paper structure, the evaluation is designed to test three things. First, whether a single denoiser can truly support many source-target combinations without task-specific architecture. Second, whether training only on bimodal paired data is sufficient for broader any-to-any translation behavior. Third, how the two multi-condition strategies compare: score composition versus caption-based adaptation. The expected trade-off is straightforward: score composition is more flexible and training-free, but weaker at modeling interactions among conditions; caption-based adaptation requires a small extra finetuning step, but usually gives better consistency under multiple conditions.

For readers interested in pretraining-style lessons, the ablations matter more than any single benchmark number. The most useful checks are likely: what happens when token attributes are removed; whether role-based positional embeddings are necessary for cross-task generalization; how much caption-based adaptation adds beyond pure score composition; and which modality pairs are easiest or hardest under pair-only training. The provided excerpt does not expose the full metric tables, so it is better not to overstate specific numbers beyond the headline scale comparisons.62:T4c4,For a skim, start with the Introduction and the main method figure to pin down the actual constraint being solved: unified any-to-any token diffusion trained from paired data, not just another multimodal benchmark entry. Then focus on two design choices: the token attribute tuple and the role-based positional embedding. Those are the mechanisms that let the model preserve modality-native structure instead of drifting toward a shared-latent solution.

In the experiments, prioritize three parts. First, the main comparison with OmniFlow and CoDi to understand the data-efficiency and parameter-efficiency position. Estimated reading time is around 20 minutes. If your interest is new language-modeling paradigms or unified multimodal token modeling, it is worth a pass. If your focus is strictly text LLM pretraining recipes, optimizers, or scaling laws, reading the method overview and the main empirical conclusions is probably enough.63:T434,The method augments a Transformer denoiser with a tractable probabilistic inference layer. From the same backbone states, it produces token potentials for per-position predictions and compact context gates that reweight shared coupling parameters. The important design choice is that the coupling is context-dependent: the model can prefer different joint token combinations under different prompts, instead of using one fixed dependency layer. Unlike approaches that attach a separately trained joint head to a frozen denoiser, Codpula trains through the joint distribution, so the backbone learns both token preferences and coupling signals. The training procedure includes a dual-flow update to handle signed learning statistics introduced by conditional normalization while keeping valid probability parameters. At decoding time, the same potentials and gates support conditional dependence queries. A proposal can be deferred if its probability changes sharply after conditioning on other proposed tokens, and this does not require an extra backbone pass within the step.64:T8db,PAR 以预训练 Qwen2.5 为底座，把 24 层模型拆成 prelude、recurrent core 和 coda：Qwen2.5-0.5B 中 layers 1–8 作为 P，layers 9–16 作为共享权重核心 C，layers 17–24 作为 Q。输入先经 P 得到静态特征 e，循环状态从 s0=e 开始。每次循环把静态输入特征和当前状态拼接，经 adapter W 投入共享核心。W 初始化为 [0 | I]，因此循环次数 R=1 时初始行为尽量接近原模型，降低 retrofit 的破坏性。训练时所有权重更新，但只对最后 8 次循环反传，以控制显存和计算。

核心监督是 progress-aligned target。若任务需要 d 个顺序操作，zj 表示执行前 j 步后的状态或答案，则第 k 次循环监督 zk，而不是最终答案 zd。这样每次循环被要求推进固定步长 c，默认 c=1。论文讨论了 forced depth 和 hold 两种 schedule：forced depth 让每个 batch 只含同一深度 d，并运行 R=ceil(d/c) 次；hold 从重尾分布采样 R，任务完成后继续保持 zd。默认采用 forced depth。

第二个关键组件是 RMS norm anchoring。每次循环后，将每个 token 的 recurrent state 按 RMS 归一到第一次循环状态的 RMS norm，参考值 stop-gradient。这样共享核心在长循环中看到的状态尺度更稳定，避免迭代数增加时 hidden norm 漂移改变“单步状态转移函数”。这不是普通 LayerNorm 替代品，而是显式把循环状态锚到初始循环分布。

论文还补了两个实际问题。第一，测试时不知道应运行多少步。PAR 训练原有输出层预测 computation 是否完成，并用短确认窗口选择答案，避免模型完成后继续循环导致答案退化。第二，中间状态标签可能不可用。prefix self-distillation 利用“前缀本身也是一个更短问题”这一结构：先在短前缀上得到最终答案，再把它作为完整输入相应循环位置的监督信号，从只有最终答案标签的数据中诱导 depth–length correspondence。对于 label-free 版本，论文还加入 positional stretch：训练时把位置索引乘以从 1 到 s_max 的随机因子，s_max ramp 到 8，测试时使用正常位置，用来缓解长 prompt 下查询位置远离早期操作的问题。65:T955,PAR starts from a pretrained Qwen2.5 model and retrofits it into a recurrent model. For Qwen2.5-0.5B, the 24 layers are split into a prelude P, a tied recurrent core C, and a coda Q: layers 1–8, 9–16, and 17–24 respectively. The input is encoded once by P into static features e. The recurrent state starts from s0=e. At each iteration, an adapter W maps the concatenation of the static features and current state into the shared core. W is initialized as [0 | I], so the model with R=1 initially matches the parent model as closely as possible. All weights are trained, while gradients are propagated through the last eight iterations.

The main supervision is progress-aligned recurrence. If a task requires d sequential operations and zj denotes the state or answer after the first j operations, then iteration k is trained to predict zk rather than the final answer zd. With step size c=1, each loop is explicitly trained to advance the computation by one task step. The paper considers two depth schedules. In forced depth, each batch contains a single task depth d and the model runs R=ceil(d/c) iterations. In hold, R is sampled from a heavy-tailed distribution and the target remains zd after the task is complete. Forced depth is the default.

The second main component is RMS norm anchoring. After each recurrent iteration, each token state is rescaled to match the RMS norm of its first-iteration state, using a stop-gradient reference. This keeps the scale of recurrent states stationary as the shared block is applied hundreds of times. The point is not generic normalization; it is an explicit anchor that keeps the learned step map operating in the state regime it saw during early iterations.

The paper also addresses two deployment issues. First, the correct stopping depth may be unavailable at test time. PAR trains the existing output layer to predict whether execution is complete and uses a short confirmation window to select the answer. Second, intermediate state labels may be unavailable. Prefix self-distillation uses valid shorter prefixes as supervision sources: predictions on a prefix are used as targets for the corresponding iteration on the full input. For this label-free setting, positional stretch is added during a short fine-tuning stage by multiplying position indices by a random factor ramped up to 8, while testing uses ordinary positions.66:T66b,The experiments focus on synthetic state-tracking tasks such as rule-table chains, object tracking, S5, and swap-S5. These tasks are appropriate because the rule is unchanged as the number of operations grows, so the evaluation isolates whether the model can repeatedly apply the same state transition.

The headline result is 16x extrapolation on swap-S5. When trained with at most 16 operations, PAR reaches 95.5% full-state accuracy at 16x length. RLT reaches 55.7%, while explicit chain-of-thought reaches 0.8%. The comparison is informative: writing intermediate steps as text does not ensure length extrapolation, especially when each step depends on the previous latent state and errors accumulate. The paper also reports that an untied model with four times the core depth extrapolates less than 2x, and a recurrent model run for more iterations also extrapolates less than 2x without the PAR alignment. Fixed-depth Qwen2.5 models from 1.5B to 7B stay near chance at 16x length, indicating that parameter scale alone does not solve this controlled algorithmic generalization problem.

The ablations support the mechanism. Intermediate-state supervision without norm anchoring helps only over short extrapolation ranges. Final-answer supervision at every loop encourages premature prediction and weakens extrapolation. Running after completion can degrade a previously correct answer, motivating the learned halting rule. Prefix self-distillation works when intermediate labels are missing, but the label-free variant needs positional stretch to reach 16x extrapolation. The benefits are reported consistently across backbones up to 7B.67:T432,Read the Introduction, Depth–Length Correspondence, Section 5, and Section 6 closely. The Introduction defines the two key failure modes: target misalignment and state drift. The method section is the core of the paper; Figure 2, the progress-aligned loss, the forced-depth and hold schedules, RMS norm anchoring, learned halting, and prefix self-distillation are the main items to inspect.

For experiments, prioritize Sections 5.1 and 5.2 to understand why more parameters, more untied depth, or more recurrent iterations are insufficient. Section 5.3 is useful for anyone using test-time compute, because it shows that continuing to loop after completion can damage the answer. Section 6 is the most useful part for implementation: it separates the effects of intermediate supervision, norm anchoring, positional stretch, and prefix self-distillation. A minimal reproduction should start with three components: predict the k-th intermediate state at the k-th loop, apply per-token RMS anchoring after each loop, and add a completion signal or an explicit stopping rule.68:Tc1a,核心设计是 blockwise flow，而不是对整段文本做全局连续生成。作者沿用 block-autoregressive factorization：前缀仍按因果方式提供条件，continuation 被切成固定大小的 block。这样做有两个直接好处。其一，跨 block 仍是标准左到右生成，因此 prefix caching 可以保留；其二，并行性被限制在 block 内，训练和推理都更容易落到现有 Transformer 基础设施上。

在 block 内，Lafa 不是用共享时间的标准 flow matching，而是引入 tokenwise time 的 asynchronous flow。具体地，作者把离散 token 先映射到 embedding 空间，用高斯噪声到 token embedding 的连续路径做 flow matching。不同位置的 token 使用不同的时间进度 τ_i(t)：靠前位置更早接近干净 token，靠后位置更慢。这给了模型一种“块内左到右偏置的双向建模”能力。它不是严格因果，也不是完全对称的双向去噪，而是介于两者之间，既允许块内信息交互，又保留文本顺序结构。这个设计比标准离散 diffusion 或 fully bidirectional masked modeling 更贴近语言的生成结构。

架构上，文章强调 causal attention on the prefix，bidirectional attention within block，并通过异步时间调度让块内不同位置处于不同噪声水平。这样模型在同一次前向中既看到稳定的前缀条件，又能在块内并行更新多个位置。由于 continuation 仍按 block 递进，历史 block 的缓存可以像 AR 一样复用，这是很多非 AR 方法做不到的。

训练上，作者不是只做 flow objective，而是联合 blockwise denoising flow 与 prefix AR prediction。这个联合目标有两个作用。第一，它让从 AR checkpoint 适配到 flow 更自然，因为模型保留了熟悉的 next-token 路径。第二，它实证上增强了 AR 能力，作者将其解释为一种 multi-token prediction effect：flow 训练迫使模型在给定前缀时更好地建模局部未来 token 的联合结构，从而反哺 AR 头。

推理上有三层。第一层是标准的 blockwise parallel flow decoding，利用 prefix cache 并行生成一个 block。第二层是 flow map distillation：把多步 ODE 积分蒸馏成 one-step 或 few-step flow map，减少采样步数，这是连续 flow 相比离散 diffusion 的一个重要优势。第三层是 self-speculative decoding：先用 flow path 快速 draft，再用同一模型的 AR path 验证接受前缀。这里和传统 speculative decoding 的不同点在于，draft 与 verifier 不是两个模型，而是同一模型的两种能力，因此额外参数和部署复杂度更低。

和已有 diffusion LM、SEDD、MDLM、LLaDA 一类离散方法相比，Lafa 的差异不只是“连续 vs 离散”。更关键的是它把 blockwise factorization、prefix caching、AR adaptation、flow map distillation、自验证推理串成了一条完整链路。和早期小规模 flow LM 相比，它最重要的进步是给出了可扩展的架构偏置与训练 recipe，而不是单纯换一个连续目标函数。69:T87a,实验规模是这篇文章最有说服力的部分。作者训练了 0.5B、7B、8B 三个规模的 Lafa，并强调总训练 token 少于 30B。这一点很重要，因为它不是从零训练一个新范式，而是展示了从预训练 AR 模型高效适配到 flow LM 的可行性。文中还明确对比了离散 diffusion 适配常见的更高 token 成本，提到可比工作可能需要高达 500B token 量级的训练，这使 Lafa 的数据效率优势很突出。

质量方面，作者在 instruction following、reasoning、coding 等多类 benchmark 上评估，并声称 learned flow 的质量可匹配甚至超过 AR 基线。更关键的是，flow 训练没有削弱 AR path，反而提升了预训练 AR 能力。这一点如果成立，意义很大，因为很多替代范式的问题在于新目标会破坏原有 AR competence，而 Lafa 给出的结果是联合训练可以形成互补。

速度方面，文章报告在 matched quality 下，相比强 AR baseline，Lafa 通过 self-speculative decoding 达到 2.54× 吞吐提升，并且在质量-速度前沿上优于同规模 AR、MTP 和离散 diffusion LM。这里要注意，作者不是只比较裸 flow 采样，而是比较“flow draft + AR verify”的完整系统，这更接近真实可用配置。

从消融角度，最值得看的是四类实验。第一，block size、异步时间调度、prefix/within-block attention 结构对质量和速度的影响，能帮助判断哪些归纳偏置是必要的。第二，联合 AR+flow 训练与纯 flow 训练的差异，尤其是 AR 能力是否真的被保留甚至增强。第三，flow map distillation 的步数压缩效果，one-step/few-step 与原始 flow 采样之间的质量损失有多大。第四，self-speculative decoding 的接受率、验证开销和最终吞吐收益，这决定了它是否只是 paper speedup，还是可部署的 speedup。

虽然摘要里没有列出所有 benchmark 的具体分数，但从全文叙述看，作者的重点不是单点榜单，而是证明在 7B/8B 规模、低于 30B token 适配预算下，flow LM 已经能进入与主流 AR/MTP/离散 diffusion 正面比较的区间。6a:T901,这篇值得精读。建议按“问题—设计—训练—推理—证据”五步读。

第一步看 Introduction 和 Figure 1/2，先确认作者到底在 claim 什么：不是单纯提出一个 flow LM，而是提出一个可从 AR 高效适配、可缓存前缀、可蒸馏、可自验证的 large flow LM。这里要特别留意他们如何界定比较对象：AR、MTP、离散 diffusion。

第二步精读方法部分里 blockwise asynchronous flow 的定义。重点看为什么要用 block-autoregressive factorization，而不是全序列并行 flow；为什么要用 tokenwise time，而不是所有位置共享同一个 t；以及 causal prefix + bidirectional within-block 这个 attention 结构如何同时服务于归纳偏置和 prefix caching。若只看一个技术点，就看 asynchronous tokenwise time，这是整篇文章最核心的建模创新。

第三步看训练目标。需要弄清楚联合 AR prediction 与 blockwise flow denoising 各自承担什么角色，loss 如何配比，初始化是否来自 AR checkpoint，训练 token 预算如何分配。这里关系到这条路线能否真正成为“AR 模型的 mid-train / adaptation recipe”，而不只是从头训练的新模型。

第四步看推理章节。重点看 flow map distillation 和 self-speculative decoding。前者决定 continuous flow 是否能摆脱多步积分的采样负担，后者决定它能否与现有 AR 验证机制结合成稳定的质量-速度折中。若你做 serving 或 decoding，这部分信息密度很高。

第五步看实验与消融。优先关注：7B/8B 与 AR baseline 的 matched-quality throughput；联合训练是否提升 AR；不同 block size 和时间调度的影响；蒸馏到 one/few-step 后的退化幅度。图表上，凡是展示 quality-speed frontier、acceptance rate、distillation steps、以及 AR capability retention 的图都值得细看。

如果你做新型语言建模范式，这篇最值得深挖的点有三个：1）continuous flow 是否比 discrete diffusion 更适合大模型适配；2）块内异步时间是否可以推广到 any-order / masked / latent reasoning 任务；3）联合 AR+flow 训练带来的“反向提升 AR”现象，到底是 regularization、MTP-like supervision，还是更深层的表示学习效应。6b:T4e5,This is a must-read paper for pretraining researchers interested in alternatives to next-token AR modeling. It matters for three reasons. First, it pushes continuous flow language modeling from small-scale proof-of-concept into the 8B regime, and does so with fewer than 30B training tokens rather than relying on massive extra adaptation data. Second, its blockwise asynchronous flow design is a meaningful architectural contribution: it preserves left-to-right structure at the block level while allowing bidirectional, asynchronous continuous generation within each block. That makes prefix caching and parallel block generation compatible, which is a major practical requirement. Third, the paper shows that flow training does not merely coexist with AR capability; it can preserve and even improve it, and this enables a self-speculative decoding scheme where the same model drafts with flow and verifies autoregressively.

In terms of contribution type, this is one of the stronger pieces of evidence so far that a non-AR language modeling paradigm can scale into the regime where mainstream LLM comparisons become meaningful. It does not displace AR yet, but it clearly moves flow LM from an interesting side path to a serious research direction.6c:Td74,The central idea is blockwise flow rather than fully global continuous generation over the whole sequence. Lafa adopts block-autoregressive factorization: the prefix remains causal, while the continuation is partitioned into fixed-size blocks. This choice has two immediate benefits. First, generation across blocks remains left-to-right, so prefix caching is retained. Second, parallelism is localized within each block, which makes training and inference much easier to implement on top of existing Transformer infrastructure.

Inside a block, Lafa does not use standard flow matching with a single shared time variable for all positions. Instead, it introduces asynchronous flow through tokenwise time. Tokens are first embedded into a continuous space, and flow matching is performed from Gaussian noise to token embeddings. Different positions follow different time schedules τ_i(t): earlier positions move toward clean token embeddings faster, later positions more slowly. This creates a left-to-right bias inside the block without enforcing strict causality. The result is a hybrid inductive bias: bidirectional interaction within the block, but with an ordering preference that better matches language than fully symmetric denoising or fully bidirectional masked modeling.

Architecturally, the model uses causal attention on the prefix and bidirectional attention within the current block, while asynchronous tokenwise time ensures that different positions are denoised at different rates. This allows the model to condition on a stable prefix while updating multiple future positions in parallel. Because continuation still advances block by block, cached history from previous blocks can be reused much like in AR decoding, which is a major practical advantage over many non-AR approaches.

Training is also carefully designed. Lafa is not trained with a pure flow objective alone; it combines blockwise flow denoising with autoregressive prediction on the prefix. This serves two purposes. It makes adaptation from a pretrained AR checkpoint natural, since the model retains a familiar next-token path. And empirically, it improves AR capability rather than degrading it. The paper interprets this as a multi-token-prediction-like effect: flow training encourages the model to better capture local future-token structure conditioned on the prefix, which then feeds back into the AR head.

Inference has three layers. First, there is standard blockwise parallel flow decoding with prefix caching. Second, the learned flow can be distilled into one-step or few-step flow maps, reducing the cost of ODE integration; this is one of the major advantages of continuous flow over discrete diffusion. Third, the model supports self-speculative decoding: the flow path drafts quickly, and the AR path of the same model verifies the accepted prefix. Unlike classical speculative decoding, this does not require a separate draft model, which lowers deployment complexity.

Relative to discrete diffusion LMs such as D3PM/SEDD/MDLM-style approaches, the difference is not only continuous versus discrete state space. More importantly, Lafa combines blockwise factorization, prefix caching, AR adaptation, flow-map distillation, and self-verification into a coherent end-to-end recipe. Relative to earlier small-scale flow LM work, the real advance is the scalable inductive bias and training recipe, not just the use of a continuous objective.6d:T9ab,The scale of the experiments is one of the paper’s strongest points. The authors train Lafa at 0.5B, 7B, and 8B parameters, with fewer than 30B total training tokens. This is important because the paper is not presenting a from-scratch alternative paradigm with unlimited budget; it is demonstrating efficient adaptation from pretrained AR models. The paper also contrasts this with discrete diffusion adaptation settings that may require far larger token budgets, citing numbers up to 500B in comparable setups. That makes the data-efficiency claim meaningful.

On quality, the evaluation spans instruction following, reasoning, and coding benchmarks. The paper claims that the learned flow matches or surpasses AR baselines, and more interestingly, that flow training preserves and can even improve the pretrained AR path. If this result is robust, it is a major point in favor of the method, because many alternative objectives trade off against AR competence rather than complementing it.

On speed, the headline result is that Lafa reaches 2.54× the throughput of a strong AR baseline at matched quality through self-speculative decoding, and that its quality–speed frontier is better than similarly sized AR, MTP, and discrete diffusion language models. The comparison is important because it is not just raw flow sampling; it is the full system with flow drafting and AR verification, which is closer to a deployable setup.

The most useful ablations are likely in four groups. First, the effect of block size, asynchronous time schedules, and prefix-versus-within-block attention structure on both quality and speed. These reveal which inductive biases are actually necessary. Second, the comparison between joint AR+flow training and pure flow training, especially whether AR capability is truly retained or improved. Third, the compression achieved by flow-map distillation: how much quality is lost when moving from multi-step flow integration to one-step or few-step maps. Fourth, the acceptance rate, verification overhead, and net throughput gain of self-speculative decoding, which determine whether the reported speedup is practically meaningful.

The abstract does not list all benchmark scores, but the full presentation makes the intended claim clear: at 7B–8B scale and under a sub-30B-token adaptation budget, flow language modeling has entered a regime where direct comparison with mainstream AR, MTP, and discrete diffusion methods is justified.6e:Taa7,This paper deserves a careful read. A good reading order is: problem framing, architecture, training, inference, then evidence.

Start with the introduction and the main overview figures. The key is to pin down the exact claim: this is not merely a flow LM proposal, but a large-scale flow LM that can be adapted efficiently from AR checkpoints, supports prefix caching, can be distilled into fast flow maps, and can be combined with AR verification. Pay attention to how the paper positions itself against AR, MTP, and discrete diffusion.

Then read the method section on blockwise asynchronous flow closely. Focus on three questions: why block-autoregressive factorization is chosen instead of fully parallel sequence-level flow; why tokenwise time is used instead of a shared time variable; and how causal prefix attention plus bidirectional within-block attention jointly support both inductive bias and cacheability. If you only study one technical idea in depth, study asynchronous tokenwise time, because it is the core modeling innovation.

Next, examine the training objective. Understand what the AR prefix loss and the blockwise flow-denoising loss each contribute, how they are combined, whether initialization comes from an AR checkpoint, and how the token budget is allocated. This is the part that determines whether the method is a realistic mid-training or adaptation recipe rather than a purely from-scratch alternative.

After that, read the inference section carefully. Flow-map distillation and self-speculative decoding are both central. The former determines whether continuous flow can escape the burden of many integration steps; the latter determines whether it can plug into a stable quality–speed tradeoff using existing AR verification machinery. If you work on serving or decoding, this section is especially valuable.

Finally, spend time on the ablations and frontier plots. Prioritize the figures showing matched-quality throughput at 7B/8B, AR capability retention or improvement after flow training, the effect of block size and time schedules, and the degradation from one-step/few-step distillation. Any plot on quality–speed frontier, acceptance rate, distillation steps, or AR retention is worth close inspection.

For researchers in alternative language modeling paradigms, three deeper questions are worth following up: whether continuous flow is fundamentally better than discrete diffusion for large-model adaptation; whether asynchronous tokenwise time can generalize to masked, any-order, or latent-reasoning settings; and whether the observed AR improvement from joint AR+flow training is mainly regularization, MTP-like supervision, or a deeper representation-learning effect.6f:T883,方法核心是 Binary Discrete Diffusion。每个位置的状态不再是词表中的一个 token，而是一个长度为 V 的二值向量，表示该 token 是否仍在候选集合中。干净样本对应 singleton set。论文给出两种连续时间 CTMC corruption：
1) binary symmetric diffusion：每个 membership bit 都可以从 0 变 1，也可以从 1 变 0。这样候选既能被删掉，也能被重新加入，适合需要回溯修正的任务。
2) binary absorbing diffusion：corruption 只增加候选，不删除候选；对应的 reverse 过程就是不断剪枝，直到每个位置只剩一个 token。

看起来状态空间是 2^V，但关键观察是每一步只需要考虑单 bit 翻转，所以每个状态只有 O(V) 个邻居。作者进一步推导出：只要模型输出常规的 V-way clean-token 预测，就能在 O(V) 时间内计算所有相邻 reverse rates，不需要枚举子集。训练仍沿用连续时间离散 diffusion 的 ELBO / path-space KL 框架，用 clean-conditioned reverse rates 作为监督目标。也就是说，模型并不需要额外的 candidate 标签、规则系统或 symbolic search，候选集动态是从最终解分布中隐式学出来的。

采样部分也不是简单照搬已有 discrete diffusion。因为状态变成候选集，作者设计了 candidate-aware sampling：包括基于 shared clean-token proposal 的精确 ancestral updates、适配 candidate-set 状态的 re-corrupt sampling，以及结合 Ψ-sampling 和 confidence-guided remasking 的 revision 规则。这里的关键不是只决定“哪些位置重采样”，还要决定“这些位置重新开放哪些候选”。这比传统 remasking 多了一层控制自由度。

和已有方法的区别可以概括为三点：
- 相比 masked diffusion：不是把不确定性压缩成一个 mask，而是显式保留多个假设；
- 相比 uniform diffusion：不是随机替换成另一个单 token，而是允许集合态，避免把多解不确定性硬编码成单点噪声；
- 相比 absorbing-style candidate pruning：symmetric 版本允许恢复候选，因此更接近真实的迭代推理，而不是单调收缩。70:T7bf,The method is Binary Discrete Diffusion. Instead of representing each position as one token from a vocabulary of size V, the state is a binary membership vector in {0,1}^V indicating which tokens are currently active candidates. A clean token is a singleton set.

The paper defines two continuous-time Markov corruption processes:
1) Binary symmetric diffusion: each membership bit can flip on or off. This allows candidate removal and later restoration.
2) Binary absorbing diffusion: corruption only adds candidates. The reverse process then progressively prunes the set toward a singleton.

Although the nominal state space is 2^V per position, each state has only V single-bit neighbors, which keeps local transitions tractable. A key derivation shows that all neighboring reverse rates can be computed in O(V) time from the model’s usual V-way clean-token prediction, without enumerating subsets. Training follows the continuous-time discrete diffusion ELBO / path-space KL framework, using clean-conditioned reverse rates as targets. Importantly, the model is trained only from clean solutions; it does not require candidate annotations, handcrafted deduction rules, or symbolic search.

The sampling side is also adapted to the new state space. The paper introduces candidate-aware sampling, including exact ancestral updates via a shared clean-token proposal, re-corrupt sampling adapted to candidate sets, and revision rules inspired by Psi-sampling and confidence-guided remasking. The extra degree of freedom is important: the sampler must decide not only which positions to revisit, but also which hypotheses to reopen.

Relative to prior kernels, the distinctions are clear:
- versus masked diffusion: uncertainty is not collapsed into a single mask token;
- versus uniform diffusion: uncertainty is not forced into one random token;
- versus absorbing-only pruning: the symmetric process supports non-monotonic revision, which is closer to actual iterative reasoning.71:T668,The main evaluation uses three structured reasoning/planning tasks with exact solve-rate metrics: Sudoku-Extreme, Boxoban, and graph coloring. The comparisons are controlled for architecture, training budget, and sampler tuning, and evaluation uses direct single-attempt generation without verifier-guided reranking. That setup matters because it isolates the quality of the learned generative process itself.

The central empirical pattern is consistent: binary symmetric diffusion outperforms uniform diffusion, and both outperform masked diffusion and binary absorbing diffusion. The gap between binary symmetric and uniform grows in harder regimes, including low-clue Sudoku, longer-horizon Boxoban, and graph coloring beyond the training graph size. This directly supports the paper’s claim that candidate-set states are better suited to globally constrained iterative refinement.

The paper also includes text-side checks on Text8, TinyStories, and OpenWebText. Binary diffusion remains competitive with established kernels, suggesting that the richer state representation does not immediately break generic language modeling. Still, the text results are better read as feasibility evidence than as proof that this is already the best general-purpose pretraining objective.

Among the ablations, the most informative one is symmetric versus absorbing. Performance drops when the model is restricted to monotonic pruning, which indicates that the ability to reopen candidates is not cosmetic; it is central to the method. The paper also emphasizes finite inference budgets, which is the practically relevant regime for diffusion LMs.72:T514,Start with the introduction. The key idea is not simply 'another discrete diffusion model' but 'what should an intermediate state represent'. Then read the definition of the binary symmetric and binary absorbing forward processes, followed by the reverse-rate derivation that reduces computation to O(V) from a standard V-way prediction. That part determines whether the proposal is genuinely scalable.

Next, read the sampling section carefully. Candidate-aware sampling, re-corrupt updates, and revision rules are essential to the full story. Looking only at the training objective would miss how the representation is meant to function at inference time.

For experiments, prioritize the main tables on Sudoku, Boxoban, and graph coloring, especially the difficulty-stratified results and the symmetric-versus-absorbing comparison. The text experiments can be skimmed as a sanity check.

Expected reading time is about 35 to 50 minutes. If reading selectively, focus on the overview figure, the reverse-rate derivation, and the main reasoning-task results. The deeper questions worth carrying forward are whether this remains practical with very large vocabularies, and whether the candidate-set state can be combined with subword, byte-level, or multimodal token spaces without becoming unwieldy.73:T879,The method introduces Meta Experts, a shared expert pool accessible from multiple layers, in contrast to conventional Local Experts that belong to a single layer. The paper studies several configurations: pure Local, pure Meta, and mixed Local+Meta variants. Two groups of variables are explored systematically. The first is quantitative: the ratio between Meta and Local experts in the whole model, and the ratio between Meta and Local experts among the activated experts in each layer. The second is topological: whether every layer contains both types, whether only some layers use shared experts, and whether part of the original hierarchical organization is retained.

The key point is that this is not just naive parameter tying. The sharing is embedded inside sparse MoE routing. Each layer still performs top-k expert selection, but the candidate set can now include experts from a cross-layer shared pool rather than only layer-private experts. This changes the storage-retrieval structure without increasing the activated expert count. A shared expert can be trained by tokens arriving from multiple depths, which may improve parameter reuse and encourage more general expert functions. At the same time, compute per token remains close to the original MoE budget.

The paper’s mechanism story is also more specific than a pure compression argument. The authors interpret Meta Experts as introducing more flexible residual-like paths across depth. In a standard hierarchical stack, hidden states interact across layers through forward residual connections only. With shared experts, shallow and deep layers can access the same expert within a single forward pass, which the paper describes as an activation-level backward residual connection. The term is conceptual rather than literal backpropagation, but the intended point is clear: parameter updates and representation access become less strictly layer-local. This differs from Looped Transformers, which also reuse parameters across depth but do so by increasing recurrence and serial depth. Meta Experts keep the number of layers unchanged and instead alter the cross-layer access topology of experts.74:T68e,The experimental section appears to have three main parts. First, the headline comparison: models with Meta Experts achieve lower cross-entropy loss and higher downstream accuracy than purely Local-Expert MoE baselines. The most important quantitative result stated in the text is that, under a fixed number of activated experts and fixed expert granularity, the proposed model matches vanilla MoE performance with only about 70% of the total experts. That implies higher effective capacity per parameter.

Second, the paper runs structural ablations over the Meta/Local total-number ratio, the activated-number ratio, whether Meta Experts are present in every layer, and whether only part of the hierarchy is shared. The takeaway is not that one narrow configuration wins, but that Meta Experts help fairly consistently across a range of settings. That is useful because it suggests the gain is not tied to a fragile hyperparameter point.

Third, the paper includes mechanism-oriented analyses around parameter redundancy and representation retrieval paths. The authors argue that Meta Experts reduce redundancy and provide more flexible storage/retrieval routes for hidden states. The explanation is still empirical rather than fully formal, but it goes beyond a simple “fewer parameters, same performance” story.

From the provided full-text excerpt, the exact model sizes, training-token counts, benchmark names, and absolute downstream gains are not visible, so it would be unsafe to invent them. The reliable quantitative claim available here is the “70% experts for comparable performance” result, together with lower cross-entropy and better downstream accuracy.75:T4f4,This is a skim paper, so the goal is to decide whether the idea is structurally meaningful rather than to inspect every derivation. Start with the introduction and isolate the real target: the paper is not mainly about routing stability or load balancing, but about redundancy across depth. Then jump to the method figure and equations defining Meta Experts. Check exactly what is shared: only the expert pool, or also the router; and whether each layer routes over the same candidate set or a mixed local/shared set.

After that, spend most of the time on the empirical comparison section. Three plots or tables matter most: performance versus total expert count under fixed activation budget, ablations over the Meta/Local ratio, and results when only some layers use Meta Experts. Those are the pieces that tell you whether the method is a robust architectural change or just a narrow parameter-sharing trick.

Finally, read the residual-connection explanation with some caution. The useful question is whether the claimed activation-level backward residual can be turned into measurable quantities such as cross-layer co-activation patterns, gradient similarity, expert specialization, or expert usage entropy. A practical skim should take around 30 to 45 minutes.76:T8ec,There are two central components. The first is the Asymmetric Planner-Executor architecture. A diffusion LM acts as the planner and generates K reasoning trajectories in parallel for the same query. A larger autoregressive model acts as the executor, evaluates the candidates, selects the best plan, and synthesizes the final answer. The asymmetry is not just about model size. It is about role specialization: the DLM handles parallel exploration, while the ARM handles conditional understanding, candidate discrimination, and fluent final synthesis. This division is motivated by the fact that bidirectional denoising is naturally suited to globally refining a whole reasoning trace, whereas AR models remain stronger at coherent conditional generation once candidate plans are available.

The second component is RDC, Reward-Guided Denoising for CoT. The paper interprets each reverse diffusion step as a thought step, and the full denoising trajectory as a stochastic chain of thought. Standard diffusion training optimizes reconstruction or likelihood-related objectives; RDC augments this with a terminal reward that reflects whether the trajectory leads to a correct answer. In the paper’s framing, this is an integrated denoising-guidance objective: instead of reranking trajectories only after generation, the reverse transition operator p_theta(x_{t-1} | x_t, q) is trained to prefer intermediate states that are more likely to end in correct solutions. That is the key distinction from best-of-N or post hoc reranking. The reward is meant to reshape the planner’s generation distribution, not just filter its outputs.

From a modeling perspective, the important move is to treat diffusion trajectories explicitly as reasoning trajectories and to inject outcome supervision into the denoising dynamics. This differs from AR process reward models, which usually score already generated steps. Here the reward influences the denoising transitions themselves. The paper also includes a theoretical motivation: under logarithmic resource constraints, parallel refinement is argued to be strictly more expressive than strictly sequential generation. That result is best read as architectural motivation rather than a decisive complexity-theoretic prescription for deployment.77:T4c3,From the visible full-text content, the headline result is that CoRAL outperforms prior diffusion-based methods on vision-language reasoning benchmarks and approaches strong AR baselines in the quality-efficiency tradeoff. However, the provided content does not include the full result tables, model sizes, training-token counts, planner/executor scales, benchmark names, or exact gains, so it would be unsafe to invent precise numbers.

That said, the experimental structure is fairly clear from the method. The critical comparisons should be: CoRAL versus pure DLM reasoning and pure ARM reasoning, to test whether the hybrid architecture actually improves the quality-latency tradeoff; RDC versus standard diffusion training, to verify that reward-guided denoising improves correctness rather than surface fluency; ablations over the number of parallel trajectories K, to study diversity versus executor selection gain; and efficiency analyses, ideally in wall-clock or decoding rounds, to support the claim that parallel planning mitigates the sequential bottleneck. When reading the experiments, the main question is whether the gains truly come from better planner behavior or mostly from executor-side reranking.78:T518,This is a skim paper, not one to read line by line. Then inspect the main architecture figure and the APE interface. It matters whether the planner outputs full chains of thought, compressed plans, or some intermediate representation. After that, read the RDC section with one question in mind: how exactly does the reward enter the denoising objective, and does training require verifiable answers or an external judge?

The authors set the classification prior's max_classes to two and keep the rest of the TabICLv2 recipe unchanged, including optimizer settings, learning rate, weight decay, dropout, sequence-length distribution, and the regression prior configuration. The proposed explanation is that classification is implemented as an in-context comparison operation. Labels from the training rows are encoded and injected into the context, and predictions are obtained by comparing query-row representations against class-conditioned representations or prototypes derived from the context. Under a shared label encoder, the model is not tied to a fixed class-specific embedding table, so binary match/mismatch supervision can train an operator that accepts more than two candidate classes at inference. The paper also separates three notions that are often conflated: the class count sampled by the prior, the per-forward comparison cap, and the number of classes the system can express. In TabICL-style inference, K-way problems can be decomposed into smaller subproblems and recombined through hierarchical classification and mixed-radix ensembling, so max_classes limits one comparison step rather than the total output cardinality.7a:T408,On 38 TabArena classification datasets, using 200 bootstrap rounds and an Elo scale anchored at the default Random Forest = 1000, the binary two-stage recipe reaches 1590.1 Elo with bagging inference. Expect ~30–45 minutes for a solid skim; deeper reading is needed if you plan to reproduce or adapt the privacy accounting and the guidance mechanics.7d:Taa6,方法由三个关键部件组成。

第一，训练目标。作者采用 uniform token replacement 而不是 mask corruption。也就是每个位置以概率 1-α_t 被替换成词表中的均匀随机 token，而不是替换成特殊 [MASK]。这样得到的输入始终是一份“完整草稿”，错误 token 没有显式标记，模型必须同时学会两件事：当当前位置本来就对时要保留，当它错时要修复。训练时在所有位置上监督 clean-token posterior，等价于让 denoiser 在完整但带噪的草稿上做全位置重建。

第二，单次前向的上下文评估。直接拿 denoiser 对当前 token 的概率给草稿打分会有偏差，因为在 uniform corruption 信道下，观察到 token x_i 本身会显著提高 x_i 为真的后验概率，即便把该位置拿掉后，周围上下文其实更支持另一个 token。作者用已知的 corruption process 做 Bayes 校正，把“观察到自身 token 带来的证据”除掉，再重归一化，恢复出该位置的 cavity conditional，也就是 p(x_i | c, z_{-i}, t) 这一类“给定条件和其他 noisy token，但不看自己”的分布。然后把草稿每个位置真实 token 的负对数 cavity conditional 相加，得到 cavity energy。这个量不是精确联合似然，而是一个噪声平滑后的 pseudo-likelihood 型能量分数，但足够用于候选草稿之间的比较。

第三，推理算法 propose-read-retain。推理不是标准 diffusion ancestral sampling，也不是每轮完全重启。流程是：保留当前最优草稿；对其做部分 re-noise，避免陷入局部最优，同时保留部分结构；用同一个 denoiser 对所有位置并行预测 clean token，直接形成 candidate draft；再用一次新的前向、在固定 read noise level 下计算 candidate 的 cavity energy；若能量更低则接受，否则保留旧草稿。所有 proposal pass 和 scoring pass 都计入固定预算，最后返回最低能量的草稿。这里有两个设计很关键：一是“提案”和“评估”分开，避免用生成时的同一组 logits 给自己背书；二是 retain best draft，而不是每轮独立采样，这使得搜索更像局部修订而不是盲目重启。

和已有方法相比，差异主要在三点。相对 MDLM/UDLM 一类离散 diffusion，作者不依赖 reverse transition 逐步采样，而是把 denoiser 的 clean-token 预测直接当作修订操作。相对普通 non-autoregressive refinement，作者补上了一个有理论依据的整稿评分机制，而不是默认并行替换一定更好。相对 energy-based LM，这里的能量不是单独训练的打分器，而是从 denoiser 的后验结构中解析出来的。7e:T477,For pretraining and alternative language-modeling paradigms, the contribution is meaningful in three ways. First, it moves diffusion-style language modeling away from schedule-driven ancestral denoising toward a draft-refinement loop where the denoiser acts as both editor and evaluator. Second, it introduces cavity energy, which turns a denoiser trained under uniform corruption into a contextual whole-draft scoring mechanism resembling noise-smoothed pseudo-likelihood. That is relevant beyond this paper: masked LM, any-order LM, energy-based LM, and draft-based reasoning all face the same issue of scoring partially self-supported token configurations. Third, it identifies and fixes a subtle but important failure mode: denoiser confidence on an observed token mixes contextual support with evidence from seeing that token itself. If that self-token evidence is not removed, the model can prefer internally stable but wrong drafts. This is not a drop-in replacement for mainstream large-scale AR pretraining, but it is a serious step in the line of work that tries to challenge next-token decoding with alternative generation dynamics.7f:T9f4,The method has three main components.

1) Training under uniform corruption. Instead of mask corruption, each token is independently replaced with a uniformly sampled vocabulary token with probability 1-α_t. The noisy input is therefore always a complete draft: every position contains an ordinary token, and wrong positions are unmarked. The denoiser is trained to reconstruct the clean sequence at every position. This forces it to learn both preservation and repair: keep a token when it is already supported, change it when the surrounding draft suggests it is wrong.

2) One-pass contextual evaluation via cavity correction. A naive score based on the denoiser probability of the current token is biased, because under the known corruption channel, observing token x_i itself is strong evidence in favor of x_i, even if the rest of the draft would support another token. The paper derives a correction that divides out this self-token likelihood and renormalizes, recovering the cavity conditional: the distribution of x_i given the condition and all other noisy draft tokens, but not the observed token at position i itself. Summing the negative log cavity probabilities assigned to the draft tokens yields cavity energy. This is not an exact joint likelihood; it is a learned, noise-smoothed pseudo-likelihood-style energy. But it is enough to rank candidate drafts.

3) Propose-read-retain inference. Inference starts from random tokens. At each round, the current retained draft is partially re-noised, then the same denoiser predicts clean tokens in parallel to form a candidate draft directly, without a diffusion reverse transition. A fresh forward pass at a fixed read level computes the candidate's cavity energy. The candidate is accepted only if its energy is lower; otherwise the retained draft stays. Proposal passes and scoring passes both count toward a fixed inference budget, and the final output is the lowest-energy draft seen so far.

The design differences from prior work are important. Compared with MDLM/UDLM-style discrete diffusion, the model does not rely on schedule-specific reverse transitions for generation; clean-token predictions are used directly as edits. Compared with generic non-autoregressive refinement, the paper adds a principled whole-draft evaluation rule instead of assuming that parallel local improvements compose globally. Compared with energy-based LM, the energy is not learned by a separate scorer; it is extracted from the denoiser's posterior structure using the known corruption process.80:T686,Experiments focus on synthetic reasoning tasks that require global consistency rather than fluent local continuation: Countdown, Sudoku-Extreme, and Maze-Hard. The model is small, only 6M parameters, which makes the comparison about generation dynamics rather than scale.

Main results: DRLM reaches 87.6% on Countdown-4, 44.4% on Countdown-5, 93.9% on Sudoku-Extreme, and 73.0% on Maze-Hard. Relative to the strongest diffusion baseline evaluated in the paper, the gains are +14.3, +34.1, +28.4, and +33.7 percentage points respectively. The size of the gains suggests that the benefit is not a minor decoding tweak; it comes from the proposal-and-evaluation loop itself.

The ablations are especially informative. Retaining the best draft matters: restarting independently or failing to preserve the lowest-energy draft hurts performance, which shows that the search accumulates structured improvements over time. Partial re-noising is better than either freezing the draft too aggressively or restarting from scratch, indicating a useful balance between preserving global structure and escaping local optima. Self-token correction is critical: without it, the model overvalues drafts whose tokens are merely self-supported by observation under the corruption channel. Separating proposal from evaluation with a fresh read pass also helps, meaning the logits used to generate a candidate should not be trusted as an unbiased score of that same candidate.

The largest gain appears on Countdown-5, which is consistent with the paper's claim: the harder the task depends on global compatibility among many local choices, the more valuable whole-draft evaluation becomes.81:T599,Read the paper in three passes.

First, focus on the cavity derivation. The key question is not whether every equation is elegant, but why denoiser confidence on an observed token is biased in the first place, how the known corruption channel lets the authors remove that bias, and why the resulting quantity behaves like a pseudo-likelihood term. That is the conceptual center of the paper.

Second, study the propose-read-retain algorithm and its pseudocode. Pay attention to the separation between proposal noise and read level, and to the use of a fresh scoring pass. This is what turns the method into energy-controlled local search rather than ordinary diffusion decoding.

Third, spend time on the ablations. The most important comparisons are: with vs. without self-token correction, with vs. without best-draft retention, and with partial re-noising vs. alternative restart strategies. Those three ablations map almost exactly to the three pillars of the method.

A denoising head is trained with regression (MSE) to predict clean embeddings (x-prediction), and a decoding head maps embeddings to vocabulary only at the final step.

Mechanism argument:
1) Measure tail collapse by comparing generated word rates to held-out human text from the same distribution, with rarity defined by corpus frequency (not model probability).
2) Explain collapse via mean-seeking regression: when the conditional distribution over tokens is multi-modal (rare token vs common competitor), regression pulls the state toward the conditional mean, effectively favoring the common mode. By the time the final decoding head is applied, each position has only ~1.02–1.05 “effective candidates,” so sampler knobs cannot recover the tail.

GRAFT (training-free) restores a discrete sampling interface mid-generation:
- During denoising, it periodically reads the decoding head to obtain a token distribution.
- It identifies rare tokens that still have substantial probability but are being overtaken by more common competitors.
- It restarts generation from noise while hard-fixing (committing) those rare tokens from the first step, letting the rest of the sequence adapt around them.
- Repeating this read-and-restart accumulates committed rare words; a final generation produces the output.
Subword-level constraints and an anti-repetition correction reduce artifacts introduced by hard token fixing.83:T44e,HMDLM augments masked discrete diffusion with a discrete hierarchy variable h_i for each position.
- Forward diffusion: not only corrupts tokens x toward [MASK], but also diffuses hierarchy states toward an unknown/masked state, so the reverse process must recover structure.
- Reverse denoising is factorized into two stages:
  1) Predict hierarchy for masked positions: p(h | x_t).
  2) Predict tokens conditioned on hierarchy: p(x_0 | x_t, h).
  This encourages the model to infer “which level this position belongs to” before committing to token identities.
- Level-specific schedules: each hierarchy level has its own noise/unmasking schedule, implementing “resolve higher-level positions earlier” at the process level rather than via ad-hoc decoding.
- Training: derives a hierarchy-aware negative ELBO (NELBO) for the joint diffusion over tokens and hierarchy.
- Position-hierarchy vs prior work: contrasts with anchor-based diffusion (importance depends on token identity) and planning-aware decoding (often inference-time only); HMDLM bakes hierarchy into both training and generation.84:T7fe,The paper is a controlled empirical study built around five pretraining variants. The starting point is an 86M-parameter model trained on four languages in four scripts. From there, mpixel 8l adds four more languages in an already seen script, allowing the authors to test language diversity while holding script familiarity fixed. mpixel 8s adds four languages in previously unseen scripts, testing script diversity. mpixel base combines both expansions and reaches sixteen languages. mpixel large scales capacity from 86M to 307M to test whether larger models mitigate multilingual interference.

The data comes from FineWeb and multilingual FineWeb2. A notable design choice is to allocate equal numbers of image patches per language rather than equal numbers of documents or text tokens. That is the right unit for a pixel LM and makes compute more comparable across scripts. Each language receives roughly 7.5B image patches, with a maximum sequence length of 512 patches.

A technically important part is the multilingual rendering strategy. The paper does not use one universal rendering rule. It defaults to grapheme-aware bigrams to avoid splitting diacritics from base characters. For CJK, where wide characters make bigrams inefficient, it renders one character per patch. For Arabic and Hebrew, where bigram rendering can break ligatures and visual order can distort word structure, it uses word-level rendering in logical order. This is partly an engineering contribution, but for pixel LMs it directly affects redundancy, effective context length, and cross-lingual sharing.

The analysis goes beyond downstream scores. The authors use ABX discrimination to study cross-lingual alignment and probing to locate sentence-level and word-level information across layers.
