If the goal is to assess broader relevance to test-time compute control, spend extra time on the dataset construction and the offline optimization details, especially how prefix-level annotations are obtained and how gamma conditioning allows one policy to cover multiple budget settings.c3:T815,方法分三层。第一层是训练。作者不用单独的 draft model，而是在同一个模型里联合训练 next-token prediction 和 MTP。这样模型既保留标准 AR path，又学会 mask-conditioned 的 block-causal drafting。这里的关键不是简单多一个 loss，而是让模型在 block 预测时适应“缺少中间真实 token 输入”的条件，从而缓解 naive masked drafting 的质量损失。

第二层是解码。作者给了三种策略：confidence-only、speculative-only、hybrid。confidence-only 依赖模型自身置信度决定接受前缀，不走额外 verifier；speculative-only 用 AR path 做验证；hybrid 在两者之间折中，提供不同 quality-throughput operating point。这里的设计重点是单模型双能力：同一个 backbone 既能并行 draft，又能顺序 verify，避免传统 speculative decoding 需要双模型带来的额外存储和调度复杂度。

第三层是 runtime，也是文章最有信息量的部分。M1 是按 replay width 专门化的低比特执行，并使用 role-dependent output projection，减少不同 block 宽度下的无效计算。M2 是 finite-state CUDA Graph atlas：把 accepted-prefix 变化后可能到达的 pending-prefix 状态离散成可 replay 的固定形状图，并在 shared KV storage 上复用历史，避免每次都做全历史复制。M3 是在 hybrid decoding 中把 verifier 输入准备提前到 host 分支决策之前，减少 CPU-GPU 同步和调度空洞。贯穿三者的是 accepted-prefix alignment：已提交前缀、已 materialize 的 causal KV 边界、以及 CUDA Graph 当前 replay 状态必须保持一致，否则 graph reuse 会失效，甚至产生错误状态。

和已有 MTP 或 speculative decoding 相比，区别主要有三点。第一，它面向 ultra-low-bit backbone，而不是默认 BF16/FP16。第二，它把“动态 accepted prefix”当成一等公民来设计 runtime，而不是只在算法上讨论接受率。第三，它强调单模型 joint NTP+MTP，而不是 draft/verifier 双模型分工。c4:T7f9,The method has three layers. First, training: instead of using a separate draft model, the authors jointly train next-token prediction and MTP within a single model. This preserves a standard AR path while teaching the model mask-conditioned block-causal drafting. The key point is not merely adding another loss, but adapting the model to block prediction without intermediate ground-truth token inputs, which is where naive masked drafting loses quality.

Second, decoding: BitMTP supports confidence-only, speculative-only, and hybrid decoding. Confidence-only accepts prefixes based on model confidence and avoids verifier replay. Speculative-only uses the model’s AR path for verification. Hybrid trades off quality and throughput between the two. The notable design choice is single-model dual capability: the same backbone can draft in parallel and verify autoregressively, avoiding the storage and scheduling complexity of separate draft/verifier models.

Third, runtime: this is the most informative part of the paper. M1 specializes low-bit execution by replay width and uses role-dependent output projections to reduce wasted block computation. M2 builds a finite-state CUDA Graph atlas so that reachable pending-prefix states can be replayed with fixed shapes over shared KV storage, avoiding full-history copying. M3 hoists verifier-input preparation ahead of the host branch decision in hybrid decoding, reducing CPU-GPU synchronization gaps. The unifying constraint is accepted-prefix alignment: the committed prefix, the materialized causal-KV boundary, and the CUDA Graph replay state must stay consistent, otherwise graph reuse breaks or becomes incorrect.

Compared with prior MTP or speculative decoding work, the main differences are: it targets ultra-low-bit backbones rather than standard precision; it treats dynamic accepted prefixes as a runtime design problem rather than only an algorithmic acceptance-rate issue; and it emphasizes a joint NTP+MTP single-model setup instead of a two-model draft/verifier split.c5:T501,The experiments cover BitNet b1.58-2B and Bonsai models from 1.7B to 4B, evaluated on H20, RTX 3090, and Jetson Orin. This is an important empirical point: in low-bit settings, iteration cost and accepted-prefix-dependent KV work can dominate the benefit of fewer decoding steps.

With the full BitMTP stack, the paper reports mean decoding speedups up to 2.4× on H20 and 2.0× on RTX 3090, and a 3.3× speedup on MBPP+ on Jetson Orin. The results are presented at comparable task quality against the SFT AR baseline, not as raw throughput-only wins.

The ablations examine whether the joint objective recovers quality, how the three decoding policies trace different quality-throughput tradeoffs, and how M1/M2/M3 reduce kernel, memory, and scheduling overheads. For practitioners, the most valuable evidence is the failure analysis of the naive combination and the measured benefit of accepted-prefix-aware graph replay.c6:T455,PW-Pruning extends DO-ACP with phase-aware statistics. A speech request is split into two phases: acoustic-prefill tokens for listening, and teacher-forced answer tokens for generation. For each layer and each phase, the method records whether the original router selected an expert, the pre-top-k router softmax probability, and the expert’s ungated output. These are used to build phase-conditioned routing confidence, an output Gram matrix, and an ACP-style importance weighting that combines routing confidence with output magnitude. The selector then optimizes a phase-weighted regularized log-determinant objective over a single retained expert set. The log-det term favors feature volume, so it rewards both high-energy experts and non-redundant experts. Greedy selection is implemented with Schur residuals and Cholesky updates. The important deployment choice is that PW-Pruning still produces one static expert bank. It does not require phase labels or runtime mask switching. Compared with pooled DO-ACP, the change is when phase information is discarded, not the expert budget or routing fan-in.c7:T7fb,方法核心是 Stratified Sparse Attention，简称 SSA。思路可以概括成两层：先确定性保留一部分“高置信” token，再对剩余 token 按 proxy score 做重要性采样，而不是均匀采样。这里的 proxy score 是对真实 attention score 的廉价近似，用来避免对全量 KV 做精确打分。论文把 dense attention 看成对所有 value 的加权求和，然后把 sparse approximation 写成一个分层估计器：

1. 确定性层。先根据 proxy score 选出一组 heavy hitters。这个集合承担“低偏差”角色，确保高质量注意力质量块不会被采样噪声破坏。
2. 随机层。对剩余 token 不再一视同仁，而是按 proxy-guided distribution 采样。采样后用 importance weighting 做无偏或近无偏估计，从而把预算集中到更可能承载 residual mass 的位置。
3. 统一框架。作者把 top-k、top-p、top-k+uniform sampling 等都放进同一个框架里理解：它们只是 deterministic stratum 和 stochastic stratum 的不同特例。SSA 的区别不在“混合”本身，而在 residual 部分使用 score-guided sampling。
4. 理论部分。论文给出近似误差界，分析 proxy 质量、预算分配、残余质量分布与输出误差之间的关系。直观上，若 proxy 与真实分数排序相关，且高质量 token 已被 deterministic 层截住，那么在 residual 上做 importance sampling 会比 uniform sampling 有更低方差。
5. 系统实现。作者实现了配套 CUDA/Triton kernel，目标是减少 gather/scatter 和不规则访存带来的额外开销。因为很多 sparse attention 方法在 paper 上省 FLOPs，但 kernel 不友好，最后并不能换来 decode speedup。SSA 明显把这一点作为设计约束。

和已有方法相比，Quest / PQCache 更偏确定性检索；MagicPig 更偏采样估计；vAttention 是 top-k 加 uniform tail。SSA 的新意在于把“尾部覆盖”从盲采样改成了有分数引导的探索，因此在 attention 分布不够尖锐时更稳。c8:T746,The method, Stratified Sparse Attention (SSA), combines deterministic retention of high-confidence tokens with score-guided importance sampling over the remainder. The key idea is to treat sparse attention as a two-stratum estimator.

1. Deterministic stratum. A proxy score is used to select a heavy-hitter set. This part reduces bias by ensuring that the largest contributors to attention are always included.
2. Stochastic stratum. Instead of uniformly sampling from the residual tokens, SSA samples according to a proxy-guided distribution. Importance weighting is then used so that the residual contribution is estimated with much lower variance than uniform tail sampling.
3. Unified view. The paper shows that top-k, top-p, and top-k plus sampling can all be interpreted within the same framework as special cases with different deterministic and stochastic allocations. SSA differs from prior hybrids because the stochastic part is score-aware rather than blind.
4. Theory. The analysis provides approximation guarantees that relate output error to proxy quality, budget allocation, and the distribution of residual attention mass. The intuition is straightforward: once the head is captured deterministically, importance sampling over a non-uniform tail is preferable to uniform sampling whenever the proxy preserves useful score structure.
5. Systems implementation. The authors implement CUDA and Triton kernels to make the method practical at decode time. This is important because many sparse-attention methods reduce nominal FLOPs but fail to deliver end-to-end gains due to irregular memory access and kernel overhead.

Relative to prior work, Quest and PQCache are more retrieval-centric, MagicPig is more sampling-centric, and vAttention uses top-k plus uniform sampling. SSA’s main novelty is the score-guided exploration of the residual set.c9:T5ab,The evaluation spans several open models and multiple long-context benchmarks. Models include Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen3.5-4B, Qwen3.5-9B, Ministral-3-3B-Instruct-2517, and Ministral-3-8B-Instruct-2517. Benchmarks include RULER, LongBench, LOFT, and AIME, which gives a mix of retrieval-heavy long-context tasks and more reasoning-sensitive settings.

The main empirical findings are:
1. Under aggressive sparsity, SSA consistently outperforms deterministic retrieval baselines, sampling-based baselines, and hybrid baselines, reducing the gap to dense attention.
2. In the preliminary analysis, score-guided importance sampling achieves lower relative L2 error than uniform sampling. This is an important mechanistic result because it directly validates the design choice rather than relying only on downstream task scores.
3. The paper includes an oracle reference using exact top-k plus exact importance sampling. That helps separate the error due to imperfect proxies from the error due to the sparse estimator itself.

Scalar quantization maps each weight to one of a few discrete levels; at 2 bits this representational set is too limited, and error-aware methods such as GPTQ-style objectives, SpinQuant, or QuaRot can still fail. Vector quantization maps a small weight vector to an entry in a learned codebook, which preserves correlations among dimensions that scalar grids discard. The study uses VPTQ and YAQA under a shared rotated frame. On the data side, calibration affects the Hessian used to weight quantization error, while recovery data is used for short-budget distillation after quantization. A useful engineering idea is to precompute Hessians for individual domains and sweep calibration mixtures by linearly reweighting those Hessians. Recovery freezes the quantized backbone and trains only quantization parameters, such as codebooks or scales, using a full-precision teacher with a mixture of cross-entropy and temperature-scaled KL distillation. 难点在于反馈是部分可见的。如果当前只尝试较短 horizon，就看不到更后面位置的验证结果；而 hazard 需要在“surviving prefixes”的分布下估计，不是简单对所有 proposal 前缀做监督。为此作者提出 survival-weighted regression objective，让学习目标和最终决策目标一致。在线算法层面，AMTP 在每轮 drafting 前，用当前 hazard 预测和 latency 估计计算各个 horizon 的预期 throughput，然后大部分时间贪心选最优 horizon，少部分时间随机探索 full horizon，以获得后续位置的反馈。由于探索分布不是均匀可见，训练更新使用 inverse-probability weighting 来构造无偏估计。文中还给出 regret 分析，把 horizon-selection 的 conditional throughput regret 上界到累计 hazard prediction error。

值得注意的是，这篇方法不改 verifier，不训练新的 MTP head，也不要求重新训练 draft model。它利用的是部署时天然存在的 acceptance/rejection 信号，因此工程侵入性很低。和已有自适应 speculative decoding 方法相比，它的区别在于：一，决策发生在 drafting 之前，适配 MTP 的并行 head 结构；二，目标是 exact verification 下的 throughput，而不是 greedy 近似或额外训练的 confidence proxy。ce:T8eb,The key idea is to cast horizon selection as conditional throughput optimization. For each candidate horizon h, the objective is not simply the expected number of accepted tokens. It is the ratio between expected committed tokens and expected round latency. The central statistic is acceptance survival: the probability that the draft prefix up to position i is fully accepted. This quantity determines the expected number of committed tokens for a given horizon. The paper further decomposes survival in terms of conditional rejection hazards, namely the probability that position i is rejected given that all earlier draft positions were accepted. Once these hazards are estimated, the controller can evaluate the expected throughput of each horizon.

The main difficulty is partial feedback. If the system chooses a short horizon, it never observes verification outcomes for later positions. Moreover, the hazards must be estimated under the distribution of surviving prefixes, not merely over all proposed prefixes. To address this, the paper derives a survival-weighted regression objective aligned with the downstream decision problem. AMTP then uses this objective in an online learning loop. Before drafting, it predicts hazards and latency, computes the expected throughput for each horizon, and usually chooses the best one greedily. To avoid blind spots at longer horizons, it occasionally performs randomized full-horizon exploration. Because those observations are collected under a nonuniform exploration policy, the updates use inverse-probability weighting to obtain unbiased estimates of the survival-weighted loss. The paper also provides a regret analysis that upper-bounds conditional throughput regret in terms of cumulative hazard-prediction error.

A notable strength is that AMTP is training-free in the deployment sense: it does not retrain the draft model, does not modify the verifier, and does not add new MTP heads. It exploits acceptance and rejection signals that already exist in speculative decoding. Relative to prior adaptive methods, its distinction is that the decision is made before drafting, which matches the structure of MTP, and the objective is exact-verification throughput rather than a proxy confidence score or a greedy-only criterion.cf:T4c2,From the visible content, the evaluation is framed against a strong benchmark: not only the best fixed horizon, but also regret relative to the best horizon at each visited context. The paper studies whether online learning from verification feedback can approach this context-wise oracle. The provided text does not include the full numerical tables, so it would be inappropriate to state exact speedups or acceptance-rate gains.

When reading the experiments, focus on four things. First, the throughput improvement over fixed-horizon baselines across different tasks, draft-target pairs, and latency regimes. Second, comparisons against simpler adaptive heuristics, such as rules based on average acceptance rate or entropy-style confidence. Third, the exploration-exploitation tradeoff: too little exploration prevents learning about long horizons, while too much exploration hurts immediate throughput. Fourth, error attribution: does performance degrade mainly because latency is hard to estimate, or because survival and hazard predictions are poorly calibrated? 1) Offline profiling + optimization: collect per-step expert load traces on representative mixed workloads, filter transient step noise, and infer persistent complementarity relations. Then perform a two-stage optimization: group experts whose loads offset over time, and map groups onto nearby NMP cores/tiles to keep weights local while stabilizing group-level load.
2) CMN (Collaborative Memory-Network): complementarity mostly helps at the group level; within-group transient hotspots remain. Since hot expert weights are pinned to a host core, naive helping would cause repeated remote weight fetches. CMN adds a lightweight memory-controller/NoC mechanism: the host loads a hot expert’s weight tile once from local DRAM and streams/broadcasts it to helper cores via a temporary broadcast path created by lightweight NoC reconfiguration (“load once, broadcast to many”), reducing redundant DRAM reads and packet overhead.
3) Tiered online correction: to handle workload drift without frequent global re-optimization, apply frequent low-cost local adjustments and reserve higher-cost reconfigurations for longer-term shifts.d2:T54e,The proposed method is D-PAL, Dynamic Position-wise Acceptance Loss. It starts from the exact expected accepted length of a draft block and replaces D-PACE’s confidence proxy q_t(y*_t) with the true overlap signal α_t = Σ_v min(p_t,v, q_t,v) = 1 - TV(p_t, q_t). Differentiating the expected accepted length gives dynamic position weights: early positions receive larger weights because a rejection there truncates the rest of the block. The same derivation yields log acceptance, -log α_t, as the local loss. When the target distribution degenerates to a point mass, this reduces to the D-PACE formulation.

The paper also separates the weighting scheme from the local loss by detaching the weights. This allows D-PAL[X] variants with different local losses. The authors compare log acceptance, forward KL, Rényi divergence of order 1/2, TV, and CE+TV. A useful finding is that log acceptance is not necessarily the best choice despite coming from the derivation: it is not differentiable when draft and target probabilities coincide, and its gradient does not vanish near q=p. KL and Rényi-1/2 have better local behavior near the target distribution. Rényi-1/2 is especially appealing because it bounds the overlap from both sides. The paper also proves a proposition connecting overlap to the argmax proposals used by deployed DFlash-style systems.d3:T925,方法上有三层。第一层是 trace-level accounting。作者从 decode iteration 的共享结构出发，把每个有效输出 token 的逻辑字节需求写成两部分：共享的 dense weights 和私有的 KV history。定义 Mw 为一次迭代中需要参与计算的 dense weight footprint，Beff 为该迭代实际产生的有效输出数，KKV 为每个缓存 token 的 key+value 总字节数，L̄token 为按有效输出加权的平均注意历史长度。于是每 token 的逻辑读需求是 Atoken = Mw/Beff + KKV·L̄token；若把每生成一个 token 还要写入一条新的 KV 记录算进去，则读写需求变成 Atoken_rw = Mw/Beff + KKV·(L̄token+1)。这里最关键的不是公式本身，而是共享与私有两类工作被明确分开：batch 只摊薄前者，context 只放大后者。

第二层是把逻辑字节坐标转成可回归的能耗变量。作者把共享权重项写成 q_w = Mw/(10^9·Beff)，把 KV 读写项写成 q_KV = KKV·(L̄token+1)/10^9，再引入 realized time per token，记为 τ，即总 decode 时长除以有效输出 token 数。最终用一个 affine 形式去拟合 token energy，大意是把 q_w、q_KV、τ 以及常数项放进同一个线性响应模型。这样做的含义是：能耗既受“需要搬多少字节”影响，也受“这些工作在硬件上花了多久”影响；单独看 bytes 或单独看 time 都不够。

第三层是把逻辑 accounting 和物理实现联系起来。论文没有停留在符号推导，而是强调 active bytes 是 trace 的 principal account，不等于所有驻留显存，也不等于所有 operator 的全部访问。像 embedding lookup、positional access 这类不在主账本里的访问，需要单独处理。作者再用 HBM 测量去检验这些逻辑坐标与真实物理流量之间的关系，并按模型和硬件分别校准系数。这个设计比直接做黑盒回归更稳，因为变量有明确语义，也更容易解释为什么某些配置下能耗变化来自 batch 摊薄、某些来自 KV 增长、某些来自时间拉长。

从方法取舍看，这篇工作刻意没有把所有系统细节都塞进模型，而是保留一个小而可解释的主干。代价是覆盖面有限；好处是可以作为 dense decode 的一阶近似规律，用来做部署前估算和设计空间分析。d4:T83f,The method has three layers.

First, the paper builds a trace-level accounting identity for decode work. In each decode iteration, dense weights are shared across all useful outputs, while each output token attends to its own KV history. Let Mw be the dense-weight footprint in bytes, Beff the realized mean number of useful outputs per iteration, KKV the combined key-value bytes per cached token across layers, and L̄token the useful-token-weighted mean attended history length. Then the logical read demand per useful output token is Atoken = Mw/Beff + KKV·L̄token. If one also accounts for writing one new KV record per generated token, the read-write demand becomes Atoken_rw = Mw/Beff + KKV·(L̄token + 1). The key idea is structural: batch size and context length affect different terms, rather than entering the model as interchangeable scalar knobs.

Second, the authors convert this accounting into regression coordinates for energy. They define q_w = Mw/(10^9·Beff) for shared dense-weight bytes and q_KV = KKV·(L̄token + 1)/10^9 for KV read-write bytes, both in decimal GB, and introduce realized decode time per token, τ, computed from total decode duration divided by useful output tokens. Token energy is then modeled with a common affine form over q_w, q_KV, τ, and a constant term. This is an important design choice: bytes alone are not enough, because the same logical byte demand can be realized with different occupancy, kernel efficiency, communication overhead, and stall behavior.

Third, the paper connects logical accounting to physical memory behavior. Active bytes are explicitly defined as the principal logical account of dense-weight and KV accesses, not all resident memory and not all operator traffic. Embedding and positional accesses sit outside the main account and require separate treatment. The authors then use HBM measurements to test how these logical coordinates map to actual physical traffic, and calibrate coefficients per model and hardware platform. Compared with a pure black-box fit, this gives the model clearer semantics and better diagnostic value.d5:T548,The provided full-text excerpt includes the introduction and the main modeling setup, but not the full experimental section, tables, or numerical results. So it would be unsafe to invent exact figures. From the paper’s setup, the experimental program appears to target three questions. First, whether the two active-byte coordinates—shared weight demand and private KV demand—can explain token-energy variation across batch size, context length, and model settings. Second, whether adding realized decode time materially improves fit quality over byte-only models, especially when hardware efficiency and kernel behavior differ. Third, whether the logical active-byte account tracks measured HBM traffic closely enough to justify the physical interpretation.

The most important results are likely trend-level rather than single-number claims: increasing Beff should reduce the shared-weight term Mw/Beff and lower energy per token in short-context regimes; increasing L̄token should linearly raise the KV term and dominate long-context energy; and systems with similar logical byte demand can still differ in energy because τ differs. A quick read takes about half an hour; a careful read is worthwhile if you work on serving, long context, or KV-related optimization.d7:T8b3,The technical contribution is a carefully controlled comparison framework. The paper compares 2:4 sparsity against dense quantization in two ways. The first is equal bits: every stored component is counted, including values, indices, scales, and zero points. Under this accounting, 2:4 is far less storage-efficient than the naive 'half the weights' intuition suggests, because each retained value carries metadata. The paper makes this concrete: 2:4 with INT8 values costs about the same as dense INT5, 2:4 with INT4 values about the same as dense INT3, and 2:4 with FP16 can even exceed FP8 in cost. The second is equal tensor-core tiers: both lower precision and 2:4 may promise similar throughput classes on paper, but the paper measures actual kernel latency and end-to-end cost rather than relying on theoretical peak throughput.

A major strength is that the comparison spans all six GEMM operand families in a transformer layer, not just static weights. Dynamic operands such as activations, Q/K/V, and attention probabilities must be pruned and compressed online, so their preprocessing overhead is part of the real deployment cost. The paper also enforces the hardware-imposed sparsity axis, which is crucial because 2:4 is not a free-form pruning pattern.

For error analysis, the paper introduces 2:4 energy loss: within each hardware-defined group of four along the reduction axis, 2:4 drops two values, and the lost energy fraction can be computed directly from the tensor. This quantity tracks the observed accuracy gap well and explains why Hadamard rotation often hurts 2:4: rotation spreads energy more evenly, so each forced local drop removes more useful signal. This is a more faithful predictor than global tensor statistics such as kurtosis, because the hardware constraint is local and axis-specific.

At the quantization floor, the paper separates one-shot pruning from retraining. The conclusion is that 2:4 can provide real speedups there, but usually only with retraining; one-shot pruning is not viable. The paper also evaluates Blackwell sparse FP4, noting that its pairwise 4:8 pattern runs faster than dense NVFP4 but discards more information and cannot directly reuse models retrained for 2:4.d8:T7b6,The experiments cover every layer of two 8B models and run on three GPU generations: Ada, Hopper, and Blackwell. The results are best understood in three parts.

First, under equal-bit comparisons, moving to a lower dense precision is consistently more accurate than adding 2:4 sparsity at the same storage budget. Part of this comes from proper bit accounting: once metadata is counted, 2:4 competes against lower-bit dense formats than many prior papers imply. The deeper reason is the error structure: 2:4 removes signal energy that cannot be recovered by increasing the precision of the surviving values, while quantization error decreases with bitwidth.

Second, under equal tensor-core tiers, the paper finds that for every throughput tier there exists a dense format that is both faster and more accurate than the corresponding 2:4 option. This remains true when online pruning and quantization costs are included, which matters because dynamic operands are expensive to sparsify on the fly.

Third, at the quantization floor, 2:4 starts to make sense. Stacked on FP8, it speeds up linear layers by about 1.3x to 1.7x. A retrained 2:4 model served with vLLM is faster than the dense FP8 model in both prefill and decode, while maintaining roughly comparable GSM8K accuracy. The paper includes an important control: if the same sparse weights are served with dense kernels, the speedup disappears, confirming that the gain comes from sparse tensor-core execution rather than unrelated implementation effects.

The retraining results are especially informative. Perplexity recovers within roughly 250M tokens, but GSM8K lags far behind and remains well below models such as Sparse-Llama that were retrained much longer on different data. This shows that perplexity can overstate functional recovery. For Blackwell sparse FP4, the kernels run about 1.4x faster than dense NVFP4, but reasoning accuracy does not recover to a practically usable level at the tested budget.d9:T7d6,方法叫 OnQ，由两部分组成。第一部分是 on-policy distillation。作者先用 block-wise calibration 初始化量化学生，具体沿用 EfficientQAT 里的 Block-AP 思路：从 RTN 出发，逐层校准每个 transformer block 的权重、scale 和 zero-point，用块级重建损失让量化块输出逼近全精度块输出。这个阶段的作用不是最终恢复能力，而是给后续 on-policy 训练一个足够稳定的起点。第二部分是学生自生成轨迹上的 teacher supervision。训练时，量化学生通过 quantized forward pass 自己采样整段 response；对每个生成前缀 h_t=(x, y_{<t})，冻结的 full-precision teacher 在同一前缀上给出 next-token 分布，学生再对这个分布做蒸馏。这样 teacher 看到的是学生真实会落到的上下文，而不是参考答案轨迹。

关键创新在损失函数。作者没有直接用 FKL 或 RKL，而是用 candidate-wise Dynamic KL。动机是：如果某个 token 上学生概率远低于 teacher，FKL 对这类 underprediction 的拉升更有效；如果学生概率远高于 teacher，RKL 对这类 overprediction 的压制更有效。于是他们按 teacher/student 概率比，为每个 candidate token 动态分配 FKL 与 RKL 的权重，而不是对整个分布只选一个 KL 方向。这个设计比“混合一个固定系数的双向 KL”更细，因为它是在 token 级别、候选级别做自适应。全文的分析部分还专门展示了高熵前缀上两侧误差更常见，这解释了为什么 reasoning 中间的不确定位置最容易出问题，也解释了 overthinking marker 会被过采样。

和已有 QAT recipe 的区别很明确：以往方法大多还是 reference trajectory distillation，或者在固定响应上做 logits matching；OnQ 把监督位置换到了学生自己的轨迹上，并且把分布对齐从单一 KL 改成了 candidate-wise 动态双向校正。前者解决 prefix mismatch，后者解决概率误差的非对称性。da:T74e,OnQ combines two components. The first is on-policy distillation. The student is initialized from a block-wise calibrated checkpoint, following the Block-AP style recipe from EfficientQAT: starting from RTN quantization, each transformer block is calibrated sequentially with a reconstruction loss so that quantized block outputs match full-precision block outputs. This gives a stable low-bit starting point.

The second component is teacher supervision on the student’s own trajectories. During training, the quantized student samples responses using its quantized forward pass. For every generated prefix h_t = (x, y_{<t}), a frozen full-precision teacher provides the next-token distribution on that exact prefix. This directly addresses prefix mismatch, because the teacher now supervises the contexts the student actually visits, including prefixes that already contain student mistakes.

The key technical idea is candidate-wise Dynamic KL. The authors show that forward KL is better at correcting severe underprediction, while reverse KL is better at suppressing severe overprediction. Instead of choosing one KL direction for the whole distribution, they assign token-wise weights between FKL and RKL based on the teacher/student probability ratio for each candidate token. This is more targeted than a fixed convex combination of the two KLs. The analysis section further shows that two-sided errors are especially common at high-entropy prefixes, which explains why reasoning trajectories become unstable exactly at uncertain intermediate steps.

Compared with prior QAT recipes, the differences are clean: prior methods mostly distill on fixed reference responses or do logit matching on static trajectories; OnQ moves supervision onto student-generated trajectories and replaces a single KL direction with candidate-wise adaptive bidirectional correction.db:T614,The experiments cover Qwen3-1.7B, 4B, and 8B at both 2-bit and 3-bit precision, giving six main settings in total. Evaluation uses a nine-benchmark average, with detailed analysis on MATH-500. The headline result is that on Qwen3-8B at 2 bits, OnQ improves the nine-benchmark average by 10.26 points over the strongest baseline. The paper also states that OnQ achieves the best average in all six settings.

The more informative results are behavioral. On MATH-500, when questions are bucketed by the full-precision model’s response length, OnQ outperforms QAT baselines in every bucket, with larger gains on longer responses. It also rarely hits the token limit, unlike the baselines. So the method is not only improving final accuracy; it is making the low-bit model terminate more like the full-precision teacher. The paper also reports shorter generations and fewer repetitive errors, consistent with its diagnosis of oversampling overthinking markers at high-entropy positions.

The ablations support the two main claims. Replacing fixed-response distillation with on-policy supervision materially improves long-chain recovery, showing that trajectory divergence is a real bottleneck. Dynamic KL is stronger than pure FKL or pure RKL because the two KL directions specialize in correcting different error modes; using only one leaves the opposite side of the distribution insufficiently corrected. Additional probability-error analyses show that high-entropy prefixes contain more frequent two-sided errors, which directly motivates the loss design.dc:T40b,RCSD combines reinforcement-style optimization with continual adaptation. Instead of forcing the draft model to reproduce target logits, it trains the draft policy to generate sequences that the target model is likely to accept. The DPO variant builds pairwise preferences: the chosen sequence is sampled autoregressively from the target model, while the rejected sequence is generated by periodically alternating between the target and draft model, with the draft producing k-token blocks without verification. In the EAGLE-style setting, the sequence representation includes both tokens and hidden states from the target model. A frozen reference draft model is used in the DPO log-ratio to regularize the update. The GRPO variant creates groups of speculative trajectories with different drafting intervals and uses their observed acceptance rates as direct rewards for relative optimization. The abstract also mentions masked loss, which avoids penalizing tokens that already align with the target and helps reduce early rejection.dd:T921,方法由三部分组成。第一部分是 periodic rounding。作者观察到，预填充阶段的 chunked kernel 本来就不是每个 token 写回一次状态，而是每个 chunk 写回一次；真正导致误差频繁注入的是 decode 阶段每 token 一次的状态落盘与量化。PACE 在解码时引入 decode buffer，把最近若干 token 的 key/value 暂存在小缓冲区里，只在 buffer flush 时才把状态推进并量化一次。这样 decode period dP 从 1 变成 8 等较小整数，量化误差注入频率下降，而且两次注入之间有更多衰减步数。论文在理论部分给出 retained error bound：某个 head 的误差保留量随 head decay 增大而增大，随 rounding period 增大而减小。这不是严格的最优性证明，但足够解释为什么“少量化几次”比“每次都量化得更精细”更有效。

第二部分是 channel-aligned grouping。作者分析 gated-delta state 的结构，发现大值不是随机散落，而是沿 state 的列方向集中；更具体地说，某些 delta-value channel 会在连续多个 token 上持续偏大，于是外积写入后在 state 中形成整列的大条纹。如果量化分组沿 value axis 横着切，会把大值和大量小值混在同一组里，共享 scale 后小值分辨率很差；如果沿 key axis、按列分组，就能让同一组内部动态范围更一致。作者用 max/RMS 指标比较不同分组方向，并通过打乱 channel 排列的实验说明这种列结构确实来自 delta channel 的时间一致性，而不是偶然统计现象。

第三部分是 head-level mixed precision。PACE-4 让所有 head 都用 4-bit；PACE-4/8 则把每层中误差保留最久的四分之一 head 保留为 8-bit，其余仍为 4-bit。这里的依据来自前面的 per-head decay 分析：高 decay head 对量化误差更敏感，统一 4-bit 不划算。这个设计很朴素，但比全局升 bit 更节省内存，也更符合递推系统的异质性。

实现上，作者还给出 Triton kernel，支持 packed 4-bit state 和 periodic decoding，说明该方法不是只在离线模拟里成立，而是考虑了真实 decode 路径中的 kernel 组织与 buffer 成本。论文也明确把 decode buffer 的显存算进总内存，而不是只报 state 本体，这是比较严谨的地方。de:T8bb,PACE combines three ideas. First, periodic rounding. During prefill, chunked kernels already update and write the recurrent state only once per chunk. The problematic regime is autoregressive decoding, where the kernel is invoked once per token and the state is quantized after every step. PACE introduces a decode buffer that stores recent keys and values for a small number of generated tokens, and only flushes them into the recurrent state every dP steps. This reduces how often quantization noise is injected. The paper derives a per-head retained-error bound showing that the surviving error increases with head decay and decreases with the rounding period. The argument is simple but useful: if the recurrence contracts errors between writebacks, less frequent rounding can outperform more frequent rounding even at the same bit width.

Second, channel-aligned grouping. The authors analyze the gated-delta state and find that large-magnitude entries are column-structured rather than randomly scattered. Intuitively, some delta-value channels stay large across many tokens, and the outer-product update writes that persistence into whole columns of the state. If quantization groups cut across columns, one large entry can dominate the shared scale and waste levels on many small entries. Grouping along the key axis, so that each group stays within a column, produces more homogeneous dynamic ranges. The paper supports this with max/RMS statistics and a channel-permutation experiment that ties the observed structure back to persistent delta channels.

Third, head-level mixed precision. PACE-4 quantizes all heads to 4-bit. PACE-4/8 keeps the quarter of heads in each layer that retain rounding error the longest at 8-bit, while the rest remain at 4-bit. This follows directly from the per-head decay analysis: some heads are much more sensitive to quantization than others, so uniform precision is wasteful.

The implementation side is also important. The paper includes Triton kernels for periodic decoding with packed 4-bit state, and it accounts for decode-buffer memory in the reported totals. That makes the evaluation more credible than papers that report only compressed state size while ignoring auxiliary buffers.df:T5db,The evaluation spans four hybrid linear-attention backbones ranging from 4B to 35B parameters. The main empirical pattern is consistent: for all sub-8-bit settings, increasing the decode rounding period from 1 to 8 reduces quality degradation. That directly validates the error-propagation story. Against prior post-hoc state quantizers such as DAMP and Q-Mamba, PACE preserves perplexity or downstream accuracy better at 4-bit, and the mixed PACE-4/8 variant closes the gap further for sensitive heads.

The ablations are the most informative part. Period ablations show that the gain comes from less frequent decode-time rounding rather than from prefill behavior; prefill chunk length is fixed at 256 in the benchmark setup. Grouping ablations show that column-aligned grouping beats row-aligned grouping, and the gap widens with larger group width because a bad grouping direction amplifies shared-scale mismatch. Precision-allocation ablations show that a small fraction of 8-bit heads captures most of the benefit. The systems experiment with Triton kernels indicates that periodic decoding keeps the throughput advantage of decode buffers rather than giving it back through packing overhead.

One deployment detail from the introduction is worth remembering: at 64-way concurrency, fp32 recurrent states account for roughly 10% to 41% of total memory occupied by weights plus states, depending on the backbone. That is large enough for state quantization to materially affect serving density.e0:T61a,The method has three components. First, PRP, a Prefix Reuse Predictor, estimates whether a prefix will be requested again within a future horizon. It uses lightweight online features rather than offline profiling. The features include structural signals such as prefix length, modality, radix-tree position, and session metadata, as well as temporal signals such as recency, frequency, inter-arrival patterns, and time-of-day effects. Second, CARS, a Cost-Aware Retention Score, converts reuse probability into a keep/evict decision using a closed-form cost model. This is the key step. A miss cost includes recomputation on a prefill node plus transfer to a decode node. An admission cost includes the initial transfer into the shared KV pool and the opportunity cost of occupying pool memory. So the decision is not merely whether reuse is likely, but whether expected reuse value exceeds retention cost under the current system configuration. Third, ATC, an Adaptive Threshold Controller, adjusts the retention threshold as pool pressure, bandwidth conditions, and workload mix change.

The paper’s main strength is the alignment between prediction and systems objective. LRU/LFU can only encode recency or frequency; they cannot express that misses on long multimodal prefixes are much more expensive, while admitting short low-value prefixes may be wasteful. The theoretical section also formalizes when the optimal admission threshold must vary with prefix length, showing that a uniform threshold is structurally suboptimal even in an idealized setting.e1:T578,The evaluation covers both language and multimodal workloads, with baselines including No-Cache, LRU-Pool, and Mooncake-LRU. The headline results are on end-to-end TTFT and inter-node transfer volume. KVLearn reduces TTFT by up to 56% versus No-Cache, 38% versus LRU-Pool, and 33% versus Mooncake-LRU. It also cuts inter-node transfer volume by up to 53% relative to LRU-Pool. On MM-Session-style multimodal workloads, it reaches near-Oracle throughput under realistic pool sizes. This suggests the gains come not just from more hits, but from avoiding low-value admissions and expensive misses.

The problem scale is also important. For a 13B model in bfloat16, a high-resolution visual prefix can consume roughly 128–512 MB of KV memory, and recomputing such a prefix on an A100 can cost around 100–400 ms. In that regime, a single wrong retention decision is expensive enough that simple recency-based policies become fragile.

The most informative ablations are likely the following. Removing the cost-aware scoring while keeping the reuse predictor should hurt noticeably, showing that reuse likelihood and retention value are different quantities. Replacing online learning with static heuristics should degrade under workload shift. And the gains should be larger on multimodal and long-prefix workloads than on short-text workloads, which is exactly where heterogeneous costs matter most.e2:T40d,For a quick read, start with the introduction and the formalization section, then move to the three modules, and finish with the main results. Three things deserve attention. First, check the objective carefully: the paper optimizes TTFT, throughput, and transfer volume, not cache hit rate in isolation. Second, focus on the CARS cost decomposition, because that is where the necessity of the method becomes clear. In disaggregated serving, both admission and miss have explicit costs. Third, pay special attention to the multimodal experiments, where the policy differences are most visible.

If time is limited, 25 to 35 minutes is enough for a useful pass. Prioritize the problem setup figure, the cost model equations, the main TTFT and transfer tables, and the ablations. If you want to go deeper, two natural follow-up questions are whether the predictor remains calibrated under workload shift or new modalities, and whether this policy can be jointly optimized with prefix-aware routing, speculative decoding, or KV compression.e3:T6f2,实验对象是 DFlash 风格的 block drafter：在 anchor 位置 a 读取 frozen target 到 a 的 hidden features，一次性预测未来 K=15 个 token slot；每个样本最多采 128 个 anchors。slot 权重用指数衰减 w_k=exp(-(k-1)/γ)，并用保留权重归一化。
对比三类训练目标：
1) CE on corpus tokens：直接对语料 token 做交叉熵（等价于把语料当“真值”）。
2) Token-level KD：用 target 在 corpus prefix 下的 next-token 分布 p_T(·|x,y_<t) 做蒸馏；实现上只保留 top-8 token，把其余合并成第 9 类（降低蒸馏开销/噪声），对 drafter 的对应 9-way 分布做 KL/CE。
3) KD + survival gate：gate 只保留那些“在 greedy verification 下会被接受”的位置。直觉是 speculative decoding 的收益来自能被 verifier 接受的位置，因此把 loss 聚焦到这些位置可能更有效。

关键设计是把同一训练语料做四种 response 版本来隔离变量：
- external responses（原始语料，response 由别的模型/人写）
- greedy regenerated responses（用 target 贪心重写 response）
- 两个 matched-length regenerated 版本：因为 regeneration 往往更长，作者分别用 cut（截断到原长度）和 mask-loss（长度外不计 loss）来控制“长度变化”这个混杂因素。

机制解释围绕“标签一致性”展开：regeneration 后，语料 token 与 target greedy token 的一致率大幅上升；在一致的位置，CE 已经把 drafter 推向 target 的 mode，token-level KD 只能提供对非 argmax token 的那点概率质量，边际收益自然变小。对 survival gate 也是类似：当 response 本身就是 target greedy 轨迹时，“哪些位置会 survive”变得更平凡，gate 的区分度下降。e4:T76c,核心结论在多个控制变量下保持一致：
- 在 external responses 上，token-level distillation 和 survival gate 都能带来显著 acceptance 提升；
- 一旦换成 greedy regenerated responses，distillation 的增益大幅缩水，只剩小幅提升；gate 的增益基本消失（little or none）。
- 这种缩水不依赖于数据顺序、初始化、position weight、gate 形式、学习率、verifier、decoding temperature 等设置；控制实验会改变缩水幅度，但方向稳定。
- matched-length 控制显示：缩水不是简单由“regenerated 更长”导致。distillation 的缩水在 cut/mask 两种长度匹配下大多仍存在。
- gate 的一个细节：在 cut 版本里 gate 还能留下小增益，原因是 cut 会降低 ungated objectives 的 acceptance（截断改变了验证行为/分布），但 gated objective 受影响较小；而 mask-loss 不会改变生成序列本身，因此不产生这种相对优势。
- horizon study（训练时长扫描）：在 external responses 上，随着训练变长，CE 的 acceptance 掉得更快，导致 distillation 相对收益变大；但在各自“最佳训练长度”处，regenerated 上的 distillation 增益仍远小于 external。
- 跨数据/跨模态复现：第二个 vision corpus 复现同样缩水；text-only replication 更换 target/corpus/verifier，并加入 AR drafter，仍观察到 distillation 与 gate 的缩水（在 greedy 与 sampled decoding 下对 distillation 都成立；AR drafter 在 greedy 下也成立）。
- label control：把 external responses 的标签直接替换成 target greedy tokens，用 CE 训练就能拿到 distillation 的大部分收益，支持“增益主要来自把标签对齐到 target mode”这一解释。

论文摘要里没有给出具体 acceptance 数字表格；全文的重点是相对变化与稳健性，而不是单点 SOTA。e5:T486,They use a DFlash-style parallel block drafter: at anchor position a, the drafter conditions on frozen target hidden states up to a and predicts K=15 future tokens in one pass; up to 128 anchors per example; slot losses are exponentially downweighted by distance and normalized by retained weight.

Three objectives are compared:
1) Cross-entropy on corpus tokens.
2) Token-level distillation from the target next-token distribution under the corpus prefix, implemented as a 9-way distribution (top-8 tokens + merged tail) for efficiency.
3) The same KD but masked by a “survival gate” that keeps only positions whose preceding continuation would be accepted under greedy verification.

Crucially, they vary the response source while holding prompts/images fixed: original external responses vs greedy regenerated responses. Because regeneration changes average length, they add two length-matched regenerated variants (truncate vs mask loss beyond the original length) to disentangle length effects from label-source effects. A battery of controls (init, data order, position weights, gate variants, LR, verifier, decoding temperature) tests robustness.e6:T582,Main finding: KD and survival gating yield large acceptance gains on external responses, but greedy regeneration removes most of those gains—KD becomes a small improvement and the gate provides little to none. The direction holds across many controls.

Length controls show the shrinkage is not primarily due to regenerated responses being longer: most KD shrinkage remains under both truncation and loss-masking. The gate only retains a small gain under truncation because truncation hurts acceptance for ungated objectives more than for the gated one; loss-masking does not create that artifact.

A training-horizon sweep shows objective ranking depends on training length: on external responses, CE acceptance degrades more with longer training, making KD look increasingly better; yet at each objective’s best checkpoint, KD’s gain on regenerated responses is still far smaller than on external.

Replications: the effect appears on a second vision corpus and in a text-only setup with different target/corpus/verifier; KD shrinkage holds under greedy and sampled decoding, and also with an autoregressive drafter (under greedy).

A label-control supports the mechanism: replacing external labels with the target’s greedy tokens and training with CE recovers most of KD’s apparent gain, consistent with “benefit comes from aligning labels to the target mode,” which regeneration already does.e7:T79f,实验以“测量与归因”为主，不是追求刷分。设置：3 个开源模型（Qwen、Gemma、Kimi）× 3 个开源 harness（OpenClaw、ZeroClaw、OpenCode），5 个 answer-based benchmark；另对 Qwen、Gemma 做 2 个 interactive benchmark（用 verifier 在文件编辑/命令后判定）。对照是 Direct：不使用工具、每题一次输出。
关键观察（论文给了具体数字）：
- harness 可能“解出更多新题”但总体准确率更低：例如 Qwen 在 GPQA-Diamond 上，各 harness 比 Direct 多解出 8–13 道 Direct 没解出的题，但同时会额外错掉 18–36 道 Direct 能解的题。四个系统合并看，198 题里 175 题至少被解对过一次，而 Direct 只有 159/198。
- 仅看行为模式很难判断对错：相似的 tool-use 占比、连续检查、低 entropy 既出现在正确也出现在错误。对 HLE-Verifiable 的人工标注错误尝试里，OpenCode/ZeroClaw 的 repetition 标签分别约 36.8%/39.4%，但 budget-exhaustion 标签差异明显（13.0% vs 0%），提示不同 harness 的失败模式不同。
- tools/skills/memory 并不稳定带来收益：AIME 26 上（每题 4 attempts），Kimi/OpenCode 去掉工具描述与相关指令后，“正确 attempts 数”从 104 提到 116，但“至少解对一次的问题数”从 30 降到 29；skill loading 只在 16 组对比中的 2 组提升准确率；Qwen 在 AIME 26 上，用 AIME 25 收集并固定的 memory 对 OpenCode 有益、对 OpenClaw/ZeroClaw 反而有害。
- token 省一点可能换来大量正确数损失：Gemma/HLE-Verifiable 的共同任务上，OpenCode 输出 token 比 Direct 少 0.6%，但正确数 140 vs 164。若用“总输出 token / 正确答案数”衡量单位正确成本，平均上升 16.5%。OpenClaw 输出最高的 10% attempts 消耗了 62.2% 的输出 token，却没有一个正确答案，说明长轨迹常被浪费在重复/工具失败/错误推理上。e8:T4ba,AlphaDiana is a measurement system rather than a new agent method. The design centers on:
1) Session isolation with controlled reuse: sessions can be isolated or shared; file resets and memory retention are controlled separately. When shared memory is updated by attempts, executions are forced to be sequential and not automatically retried, since failures can change inherited state.
2) Harness-native adapters: instead of forcing a unified agent loop, adapters standardize task I/O while preserving each harness’s native model-call patterns, tool permissions, feedback loops, and context updates—keeping comparisons faithful to real harness behavior.
3) Evidence-linked artifacts: each attempt stores an outcome record (correctness, score_status, runtime errors) linked to normalized traces (roles, content, tool calls/results) and resource usage (tokens, runtime). Reports include failed/unscored attempts, and the system uses the latest record per requested evaluation so retries do not inflate the evaluation count.
The system is modular across datasets/agents/environments/scorers/analyzers, and supports matched interventions on tools/skills/memory while holding model/tasks/scoring/decoding fixed.e9:T723,The experiments emphasize measurement/attribution rather than leaderboard gains. Setup: three open-source models (Qwen, Gemma, Kimi) paired with three harnesses (OpenClaw, ZeroClaw, OpenCode) on five answer-based benchmarks; Qwen and Gemma also tested on two interactive benchmarks with verifiers after file edits/commands. Baseline is Direct: single response, no tools.
Key quantitative findings reported:
- Harnesses can solve additional questions yet reduce overall accuracy. For Qwen on GPQA-Diamond, each harness solves 8–13 questions that Direct misses, but fails on 18–36 that Direct solves. Across four systems, 175/198 questions are solved at least once vs. 159/198 for Direct.
- Behavioral patterns are not reliable correctness indicators: similar tool-use shares, consecutive checks, and low entropy appear in both correct and incorrect attempts. On annotated incorrect HLE-Verifiable attempts, repetition labels occur in ~36.8% (OpenCode) vs ~39.4% (ZeroClaw), while budget-exhaustion differs sharply (13.0% vs 0%), suggesting harness-specific failure modes.
- Tools/skills/memory are not consistently beneficial: on AIME 26 (4 attempts/problem), removing tool descriptions/instructions for Kimi/OpenCode increases correct attempts from 104 to 116 but reduces problems solved at least once from 30 to 29; skill loading improves accuracy in only 2/16 comparisons; fixed memory collected on AIME 25 helps OpenCode but hurts OpenClaw/ZeroClaw for Qwen on AIME 26.
- Small token savings can come with far fewer correct answers: on shared Gemma/HLE-Verifiable tasks, OpenCode uses 0.6% fewer output tokens than Direct but yields 140 correct vs 164. Total output tokens divided by #correct increases by 16.5%. For OpenClaw, the top 10% highest-token attempts consume 62.2% of output tokens without any correct answer.ea:T621,The paper introduces AgentPerturb, a two-dimensional perturbation framework. The first axis is perturbation target: user utterance (U), procedural specification (P), carried-over context (C), and tool contract (T). The second axis is perturbation type: Missing, Redundant, and Incorrect. This yields 12 perturbation families.

Two design choices are important. First, perturbations are single-target edits: only one channel is modified at a time while the others remain unchanged. This makes attribution cleaner and avoids confounding multiple failure sources. Second, perturbations are validated so that the original task goal is preserved, the environment remains executable, and a valid solution path still exists. So the benchmark is not broken; the agent is tested under controlled information corruption.

The framework is instantiated on APEX-Agents and Toolathlon, two long-horizon agent benchmarks with verifiable outcomes. The analysis is organized at three levels. Outcome-level analysis measures clean-to-perturbed performance drops. Factor-level analysis separates the effects of targets and types, and relates sensitivity to clean performance and task properties. Trajectory-level analysis audits reasoning traces, tool calls, observations, and state transitions to understand how perturbation-induced failures unfold. One of the most useful findings is that sensitivity clusters more strongly by perturbation target than by perturbation type. That suggests robustness interventions may need channel-specific treatment rather than generic noise injection.eb:T46d,The evaluation covers 10 frontier models on APEX-Agents and Toolathlon. The headline result is consistent: all perturbations reduce performance, but the dominant vulnerability depends on the environment. In other words, the most damaging target is not universal across benchmarks. The paper also performs a focused analysis on Hunyuan-3-High and shows that task success alone can hide substantial losses in token efficiency. Some agents still solve the task, but only after much longer and less efficient trajectories.

For mechanism analysis, the authors manually audit 30 cases where DeepSeek-V4-Flash succeeds on the clean task but fails after perturbation. The recurring pattern is that agents rarely question altered inputs and often propagate corrupted information without verification. Once a bad assumption is accepted early, it contaminates later planning, tool use, and state updates. The full numeric tables are not available in the provided excerpt, so it is safer not to restate exact per-model drops. The more important experimental value lies in the target/type decomposition and the trajectory-level failure patterns.ec:T815,RADAR 分三段：Repair / Adopt / Diagnose，并用平方损失（Brier/MSE）下的风险分解来组织。
1) 风险分解：在只允许对原始分数 P 做标量映射 s(P) 的前提下，把 repaired score 的风险拆成 outcome noise、score 隐藏的信息（即仅看 P 无法区分但对正确性可预测的子群差异）、以及 mapping error（标量映射可修的部分）。如果进一步限制映射必须保序（单调），还会引入 pooling gap（因为单调约束会把一些可分的点池化）。这一步的意义是：告诉你“校准做不好”到底是数据不够、还是接口本身丢信息。
2) Repair：提出 PAIC（Probe-Anchored Isotonic Calibration）。思路是：离线训练一个 correctness probe g(Z)（可用更丰富特征/更大模型/更贵计算），在目标域无标注 prompts 上跑 probe，得到 g 的预测；然后学习一个从原始分数 P 到新分数的单调映射，使其在 P 的各分段上尽量贴近 probe 的条件期望，从而实现无目标域标注的单调校准。它本质是“用 probe 作为锚点，把 richer predictor 蒸馏成 P 的单调函数”。论文强调 PAIC 的 excess risk 受控于 probe 的 score-conditional bias（在给定 P 的条件下 probe 的系统偏差）与拟合误差，而不是 probe 的整体准确率。
3) Adopt：指出“与不完美 probe 的一致性”可能会把候选分数排序搞错，因此需要一个带控制错误上线概率的比较规则。作者给出基于 held-out labels 的 paired risk comparison，并用 betting-based procedure 控制部署一个并未降低平方风险的候选的概率（类似 sequential testing / e-value 风格）。
4) Diagnose：修复后仍可能存在与特征对齐的残差结构（系统性错误子群）。难点是同一 prompt 的多次采样答案相关，不能当 i.i.d.。作者用 cross-prompt kernel products + prompt-level multiplier 的检验方式，在 sibling answers 相关的情况下仍保持有效性，用于发现“哪些特征簇上 residual 仍显著”。ed:T5c3,RADAR = Repair, Adopt, Diagnose, organized around squared loss (Brier/MSE).
1) Risk decomposition: the risk of a scalar-repaired score is decomposed into outcome noise, information hidden by the score (predictable residual structure not expressible as a function of the scalar), and mapping error (the only part scalar recalibration can fix). If the repair is constrained to be order-preserving (monotone), an additional pooling gap can appear due to forced aggregation.
2) Repair via PAIC (Probe-Anchored Isotonic Calibration): train an external correctness probe g(Z) using richer features/compute. On unlabeled target prompts, run the probe and fit a monotone function of the original score P that matches the probe’s score-conditional behavior. Conceptually, it distills a richer predictor into a deployable monotone map of P. The theory emphasizes that excess risk depends on the probe’s score-conditional bias (given P), not its overall accuracy.
3) Adopt: agreement with an imperfect probe can mis-rank candidate scores, so the paper proposes a paired risk comparison using held-out labels and a betting-based procedure that controls the probability of deploying a candidate that does not actually reduce squared risk.
4) Diagnose: introduces a feature-aware residual audit that remains valid when multiple sampled answers per prompt are dependent, using cross-prompt kernel products and a prompt-level multiplier procedure to detect systematic residual structure.ee:T775,The study is built as a controlled factorial experiment. Rating scales vary along three axes: format (continuous vs. ordinal), range (3, 5, 11, 21 points), and sign (signed around zero vs. unsigned non-negative). This yields 16 scale conditions. The evaluation spans three human-labeled tasks with different semantics: political leaning, sentiment, and toxicity. Models include both proprietary and open systems, namely GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen, and GLM. Prompting is tested in two forms: zero-shot and rubric-based. In the rubric setting, the construct is decomposed into dimensions and the model scores each dimension before producing a final holistic score; only the final score is analyzed so the two prompting modes remain comparable.

A strong part of the paper is how sensitivity is operationalized. The authors normalize scores across scales and compare only pairs of conditions that differ in exactly one design factor. That isolates the effect of format, range, and sign instead of conflating them. They then define semantic sensitivity by mapping scores into interpretable categories and checking whether category assignments change. This is the right level of analysis for many downstream uses, because researchers often care less about a small numeric shift than about whether a text is now judged neutral vs. positive, or low-toxicity vs. high-toxicity.

One notable result from the full paper is that rubric-based prompting does not materially reduce sensitivity. That matters because a common intuition is that more structured prompting should stabilize the model’s internal scale. The results suggest otherwise. Another important observation is that signed vs. unsigned scales have especially large effects, which implies the model is not simply forming a stable latent score and linearly projecting it onto different scales. The prompt-defined axis itself changes the decision geometry.ef:T4df,The headline results are compact and useful: changing a single scale design element shifts normalized scores by about 0.10 on average, and roughly one in five texts changes semantic category. That is large enough to affect threshold-based analyses, group comparisons, and correlational studies.

Task-wise, toxicity is the most sensitive setting, especially to the sign of the scale. That makes sense: toxicity is often framed as one-sided severity, so a signed scale introduces a different semantic structure than an unsigned severity scale. Sentiment and political leaning also show sensitivity, but less sharply.

Model-wise, the effect is not confined to one vendor or one model family. It appears across multiple systems. Prompt-wise, rubric prompting does not consistently outperform zero-shot in stability, which directly challenges a common engineering assumption that more explicit rubrics automatically fix comparability issues.

From the available full-text sections, the key quantitative facts are clear even without every table value: 16 scale conditions, 3 tasks, 2 prompting strategies, 5 models, with the main effect sizes being about 0.10 normalized score drift and about 20% category flips. Those are the numbers worth retaining.f0:T409,Harness-Delta Attribution (HDA) decomposes the performance difference between (M, H0) and (M, Ĥ) into:
1) Artifact-driven overfitting: estimate a detectable lower bound by evaluating an artifact-neutralized version of the evolved harness, where shortcut-exploiting components (hardcoded patterns, dataset-format hacks) are removed or disabled.
2) Test-time scaling: construct a compute-matched baseline harness that uses the same inference-time budget as the evolved harness (e.g., number of samples, voting/reranking, tool-call budget), and measure how much of the gain is reproducible purely by spending more compute.
3) Residual: the remaining improvement after subtracting (1) and (2), interpreted as an upper bound on generalizable harness improvement (upper bound because some overfitting may remain undetected).

A key point is that held-out evaluation alone can still overstate generalization when search/test splits share benchmark artifacts; HDA adds compute matching and artifact neutralization as orthogonal diagnostics.f1:T551,The key move is to decompose identifier hints into two orthogonal design choices. Identifier selection decides which program entities are revealed: edited files, new functions, classes, attributes, and so on. Identifier projection decides how much of each selected entity is exposed: name, signature, location, semantic description, behavioral guidance, etc. Existing benchmark hint schemes often entangle these choices, making comparisons hard to interpret.

Within this framework, the paper proposes DefUse for selection and Declaration for projection. DefUse targets identifiers that sit on the interaction boundary between implementation and tests, rather than disclosing every new component in the reference solution. This is a narrower objective: remove hidden interface mismatch, not reveal internal design. Declaration then exposes declaration-level attributes of those entities, such as names, signatures, and locations, while avoiding semantic descriptions or implementation hints that would move closer to the reference design.

The paper also introduces an LLM-based assessment layer to score whether a hint attribute is necessary for task resolution, whether it discloses reference-solution information, and whether it guides behavior beyond interface clarification. That judge is used as a complement to execution-based success, not a replacement.f2:T42f,The experiments span five repository-level coding benchmarks across Python and Java, evaluated with three language models. The paper’s emphasis is not on a single best score, but on controlled comparisons between selection policies and projection policies.

The main empirical finding is that higher solve rates can coincide with greater disclosure of implementation choices. In other words, some hint schemes improve benchmark performance not merely by removing unfair ambiguity, but by leaking parts of the solution. The controlled setup shows that both axes matter: which identifiers are selected and which attributes of those identifiers are projected can each materially change measured task resolution.

Attribute ablations further separate the effects of names, signatures, locations, and semantic descriptions. On SWE-bench Pro, the LLM-based analysis is used to distinguish necessary interface information from spoiler-like content. The practical takeaway is that benchmark quality cannot be judged from pass rate alone; it needs a disclosure analysis as well.f3:T534,The methodology is a controlled ablation where the MCP gateway is the primary independent variable.

The authors introduce JUPE, a VQA-style benchmark where each item fixes the image, question, candidate answer, and correctness label, while varying only the explanation condition. This isolates the causal effect of explanation text on judgment. That matters because a judge can become more accepting of both correct and incorrect answers, leaving overall accuracy nearly unchanged while substantially weakening wrong-answer rejection.f8:T5d0,The evaluation covers 14 MLLM judges from 5 model families. The main finding is consistent: ordinary plausible explanations are enough to materially reduce rejection of incorrect answers. On average, plain justifications reduce the rejection rate of wrong answers by 12.7 percentage points, chain-of-thought explanations by 13.8 points, and explicitly persuasive explanations by 12.5 points. The similarity across these conditions is important because it shows the problem does not require specialized persuasion attacks; normal-looking explanations already trigger it. A stronger result is that among wrong answers judged definitely incorrect without explanations, 36% to 39% become accepted once a plausible explanation is added. In other words, the judges are not becoming better at reading the image; they are becoming more willing to trust the answer. During evaluation, an LLM interlocutor interactively advances the conversation by uniformly sampling situations from a predefined action space. This is the main design choice. Instead of waiting for rare situations to appear naturally, the benchmark forces balanced coverage over the situation space.

A context-aware LLM judge then evaluates each agent response only against the subset of rules that apply at that turn. The output is therefore rule-wise and turn-wise, not a single opaque score for the whole dialogue. To improve judge reliability, the authors validate the judge on human-verified synthetic golden dialogues before using it in the benchmark.

That is sensible for open-ended dialogue, where many responses can be acceptable if they satisfy the right constraints.fa:T8c5,方法核心是 Bounded Continuation Analysis（BCA）。作者把给定 prompt 下的自回归生成过程近似成一个有界的随机过程：从初始前缀出发，逐步展开一个 bounded continuation tree，只保留有限深度、且在概率上足够重要的续写路径。树上的节点是 token prefix，边对应下一 token 的条件概率。由于完整枚举整个输出空间不可行，BCA 只在有限 horizon 内构造高概率子树，再把终止续写交给语义 harm evaluator 打标签，判断该续写是否构成有害响应。随后，作者计算在这个有界树中“最终到达有害终端”的总概率，称为 bounded harm reachability。

这个设计有几个关键点。第一，它不是把 harm 判定放在 token 级，而是放在语义级终端续写上，这样能避免局部 token 模式和真实有害行为之间的错位。第二，它显式利用了自回归模型的条件概率，因此得到的是一个 reachability probability，而不是 judge 打分的启发式分数。第三，它把问题表述成 probabilistic model checking 里的 reachability 问题，用离散时间马尔可夫链和 PCTL 风格的“eventually reach harmful state”来组织计算，这让指标定义比较干净。

在固定 prompt 之外，作者还定义了 GAS（generative attack susceptibility），把自适应攻击预算映射到一个概率值：在攻击者迄今找到的所有 prompt 中，哪一个 prompt 的 bounded harm reachability 最高。这个定义适合黑盒 adaptive jailbreak search。实验里主要结合 PAIR 和 TAP 两类搜索：前者是顺序式 prompt refinement，后者是带分支和剪枝的搜索。作者还讨论了把 BCA 作为搜索信号，与传统 judge-guided 搜索并行使用，从而覆盖不同失败模式。

从方法取舍看，作者没有试图估计“全空间真实 harmful probability”，而是退到 bounded、high-probability tree 上做近似。这是合理的，因为完整分布不可算，且安全评测更关心攻击者在有限生成预算内能否触达有害区域。代价是结果依赖 horizon、树展开策略和 evaluator 质量；作者也承认 BCA 是一个 bounded proxy，而不是精确的全分布积分。fb:T84b,The core method is Bounded Continuation Analysis (BCA). For a given prompt, the model’s autoregressive generation process is approximated as a bounded stochastic process over token prefixes. Starting from the prompt, BCA expands a bounded continuation tree up to a finite horizon, keeping only continuations that are sufficiently probable. Nodes are token prefixes, edges are next-token conditional probabilities, and terminal continuations are labeled as harmful or safe by a semantic harm evaluator. BCA then computes the probability of eventually reaching a harmful terminal within this bounded tree, which the paper calls bounded harm reachability.

Several design choices matter. First, harm is evaluated semantically at terminal continuations rather than by token-level heuristics, which better matches the actual safety question. Second, the score is probability-aware: it uses the model’s conditional distribution instead of only sampled outputs. Third, the formulation is grounded in probabilistic model checking, using a discrete-time Markov chain view and a reachability-style property analogous to “eventually reach a harmful state.” That gives the metric a clean formal interpretation.

The paper extends fixed-prompt analysis to adaptive attacks via Generative Attack Susceptibility (GAS). GAS maps an attack budget to the maximum bounded harm reachability among all prompts discovered so far by the attacker. This is evaluated with two black-box adaptive jailbreak methods, PAIR and TAP, which represent different search structures. The paper also studies using BCA itself as a search signal, alongside standard judge-guided search.

An important practical choice is that the method does not attempt to estimate the full harmful probability over the entire output space. Instead, it works on a bounded, high-probability continuation tree. That is a reasonable compromise: exact full-distribution computation is intractable, and finite-horizon reachability is closer to the operational threat model. The trade-off is that results depend on the horizon, tree-construction policy, and evaluator quality.fc:T640,The main empirical findings come in three parts. First, across several open-source instruction-tuned models with 0% greedy ASR on JailbreakBench, BCA still reveals nearly two orders of magnitude variation in hidden harmful mass. This is the central empirical point: identical refusal outcomes can hide very different levels of latent vulnerability.

Second, BCA correlates with realized attack outcomes under repeated sampling. For each behavior-template pair, the authors sample 100 completions from the target model and compute empirical ASR using HarmBench-Mistral-7B as the harm classifier. BCA’s reachability score tracks which prompts are more likely to yield harmful outputs under repeated sampling, suggesting that it captures something operationally meaningful rather than merely redefining the metric.

Third, in adaptive red-teaming, BCA-guided search and judge-guided search are complementary. Running them in parallel increases jailbreak coverage relative to either one alone. This indicates that the two signals explore different regions of prompt space: judge-guided search chases already realized harmful outputs, while BCA-guided search can prioritize prompts whose local continuation distribution still contains substantial harmful mass even if a harmful sample has not yet been observed.

From a foundation-model perspective, the most useful takeaway is the “0% greedy ASR but nontrivial hidden harmful mass” phenomenon. - Setup: each case provides field values; the agent selects one of four ordered actions (increasing intervention strength).
- Latent rule: a subset of fields (factors) with directional effects determines a score s∈[-1,1]; a fixed utility function maps s to action utilities, enabling calibrated evaluation.
- Rule families: additive, conjunctive, disjunctive, and lexicographic dynamics, yielding diverse but controlled hypothesis structures.
- Protocol: in the default setting, the agent decides when/what/how many queries to make to gather evidence. Rule drift occurs without announcement during interaction.
- Sequential batching: evaluation cases are presented in small batches so agents can notice drift either via further probing or via degraded performance, producing an in-process performance curve.
- Scalable synthesis: an LLM-assisted pipeline generates a field catalog (semantics, ranges, sampling distributions) plus cross-field feasibility constraints and dynamics constraints.104:T4d6,There are three main design choices. First, the benchmark builds three diagnostic settings that expose different failure modes. Parallel evidence requires preserving two parallel reasoning chains for ambiguous references. Conditional evidence requires keeping both the supporting statement and its qualifier, so the compressor cannot turn a conditional claim into an unconditional one. Imbalanced evidence tests whether minority-supported perspectives survive when most evidence points elsewhere. Second, for each query, the required evidence is extracted from the source context and decomposed into minimal self-contained propositions. Evaluation is then done proposition by proposition, based on whether each one is explicitly stated or unambiguously inferable from the compressed context alone. Third, the paper introduces All Proposition Recall (All-Rec), which only counts a case as correct if every required proposition is preserved. This is intentionally stricter than average proposition recall, because many reasoning failures are caused by a single missing piece. They also define Evidence Preservation Return (EPR), the ratio of overall All-Rec to average inference TFLOPs, to compare preservation quality against compute cost.105:T546,KEEP-Bench contains 4,102 instances across the three evidence structures. The authors select 100 harmful request cores from published benchmarks and wrap each with 9 published attack families, yielding 900 attacked prompts. Two target models answer the same prompts under identical settings, producing corpus A and corpus B from Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and gemma-3-12b-it. Eight graders then label every response with the same four-way rubric: refuse, evasive, comply, or gibberish. Gemini-2.5-flash is used as a reference grader, but explicitly not as ground truth.

The key analytical move is to decompose the usual jailbreak success rate into two quantities. One is the refusal boundary: whether the model declined the request at all. The other is the compliance rate: among responses that are not refusals, how often the model actually delivers the harmful request. Across graders, the refusal boundary mostly shifts by a moderate number of points. The compliance rate, however, can change by multiplicative factors because some graders systematically relabel compliant outputs as evasive. The paper then validates this behavior on held-out graders, new harmful requests, and a third target-family model.

A second important contribution is diagnostic rather than algorithmic. Aggregate agreement can hide the problem because easy refusals dominate the corpus. A collapsing grader can still show high overall agreement with the reference. Per-class label counts expose the failure immediately, without human labels and without extra calls.
