1) The model is prompted to output a bounding box token span (<box> x1,y1,x2,y2 </box>) before producing rationale/answer—no external detector head.
2) After prefilling, visual patch tokens already reside in per-layer KV caches. Given the predicted box, LoRe maps it to the corresponding patch indices and amplifies their KV-cache entries, so subsequent autoregressive decoding attends more strongly to that region. This makes the newly identified evidence influence the current reasoning trajectory without generating extra visual tokens or waiting for a tool-returned crop.
3) RL training encourages selecting regions that support the final answer, effectively learning when/where to look while benefiting from the cache reweighting immediately.
Key distinction vs tool-based “thinking with images”: LoRe internalizes the visual operation as cache-level reweighting, avoiding multi-turn latency and token overhead, and removing the temporal mismatch where evidence only becomes available in the next turn.152:Ta4a,实验部分信息量很大，建议按四组预训练研究和两组主结果来看。预训练研究一：生成范式比较。作者在共享 guidance scale 下比较了连续文本生成与 token-based 文本生成。JUICE 在 GenEval 上达到 48.41，一个只做文生图的专用模型是 47.86，而三种把文本写成 token 的统一框架都低于后者。这说明在这个设定里，把文本也放进连续 encoder space 并没有拖累图像生成，反而更适合统一建模。captioning 方面，连续状态生成在措辞精确度上略弱，但图文匹配度与 AR caption 相当。预训练研究二：训练任务混合。joint denoising 与 conditional denoising 组合优于任何单独训练方式，而且收益不只是因为监督目标更多，而是因为训练分布更贴近采样分布。这个结论对 flow/diffusion 类统一模型很重要。预训练研究三：表示空间。虽然 VAE latent 的重建质量更高，但无论生成还是 captioning，语义编码器空间都更好；文本侧 Flan-T5 states 优于更大的 embedding 模型，说明“更大更通用的文本嵌入”不自动等于“更好的生成目标”。预训练研究四：缩放。backbone 从 179M 扩到 2.1B 时，SigLIP2 因为与语言对齐更好，在所有规模上 captioning 都更强；DINO 在小模型上的图像生成优势随着规模增大而消失，说明视觉空间选择与模型容量存在交互。主结果部分，作者训练了两个 2.1B JUICE 模型，分别配 Flan-T5 + SigLIP2 和 Flan-T5 + DINO，分辨率 224×224，从零开始训练，不依赖预训练 LLM。两者在 GenEval 上分别达到 0.87 和 0.88；SigLIP2 版本在 DPG-Bench 上 85.22，在 WISE 上 0.45，在 VQAv2 上 73.1。虽然不同 benchmark 的计分口径与前文预训练实验中的 48.41/47.86 不完全一致，但整体结论清楚：单套权重可以同时覆盖 compositional generation、需要世界知识的 generation、以及 VQA。最有辨识度的是规划实验。多解迷宫任务中，如果图像路径和文字步骤独立采样，二者经常各自正确但彼此不一致，joint success 只有 54.6%。若改成顺序生成，先图后文可到 95.2%，先文后图是 85.3%，但性能依赖人为选顺序。coupled sampling 达到 93.7%，接近最好顺序方案，同时不需要预先决定哪一模态先生成。视觉空间规划任务上，训练尺度内成功率 99.8%，外推到更大地图仍有 94% 和 69%。这些结果支持作者的主张：联合分布模型在需要跨模态一致性的任务上，确实比独立或固定顺序生成更自然。153:T410,The paper tackles a more fundamental question than standard text-to-image generation: can image and text be modeled by a single generative process, trained jointly from scratch, instead of using the usual asymmetric design where an LLM generates text and a diffusion or flow head generates images? Existing unified multimodal systems typically suffer from two structural constraints. They either use different generation mechanisms for different modalities, or they quantize one modality to fit the other. They also factorize outputs in a fixed order, so the first modality cannot adapt once the second starts to form. JUICE asks whether both modalities can instead live in a shared continuous target space provided by frozen pretrained encoders, and whether a single flow-matching backbone can learn the joint distribution over those representations. If that works, conditional generation, bidirectional generation, and truly coupled image-text generation all become different inference paths inside one model rather than separate systems.154:T4f1,Its importance for pretraining is threefold. First, it reframes unified multimodal modeling as a pretraining objective and representation design problem, not just a systems integration problem. The key move is to generate both image and text in continuous semantic spaces, which removes the need to anchor the whole system around a pretrained autoregressive language model. Second, the paper provides a fairly complete study of the design space that practitioners usually handle heuristically: whether text should remain tokenized or be generated continuously, which denoising regions must be covered during training, whether reconstruction-oriented spaces or semantic encoder spaces are better targets, and how these choices behave under scaling. Third, it gives evidence that joint distribution modeling yields a capability that is not captured well by standard multimodal benchmarks. The coupled-sampling planning results show that the model can let image and text revise each other during generation. That is a stronger claim than simply saying one set of weights can solve multiple tasks. At 2.1B parameters, trained from scratch, with one backbone covering text-to-image, captioning, VQA, and joint generation, this is already beyond a small proof-of-concept.155:T8e9,JUICE has three main ingredients. The first is the choice of target representation spaces. Instead of generating pixels or discrete tokens directly, both modalities are mapped into frozen pretrained encoder spaces. On the vision side, the paper compares SigLIP2, WebSSL-DINO, and VAE latents. On the text side, it compares Flan-T5 encoder states against larger text embedding models. The central insight is that the best generative target is not necessarily the one with the best reconstruction fidelity; it is the one whose geometry is semantically structured and amenable to denoising dynamics. The experiments eventually favor semantic spaces over VAE latents, and Flan-T5 states over larger embedding models. The second ingredient is the unified backbone, MM-RiT, a flow-matching Transformer trained from scratch. Image and text streams interact through bidirectional joint attention. Unlike autoregressive models, it does not generate one token at a time in a fixed order. Unlike standard conditional diffusion T2I systems, it is not a one-way generator from text to image. Instead, it takes noisy representations from both modalities and learns the velocity field that maps noise to data. Each modality has its own noise variable and schedule, so the task space becomes a two-dimensional square indexed by image noise and text noise. The edges correspond to conditional tasks: clean text plus noisy image gives text-to-image; clean image plus noisy text gives captioning or VQA. Interior points correspond to joint denoising, where both modalities emerge together. The third ingredient is the training mixture and inference-path view. The model is trained on both conditional denoising and joint denoising, not just one of them. The reason is simple and important: training should cover the regions that inference trajectories will visit. At test time, each task is defined as a path through the 2D noise square. Coupled sampling lets image and text continuously condition on each other as they co-evolve. Relative to prior unified models, the novelty is not merely continuous text generation. It is the fact that both modalities are placed under the same generative grammar: one backbone, one flow objective, one context mechanism, and one joint-distribution interpretation.156:Ta80,The experimental section is rich and should be read in two layers: the pretraining studies and the final model results. In the first pretraining study, the paper compares generative frameworks. At a matched guidance scale, JUICE reaches 48.41 on GenEval, while a model trained only for text-to-image reaches 47.86, and all three unified frameworks that generate text as tokens fall below that specialized baseline. This is an important result: making text continuous does not hurt image generation in this setup and appears to help unified modeling. For captioning, continuous-state generation loses some exact wording but remains competitive in image-text matching relative to autoregressive captions. The second study examines training-task mixtures. Combining joint denoising with conditional denoising beats either alone, and the gain is not just due to supervising more targets. It comes from better train-test coverage of the denoising regions visited during sampling. The third study looks at representation spaces. VAE latents reconstruct better, but semantic encoder spaces work better for both generation and captioning. On the text side, Flan-T5 states outperform larger embedding models, which is a useful reminder that larger generic text embeddings are not automatically better generative targets. The fourth study analyzes scaling. As the backbone grows from 179M to 2.1B parameters, SigLIP2 consistently gives better captioning because it is better aligned with language, while DINO’s early advantage on image generation fades with scale. This suggests a nontrivial interaction between representation space and model capacity. For the final models, the authors train two 2.1B JUICE variants at 224×224 resolution, both from scratch and without a pretrained language model: Flan-T5 plus SigLIP2, and Flan-T5 plus DINO. They report 0.87 and 0.88 on GenEval respectively. The SigLIP2 model reaches 85.22 on DPG-Bench, 0.45 on WISE, and 73.1 on VQAv2. The most distinctive evidence comes from the planning tasks. In multi-solution mazes, independently sampled image and text outputs are often individually valid but mutually inconsistent, giving only 54.6% joint success. Sequential generation repairs this, but performance depends on the chosen order: 95.2% when image comes first, 85.3% when text comes first. Coupled sampling reaches 93.7% without requiring that order choice. On visual spatial planning, the model solves 99.8% of maps at training sizes and generalizes to larger unseen maps with 94% and 69% success. These results support the paper’s main claim that explicit joint modeling is especially useful when cross-modal consistency matters during generation.157:T678,This one deserves a careful read. Start with the method section that defines the two-dimensional noise square and the notion of task paths through it. That is the conceptual center of the paper. Make sure to understand how text-to-image, captioning, VQA, and joint generation all become instances of the same flow-matching problem, and why separate noise scales are needed for the two modalities. Next, spend time on the pretraining ablations. The four design questions are the real methodological contribution: continuous text versus token text, conditional versus joint denoising mixtures, representation-space choice, and scaling behavior. These are not cosmetic ablations. They are the paper’s attempt to stabilize a new modeling recipe. Pay attention to which conclusions hold only at small scale and which survive scaling. Then read the coupled-sampling planning section closely, especially the qualitative trajectories showing that the modality that settles later can revise itself to match the other. That is the clearest evidence for why joint generation is different from fixed-order generation. A few deeper questions are worth keeping in mind while reading: why continuous text states preserve semantic adequacy but lose exact wording; whether frozen encoder spaces hard-code upstream representational biases into the generator; and how far this recipe is from higher resolution, longer text, and more interactive multimodal settings. If time is limited, read the introduction, the main method figure, the four pretraining studies, and the planning experiments first. That should take about 60 to 90 minutes and capture the main contribution.158:T48f,ALPS uses a two-stage recipe. Stage 1 trains a ViT-B/16 from scratch with fixed sinusoidal positional embeddings and raw final-layer patch tokens. The same tokens are supervised by four objectives: image-text contrastive learning, autoregressive captioning, pixel reconstruction, and dense correspondence. The contrastive loss uses both web captions and sentences sampled from longer synthetic captions, with separate softmaxes so that captions for the same image are not treated as negatives. The caption decoder predicts the full synthetic caption from image tokens and previous text. A lightweight convolutional decoder reconstructs images from clean and noisy tokens with L1, SSIM, and image-gradient losses. Dense correspondence adds local spatial supervision across crops and scales. Stage 2 then performs cross-view self-distillation: a student sees an augmented view and predicts frozen Stage-1 teacher patch tokens at corresponding locations in a clean view. The staged design matters because it strengthens state information after a joint multimodal foundation has been established, instead of retrofitting a CLIP-like encoder and losing language alignment.159:T48d,Routing Policy Optimization (RPO) reframes attention visibility as the exploration action.
1) Action definition (routing): visual tokens are grouped into spatial blocks. At a small set of denoising timesteps, each query block either keeps dense attention or samples additional key blocks according to the model’s native dense attention mass, producing a sparse attention route (mask).
2) Likelihood for score-function updates: routing changes the predicted velocity field v_θ(x^t,t,c). The method assigns a Gaussian likelihood to the routed velocity around the dense velocity, yielding a differentiable surrogate that scores routed transitions while updating the dense velocity network parameters.
3) Controlled two-rollout estimator: two trajectories share all non-routing sources of variation and differ only in sampled routes; the signed reward difference provides a leave-one-out advantage, reducing variance. Route proposal is non-differentiable (no gradient through the sampling pass); gradients flow through the likelihood term into the dense model. At inference, routing masks are removed and the original dense attention + deterministic sampler is used.15a:T4a7,JAVIS builds on Fun-Audio-Chat. The shared LLM runs at 5 Hz, while the speech refined head runs at 25 Hz. Instead of animating a face after waveform synthesis, the authors adapt the speech refined head with LoRA and turn it into a Joint Refined Head. Each 5 Hz LLM output is expanded into five conditioning vectors. The JRH autoregressively processes these vectors together with the embedding of the previous speech token, producing five hidden states for the current chunk. These states form the unified representation H_t. Two streaming branches consume H_t: the speech branch uses a frozen CosyVoice 3 speech decoder and vocoder to synthesize audio, while the motion branch uses an autoregressive Motion Decoder to generate continuous facial-motion chunks, which are rendered with a reference portrait. During training, the shared LLM is frozen, while the LoRA-adapted JRH and Motion Decoder are trained with both speech cross-entropy loss and motion loss. Compared with X-Streamer and Ex-Omni-2D, JAVIS avoids iterative generation of high-dimensional video latents and instead predicts compact motion controls before rendering, which is better aligned with streaming latency constraints.15b:T99c,系统由两部分组成：一个从零预训练的 5B single-stream DiT 生成器，以及一个 intention-aware 的 prompt enhancement 模块。生成器部分的关键设计是把自然语言描述和显式布局规范放进同一条文本条件通路，而不是分成独立的 layout encoder 和 text encoder。这样做的好处是接口统一，模型既能吃普通 prompt，也能吃结构化布局文本；代价是训练时必须让模型学会把不同粒度、不同结构的条件都映射到同一个条件空间。作者为此设计了三类 recipe：

第一，broad data retention。报告强调不是过度清洗到只剩高美学图像，而是保留更广泛的数据分布，尤其是包含文本、版式、界面、海报、信息卡片等复杂图形样本。对于信息密集型生成，过强的审美筛选会损失真正需要的训练信号。

第二，multi-granularity and structure-aware textual supervision。模型不仅看普通 caption，还看更细粒度、更结构化的文本监督，包括长文本内容、局部元素描述、空间关系、布局约束等。这里的核心不是简单增加 token 数，而是让监督信号覆盖“画什么”和“放哪里”两类信息。论文特别强调 unified text-conditioning pathway，因此结构化布局最终也是以文本形式表达给 DiT，而不是额外的几何控制分支。

第三，progressive-resolution training。为了兼顾全局布局和局部文字可读性，训练采用渐进式分辨率策略。低分辨率阶段先学整体构图和条件对齐，高分辨率阶段再强化文字边缘、细节和局部排版。对于长文本渲染，这比一开始就全分辨率训练更稳，也更省资源。

系统前端的 PE 模块不是简单 prompt rewrite。它会根据任务类型路由到不同的 guidance 流程，必要时检索知识和视觉参考，再生成详细的内容与布局规范。关键点在于它输出的布局描述与 DiT 训练时使用的条件接口兼容，因此不是“用自然语言尽量说清楚”，而是“产出模型真正学过的可执行规范”。这也是它和通用 generator-agnostic prompt agent 的主要区别。

如果从方法定位看，这篇工作更像“预训练 backbone + specification layer + benchmark”的系统工程。真正值得看的是作者如何把 layout control 作为预训练条件建模问题来处理，而不是只靠后处理或外接控制网络。15c:T7f6,MOSS-Image consists of a pretrained 5B single-stream diffusion transformer and an intention-aware prompt enhancement module. The generator is designed around a unified text-conditioning pathway: ordinary natural-language prompts and explicit layout specifications are both fed through the same textual interface, instead of using separate text and layout encoders. This keeps the interface simple and flexible, but it also requires the model to learn from supervision at different levels of structure and granularity.

The pretraining recipe has three notable components. First, broad data retention. The report argues against overly aggressive aesthetic filtering, because information-dense graphics, UI-like images, posters, and text-heavy visuals contain the exact signals needed for long-text rendering and layout following. Second, multi-granularity and structure-aware textual supervision. The model is trained not only on generic captions but also on finer and more structured textual signals that describe content, local elements, spatial relations, and layout constraints. The point is not merely to add more text tokens, but to cover both semantic content and placement instructions. Third, progressive-resolution training. Lower resolutions help the model learn global composition and alignment first, while later higher-resolution stages improve text legibility and local layout fidelity. For long-text rendering, this curriculum is more stable and more compute-efficient than training at full resolution from the start.

The prompt enhancement module is more than prompt rewriting. It routes requests to task-specific guidance, retrieves knowledge and visual references when needed, and outputs detailed content and layout specifications that are compatible with the generator’s training interface. That compatibility matters: the enhancer is not just making prompts longer, it is producing conditions in a form the backbone has actually learned to follow. This is the main difference from generator-agnostic prompt agents.15d:T73a,The evaluation is split between backbone rendering ability and end-to-end system performance. For rendering, the authors introduce LongLongTextBench, focused on long-form English and Chinese text generation. On this benchmark, MOSS-Image reaches a Mean-6 score of 96.3, outperforming Qwen Image 2512 at 64.9 by 31.4 points. That result supports the effectiveness of the pretraining recipe, especially the long-text supervision and progressive-resolution schedule.

For end-to-end generation, the paper introduces RealLayoutArena, which evaluates complex graphic generation from short design requests using blind pairwise human comparisons. The judgment combines instruction following, content completeness, text readability, and visual organization. MOSS-Image obtains 1698.70 Elo, ranking second overall behind GPT Image 2 and ahead of Seedream 5.0 Pro. This suggests that prompt/specification quality is a major bottleneck, but also that the backbone itself is strong once given high-quality executable conditions.

- Image tokenizer: trained from scratch on GPIC images, Cosmos-Tokenizer-style encoder–decoder with FSQ; 8× spatial downsampling; 256×256 becomes a 32×32 grid (1024 tokens); codebook size 64k.
- Text tokenizer: scratch-trained byte-level BPE with vocab 16,384, trained on GPIC captions plus OpenWebText for coverage (tokenizer training, not LM pretraining).
- Joint vocabulary: 16,384 text + 64,000 image + 256 special = 80,640, with shared embedding and output head.
- Sequence formats: Text-only, Image-only, Image-to-Text (I2T), and Text-to-Image (T2I). T2I uses caption prefix conditioning to generate image tokens.

- Objective: weighted next-token cross-entropy with separate text/image terms and an image-loss weight λ_img, normalized by non-padding tokens.
- Controlled study: under a fixed pretraining budget, vary the mixture and schedule of text-only vs T2I vs I2T to measure their effect on T2I quality.15f:T799,方法核心是 Heterogeneous Action Interface, HAI，由两部分组成。其一是 Schema-Guided Action Adaptation，用来解决异构动作空间的语义对齐。作者不把动作向量当成无语义的数值数组，而是把每个控制维度转成由 schema 定义的 semantic token，再把该维度在当前时刻的精确数值通过 affine modulation 注入。这样做等于把“控制含义”与“同步数值”解耦：语义部分可跨任务共享，数值部分保留执行精度。相比直接拼接 raw action vector，这种做法不依赖固定维度顺序，也更容易迁移到离散+连续混合控制空间。

其二是 Agent-Aware Spatial Modulation，用来解决多 agent 的动作归属。作者从 agent description 派生 agent-specific spatial gate，让每个 agent 分支只选择性更新与目标实体相关的视觉 token，并且只接收对应动作流的条件。这里的关键不是简单加一个 agent embedding，而是在共享视觉特征空间里显式做空间门控，减少多个动作流在同一 latent 上互相污染。论文强调不需要在推理时额外提供 boxes、poses、masks 或 reference image，这说明它希望把 stream-to-entity binding 内化到模型条件接口里。

在训练与部署衔接上，作者先有一个 bidirectional video teacher，再把完整 HAI 保留下来，迁移到 blockwise causal generator。迁移过程结合了 autoregressive tuning 的 teacher forcing 和面向 streaming video 的 distribution matching distillation。为了解决动作与压缩视频 latent 的时间对齐，文中还引入 causal temporal alignment 和 global latent offset，使缓存 rollout 时动作窗口能同步前移。另一个工程上稳妥的设计是 residual 通过 zero-initialized projection 注入，避免新控制分支在初始化时破坏已有视觉先验。这一点和很多 adapter / control 注入方法的稳定化思路一致。160:T677,The method is built around a Heterogeneous Action Interface (HAI). One component, Schema-Guided Action Adaptation, addresses heterogeneous control spaces. Instead of feeding raw action vectors directly, each control dimension is converted into a semantic token defined by its schema, while the synchronized numeric value is injected through affine modulation. This decouples semantic meaning from task-specific vector layouts. The design is motivated by the fact that the same tensor dimension can mean entirely different things across environments, so raw vectors are a poor shared interface.

The second component, Agent-Aware Spatial Modulation, addresses stream-to-agent binding. From an agent description, the model derives an agent-specific spatial gate that selectively updates visual tokens associated with the intended entity. Each branch attends only to its corresponding action stream. The point is to prevent action leakage across agents in a shared latent space, especially when entities overlap, look similar, or interact closely.

For efficient rollout, the paper keeps the full HAI while transferring a bidirectional video teacher to a blockwise causal generator. This uses teacher forcing for AR tuning and distribution matching distillation for streaming video. The paper also introduces causal temporal alignment between raw actions and compressed video latents, plus a global latent offset so action windows advance consistently with cached rollout. Residual control signals are injected through zero-initialized projections, which helps preserve the pretrained visual prior at initialization and makes the adaptation path more stable.161:T413,The evaluation spans six multi-agent environments across games and robot manipulation, covering both discrete and continuous control spaces. The metrics are aligned with the paper’s claims: visual fidelity, action adherence, agent attribution, and real-time efficiency. The abstract does not expose the full numeric tables, but the experimental structure is clear: compare HAI against weaker action interfaces and test whether the model can maintain independent control for multiple agents while also generalizing across heterogeneous action schemas.

The most informative parts are likely the ablations. In particular: what happens to agent attribution when spatial modulation is removed; how much cross-task action understanding degrades without schema-guided adaptation; whether zero-initialized residual injection improves stability during transfer; and how much control consistency is retained after distilling into a causal streaming model. For a pretraining-oriented reader, these ablations matter more than the headline demo quality.162:T48a,CineEvolve models multi-shot creation as iterative trajectories: initial narrative/shot planning and storyboard generation → defect critique → targeted revision. A single vision-language policy is prompted to act as both Director (create/revise) and Critic (diagnose/score), enabling the critic to evaluate against the director’s own narrative intent.

Training:
- Supervised warm-up on curated trajectories to learn planning, critique language, and revision actions.
- Alternating RL: the Critic is optimized on dynamic storyboard rollouts with composite critic rewards; the Director is optimized for both initial creation and targeted revision using the updated Critic’s self-evaluative scores plus narrative coherence and tool-executability rewards.

E-GRPO targets co-evolution advantage inflation via:
- Historical anchoring: calibrating updates against historical policies/distributions.
- Revision safeguarding: preventing destructive or reward-hacking revisions during refinement.

The system relies on external visual generation tools to render storyboard frames from tool calls; the policy focuses on structured plans and revision instructions.163:T4f3,T-DIG reformulates diverse image-set generation as a conditional generation problem. Given a base prompt and a free-form textual axis of variation, the system should produce K images that differ along that axis while staying aligned with the original prompt. The key design choice is to leave the text-to-image model frozen and instead train an LLM policy that expands the base prompt into K axis-conditioned prompts, or into edit instructions in the editing mode. Those prompts or edits are then executed by a frozen image generator or editor. Training uses GRPO. The reward has two parts: a text-conditioned diversity reward based on TPIPS, which measures whether the image set actually differs along the requested axis, and a baseline-relative alignment penalty that discourages drifting away from the original prompt just to gain diversity. The full system is interactive: users can inspect default samples, receive suggested axes, specify set size and diversity strength, and either regenerate or edit an existing set. Because there is no standard dataset of prompts paired with user-written variation axes, the authors build training and validation data from HPDv2 prompts with VLM-generated axes, and collect a 405-example test set from real user interactions.164:T44e,LoCD has two main stages. First, it localizes a critical span in the student trajectory that should be revised and attributes the relevant privileged context to that span. Second, it performs localized distillation: the privileged teacher continues from the student’s own prefix, regenerates only the localized segment, and the student is trained on that teacher-generated segment without access to the privileged context. Compared with off-policy distillation, the teacher does not take over the entire trajectory, so the training states remain closer to the student’s inference-time distribution. Compared with on-policy distillation, supervision is not restricted to tokens sampled by the student; the method can insert the teacher’s corrected behavior at the point where the student begins to go wrong. The paper also diagnoses a sequential learning bottleneck in on-policy distillation through controlled knowledge injection: longer target answers require progressively more training because later-token supervision becomes useful only after the student starts producing compatible prefixes.165:T99b,方法分两步看更清楚。HeirCommit 解决的是“如何决定是否继承这次更新”。在每一轮，系统从当前 root state St 出发，原生 host 会产生若干 native branches。传统做法通常直接从这些 branch endpoint 中选一个继承。HeirCommit 不这样做。它先冻结候选 successor，然后在与训练、筛选都严格分离的新题池上，把 successor 和当前 root 做对比；只有当 successor 在 fresh probes 上确实优于 root，才 commit，否则保留 root。这里的关键不是又加了一层验证，而是验证对象从 task 变成了 realized transition。作者还强调，若直接复用筛选证据去接受某个 branch，会为多分支搜索支付 union bound，容易把偶然高分当成真实改进；fresh confirmation 则把 proposal bias 和 acceptance evidence 分开。

EvoHeir 则进一步处理 whole-state acceptance 的耦合问题。传统继承把一个分支的 gains 和 losses 打包接受：如果这个分支学到了一些新能力，但也损伤了已有能力，你很难只拿前者不要后者。EvoHeir 把流程拆成 screening、recovery、confirmation 三段。screening 先在 branch endpoint 和当前 root 之间选 recipient，决定下一轮 learner 的参数底座来自谁；这个 recipient 可以是某个 branch，也可以仍是 root。然后做 Experience Recovery：用当前轮和历史 archive 中积累的 reference solutions 去修复 recipient 的失败，同时尽量保留其成功。这样，经验吸收和参数继承被解耦。最后再用 HeirCommit 风格的 fresh confirmation 决定是否接受 recovery 后的 proposal。一个很有意思的设计是：只要经验本身合格，就进入 archive，不受这轮参数是否被继承的影响。于是“参数继承停止”不等于“经验作废”。

从度量上，作者没有只看 accuracy，而是引入更细的状态价值定义。更新审计主要看 correct-target NLL 的变化，因为 accuracy 只能看到答对/答错翻转，看不到模型对正确目标概率质量的真实变化。文中还把 value 分解为 acquired successes 和 lost successes，用来区分“学到了什么”和“丢了什么”。这使得 harmful update 不再只是最终分数下降，而是可以被更细地定位为：某次更新虽然在 admission task 上看似成功，但对独立问题集的正确目标概率没有提升，甚至伤害了已有正确行为。166:T7c8,实验分成两块。第一块是对现有自演化 host 的原生更新做审计和继承规则评估。作者在 R-Zero、Agent0、Skill-SP 三个 host 上检查 native updates，先证明 selection-to-update gap 的存在，再比较不同继承策略。结果是，HeirCommit 在相同 acceptance rate 下，相比随机继承，把被接受更新中的 harmful share 降低了 68–83%，而且在三个 host 上都成立。更重要的是，它不是只减少接受次数来换稳定性；在两类 host 上，原本 native update pool 的负增益被翻成了正增益。这说明问题确实出在“接受了错误的更新”，而不是“根本没有可学内容”。

第二块是完整的十轮 self-evolution。作者在四个 backbone 上跑了十轮、每个方法三种训练 seed：Qwen3-4B-Base、Qwen3-8B-Base、OLMo-3-7B，以及 instruction-tuned 的 Gemma-4-E4B-it。评测覆盖 7 个数学 benchmark 和 5 个通用推理 benchmark。EvoHeir 在四个 backbone 上都拿到最高的数学与通用推理平均分，并且在 48 个 benchmark-backbone 组合里，45 个优于 Agent0。按文中汇总，EvoHeir 让 base model 的数学平均分提升 7.9% 到 30.1%，是对比方法里提升幅度最大的。

几个消融和分析值得注意。其一，Recovery 本身不是简单再微调。用同样 64 条 references，Recovery 比 direct fine-tuning 平均高 1.93 个百分点，说明“修复失败且保留成功”的吸收方式比把参考解直接当监督样本更有效。其二，来自被拒绝轮次模型的经验仍然有用：把这些 rejected-round history 加进来，平均还能再带来 0.66 个百分点。这直接支持了“experience outlives the model that produced it”。其三，作者还指出十个 donor 里有八个 donor 本身弱于当前模型，但它们提供的 references 依然能提升 recipient，说明经验供体不必是更强模型；关键是它在某些局部问题上提供了可吸收的正确信号。167:T784,建议先看 Introduction 和 Figure 1，把 selection-to-update gap、whole-state acceptance、parameter inheritance vs experience inheritance 这三个概念先立住。没有这一步，后面的设计会看成普通的 update gating。

然后重点看 Self-Evolution Environment 那一节和 Figure 2。这里定义了 root state、native branches、archive、screening、recovery、confirmation 这些对象，也说明了训练池、筛选池、确认池、最终评测池是如何严格分离的。这个实验设计很关键，因为这篇工作的说服力很大程度来自“确认证据是 fresh 的”。

方法部分里，优先看 HeirCommit 的 acceptance logic，再看 EvoHeir 的 Recovery。前者回答“为什么必须用 realized transition 做判断”；后者回答“为什么参数和经验要拆开”。如果时间有限，至少把 transition regret、absorption gain、correct-target NLL gain 这几个指标定义读清楚，它们决定了作者如何把 harmful update 从概念变成可审计对象。

实验部分建议先看三类 host 的 update audit 图表，再看四个 backbone 十轮演化的主结果表。审计结果是整篇文章的地基；如果不先确认 native admission 确实经常接纳无益更新，就很难判断后面方法收益来自哪里。最后看 Recovery 和 archive 的消融，尤其是 rejected rounds 经验仍有效的分析，这部分对做 self-training、continual pretrain、RL data replay 的人最有延展性。

如果要深挖，有两个点值得继续想。第一，fresh confirmation 的样本效率和统计功效如何随 probe 数量、分支数、任务噪声变化，这关系到它能否扩展到更大规模在线训练。第二，Experience Recovery 目前依赖 reference solutions 和 archive 质量，未来可以和 verifier、process reward、uncertainty estimation 结合，形成更细粒度的经验吸收机制。168:T42b,The paper isolates a specific failure mode in self-evolving language models: task admission is not the same as learning. Systems such as R-Zero, Agent0, and Skill Self-Play generate tasks, filter those that appear learnable, train on them, and then inherit the resulting model state into the next round. The authors show that this pipeline conflates pre-update task-side evidence with post-update utility. A task can look frontier-level or verifiable before training, yet the optimizer step induced by that task may fail to increase the likelihood of correct answers on fresh questions, or may even damage existing capabilities. They call this mismatch the selection-to-update gap. The audits make the point concrete rather than philosophical: 42–52% of native admissions in Agent0 and R-Zero leave the frontier under independent responses, and 60 out of 96 Skill-SP updates have non-positive correct-target NLL gain. The real decision variable in self-evolution is therefore not which tasks to admit, but which realized successor states are worth carrying forward.169:T49e,The main contribution is not another self-play curriculum mechanism. It is a reframing of self-evolution as a state-selection problem. That matters for pretraining and self-training because once training is closed-loop, a bad inheritance decision contaminates both parameters and future curriculum. Errors compound over rounds. The paper contributes at three levels. First, it sharpens the problem formulation: task-side signals and update value are different objects, and pre-update behavior alone cannot identify whether an optimizer step is beneficial. Second, it proposes a practical correction: HeirCommit accepts an update only after comparing the frozen successor against the current root on fresh probes, while EvoHeir further decouples parameter inheritance from experience inheritance. Third, it provides an empirical lesson with broader relevance: useful experience can outlive the model state that produced it. Even references from rejected rounds can help later learners. That is directly relevant to continual pretraining, self-training, RL-generated data reuse, and any setting where one currently binds data value and parameter value to the same acceptance decision.16a:T96a,HeirCommit addresses the acceptance rule. In each round, the current root state St produces native branches through the host self-evolution loop. Standard systems typically inherit one branch endpoint. HeirCommit instead freezes a candidate successor and evaluates it against the current root on a fresh probe set that is disjoint from training and screening. The system commits the successor only if it beats the root on this new evidence; otherwise it retains the root. The key idea is that acceptance should be based on the realized transition, not on the task that motivated the update. The paper also gives a statistical argument: if one reuses screening evidence to accept among multiple branches, one pays a union-bound penalty over branches and can easily mistake selection noise for genuine improvement. Fresh confirmation removes that coupling.

EvoHeir tackles a deeper issue: whole-state acceptance bundles gains and losses together. A branch may acquire new skills while also degrading old ones, but standard inheritance forces an all-or-nothing choice. EvoHeir splits the round into screening, recovery, and confirmation. Screening chooses the recipient that will supply the next learner’s parameters, from either a branch endpoint or the current root. Recovery then repairs that recipient’s failures using reference solutions drawn from both the current round and an archive of past qualified experience, while trying to preserve existing successes. Confirmation finally applies a HeirCommit-style fresh comparison between the post-recovery proposal and the root. A notable design choice is that qualified experience enters the archive regardless of whether the donor model is inherited. Parameter inheritance can stop without discarding potentially useful experience.

The measurement choices are also important. The paper does not rely only on accuracy. Update audits use correct-target negative log-likelihood gain, which can detect whether the model actually shifts probability mass toward the correct answer even when accuracy stays unchanged. Value is further decomposed into acquired successes and lost successes, making harmful updates observable as specific trade-offs rather than only as end-to-end score drops. This gives the paper a stronger handle on why native self-evolution loops can look productive at the task level while still producing weak or negative state transitions.16b:T86b,There are two main experimental blocks. The first is an audit of native updates from existing self-evolution hosts. The authors analyze R-Zero, Agent0, and Skill-SP, first establishing the selection-to-update gap and then comparing inheritance rules. At the same acceptance rate, HeirCommit reduces the harmful share of accepted updates by 68–83% relative to random inheritance, and this holds on every host. More importantly, the method is not merely becoming conservative by accepting fewer updates. On two of the three hosts, it turns negative pool gain into positive gain, indicating that the issue is indeed poor acceptance of realized updates rather than a lack of learnable material.

The second block is a full ten-round self-evolution study. The paper runs three training seeds per method on four backbones: Qwen3-4B-Base, Qwen3-8B-Base, OLMo-3-7B, and the instruction-tuned Gemma-4-E4B-it. Evaluation covers seven mathematics benchmarks and five general-reasoning benchmarks. EvoHeir achieves the best math and general-reasoning averages on all four backbones, and beats Agent0 on 45 of 48 benchmark–backbone pairs. The reported gain on the base model’s math average ranges from 7.9% to 30.1%, the largest among compared methods.

Several analyses are especially useful. Recovery is not equivalent to simply fine-tuning on the same references: with the same 64 reference solutions, Recovery outperforms direct fine-tuning by 1.93 percentage points on average. That suggests the repair-style absorption procedure is doing something more structured than ordinary supervised replay. The archive analysis is also strong: adding experience from rounds whose models were rejected still yields an additional 0.66 percentage point gain beyond committed-round history. This directly supports the claim that experience can remain valuable even when the producing model state should not be inherited. Finally, eight of ten donors that are weaker than the current model still improve the recipient through their references, showing that an experience donor does not need to be globally stronger; it only needs to contribute locally useful supervision.16c:T823,Start with the introduction and Figure 1. The three ideas to lock in early are the selection-to-update gap, the limitations of whole-state acceptance, and the distinction between parameter inheritance and experience inheritance. Without that framing, the method can look like a generic update-gating trick.

Then read the self-evolution environment section together with Figure 2. This is where the paper defines root state, native branches, archive, screening, recovery, and confirmation, and where it explains the strict separation among training pools, screening pools, confirmation pools, and final evaluation pools. That separation is central to the paper’s credibility because the whole argument depends on fresh evidence.

In the method section, prioritize the HeirCommit acceptance logic first, then EvoHeir’s recovery mechanism. The former explains why realized transitions must be judged directly; the latter explains why parameter choice and experience absorption should be decoupled. If time is limited, at least read the definitions of transition regret, absorption gain, and correct-target NLL gain carefully. Those metrics are what turn “harmful update” from an intuition into an auditable object.

For experiments, read the update-audit figures for the three hosts before the ten-round benchmark tables. The audits are the foundation of the paper. If native admission were already well aligned with positive updates, the rest of the method would matter much less. After that, read the ablations on recovery and archive usage, especially the analysis showing that rejected-round experience still helps. That part has the most direct implications for self-training, continual pretraining, and RL data replay.

Two deeper questions are worth carrying forward. One is how the sample efficiency and statistical power of fresh confirmation scale with probe budget, branch count, and task noise. The other is how Experience Recovery could be combined with verifiers, process rewards, or uncertainty estimates to build a more granular experience-absorption mechanism.16d:T4e0,P2TPO (Page-to-Token Policy Optimization) extends GRPO-style group sampling with structure-aligned, token-level coefficients:
1) Reference-element alignment: parse both prediction and reference into ordered blocks (text/formula/table). Use content-based sequence alignment with insertions/deletions to map each predicted block to a specific reference instance y*_k, preserving identity across rollouts.
2) UAP (Unified Anchor Pricing): convert per-element quality scores s_{i,k} (bounded by c_k) into element coefficients while completing outcomes: matched blocks receive coefficients applied to their spans; missing elements (no generated span) are routed through existing boundary tokens so omissions still generate gradients; tied-but-imperfect cases use a fixed quality ceiling/anchor so centering does not erase signal when all rollouts are equally imperfect.
3) SCR (Span Credit Redistribution): redistribute a matched block’s coefficient within its token span, concentrating negative credit on aligned error positions and positive credit on correct positions, while conserving total credit mass and preserving sign. Final token coefficients combine these local terms with a shared page-level term, keeping full-page AR conditioning intact.16e:T417,RRI has five components. A proposer writes tasks and weighted rubrics. An adversary tries to exploit each rubric. A judge scores answers according to the rubric. A solver is trained from the resulting rewards. A meta-optimizer reads training feedback and confirmed exploits, then rewrites the proposer’s instructions for future task and rubric generation. Each task consists of a request x and a rubric R={(c_j,p_j)}, where c_j is a criterion and p_j is a nonzero weight in [-10,10]. Positive criteria reward required content; negative criteria penalize mistakes or unsafe behavior. Instead of trusting the generated rubric, RRI first compares an honest answer against adversarial answers designed to game the rubric. If the exploit can score too well, the rubric is repaired so that the honest answer wins. The outer loop accumulates these failures into better meta-prompts for future rubrics. The main difference from standard proposer-solver RSI is that the reward itself is recursively improved, not only the task distribution or the solver.16f:T416,The paper reports that nearly 99% of naively generated question-rubric pairs are classified as hackable, indicating that default model-written rewards are weak. On HealthBench Professional with zero training data, RRI-9B and RRI-27B improve adjusted score over the Generation Only self-improvement baseline by 10.9 and 12.4 points. When a frozen 9B model fills every auxiliary role, the gain is still 10.3 points. Adding the adversary to a loop that already co-evolves tasks and rewards adds 2.7 points in the 9B setting. For out-of-domain evaluation, RRI-27B trained only from the HealthBench Professional description improves over the base model by 6.6 points on PRBench Hard and 8.0 points on ProfBench, while Generation Only gains 1.2 and 4.7 points. The analysis covers 12,147 exploits across medical, legal, financial, and scientific tasks, grouped into five reward-failure categories plus incorrect fixes. About one third of the exploits contain wrong content that no criterion penalizes, and another third rely on loosely worded criteria.170:Tb13,方法名 SIF，Selective Internal Feedback。它包含两个核心设计：比较式奖励构造，以及选择性策略更新。

先说作者的诊断。论文先系统分析了 Intuitor 这类方法为什么会坏掉。self-certainty 用的是 token 级预测分布相对均匀分布的 KL，直观上就是模型在某个 token 位置有多“尖锐”、多确定。Intuitor 直接对整条响应的平均 self-certainty 做优化。作者发现这会掩盖序列内部结构：一个答案里某些 token 极高置信，足以把均值拉高，但关键推理步骤可能仍然低置信甚至错误。因此“均值更高”不等于“推理更好”。他们进一步看了 response 内部 self-certainty 的方差，发现训练后期方差升高，说明 certainty 分布越来越分散，均值越来越不可靠。再进一步，他们把 token 按 certainty 排序，只取不同 rank band 的均值做训练，发现高 certainty band 带来快但不稳的早期收益，中间 band 更稳，低 certainty band 信号又太弱。这一系列观察构成了 SIF 的出发点。

SIF 的第一部分是 comparative reward construction。它不再把单个 response 的平均 certainty 直接当 reward，而是先把每个 response 的 token-level certainty 排序，形成 ranked certainty profile，再在多个 certainty 窗口上做比较。这里的窗口不是原始序列中的连续 span，而是 certainty 排名上的区间。然后对同一 prompt 下采样得到的多个 responses 做 peer comparison。只有当一个 response 在多个 certainty level 上都得到足够支持，并且在同组 peer 中也占优时，才给正奖励。这样做的含义是：奖励不再来自“我整体看起来更自信”，而来自“我在多个 certainty 层次上都比同伴更一致地好”。这相当于把单点打分改成多视角排序。

第二部分是 selective policy updates。作者认为即使 reward 已经比较式构造，如果把所有样本都拿去更新，噪声仍会积累。因此他们做了两层过滤。第一层是 sample-level eligibility，只让满足支持条件的 response 参与优化；第二层是 group-level filtering，如果同一 prompt 下整组 responses 的 reward 没有区分度，比如都一样，就跳过这一组，不做策略更新。这样做的目的很直接：只在内部反馈有辨识度时学习，避免把模糊、冲突或低信息量的自反馈硬塞进 PPO/GRPO 式更新里。

从方法定位看，SIF 和依赖 final-answer extraction 的 TTRL 不同，它完全不需要抽取最终答案，也不需要 pseudo-label；和 Intuitor 不同，它不把 self-certainty 当绝对 reward，而是当相对比较信号；和一般的 confidence-based selection 不同，它把“是否更新”也纳入设计，而不是只做 reranking。171:T7d3,实验覆盖三个 backbone，在 MATH 上训练，并在 12 个数学与科学推理 benchmark 上评估，同时还做了 test-time adaptation。摘要给出的主结论是：在三个 backbone 上，SIF 的最终 checkpoint 都优于 Intuitor 和 Vigor 的最佳验证 checkpoint；训练诊断显示后期性能退化明显减轻；test-time adaptation 中，相对初始模型的提升能保持到最终 checkpoint，而不是像基线那样后期回落。

从正文片段能确认的关键实验洞察有几项。第一，作者明确展示了 continued self-certainty optimization 的失败案例：在 Qwen3-1.7B 和 Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct 的报告运行中，self-certainty 持续上升，但 MATH validation accuracy 最终降到 0。这是很强的反例，说明 internal reward 和 correctness 可以严重背离。第二，response 内部 certainty variance 在训练中上升，支持“均值不足以代表推理质量”的论点。第三，不同 certainty rank band 的训练行为差异明显：最高 certainty band 早期涨得快但后期掉得厉害，中间 band 更稳。这直接支撑了 SIF 采用 multi-window ranked comparison，而不是盯住单一 band。

如果按全文精读，实验部分最值得抓的不是单个 benchmark 分数，而是训练动态：batch accuracy、validation accuracy、policy entropy、internal reward 之间的关系。因为这篇文章的主要贡献是让内部反馈训练更稳定，而不是单纯把最终分数再抬一点。还应重点看消融：去掉 sample/group filtering 后是否重新出现后期退化；只做单窗口比较而不做多窗口比较时效果如何；不同窗口设置、group size、奖励阈值对稳定性的影响如何。

当前给出的全文片段没有完整结果表，因此无法可靠列出 12 个 benchmark 的逐项数字、训练步数、采样组大小和所有 backbone 规模。能确定的是作者至少使用了 Qwen3-1.7B、Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct，且是多 backbone 设定。172:Ta50,SIF stands for Selective Internal Feedback. It has two main ingredients: comparative reward construction and selective policy updates.

The paper first diagnoses why prior self-certainty optimization fails. Self-certainty is defined from token-level predictive distributions using KL divergence from the uniform distribution, so it measures how peaked the model’s token distribution is. Methods such as Intuitor optimize the mean self-certainty over the whole response. The authors show that this average is too coarse: a response can have a few highly certain segments that raise the mean while crucial reasoning steps remain uncertain or wrong. They further examine within-response variance of self-certainty and find that it increases during training, which means the certainty profile becomes more dispersed and the mean becomes less representative. They then sort token-level certainty values and train variants using different ranked bands. High-certainty bands give fast early gains but severe late-stage deterioration; intermediate bands are more stable. This analysis motivates the SIF design.

The first component is comparative reward construction. Instead of using a response’s mean certainty as an absolute reward, SIF sorts token-level certainty scores to form a ranked certainty profile and compares responses across multiple certainty windows. These windows are defined over certainty ranks, not contiguous token spans in the original sequence. It also compares peer responses sampled for the same prompt. A response receives positive reward only if it is supported across multiple ranked certainty levels and also wins sufficiently in peer-level comparison. In effect, the reward becomes a multi-view relative preference signal rather than a single scalar confidence score.

The second component is selective policy updates. Even with a better reward, the authors argue that not every sampled response should contribute to optimization. They therefore apply filtering at two levels. At the sample level, only eligible responses with sufficient support participate in policy optimization. At the group level, if all responses for a prompt receive identical rewards, the whole group is skipped because it carries no useful preference information. This design aims to update the policy only when internal feedback is discriminative enough to be trusted.

Compared with TTRL-style methods, SIF does not require final-answer extraction. Compared with Intuitor, it does not treat self-certainty as an absolute objective. Compared with simple confidence-based reranking, it also controls whether learning should happen at all.173:T77f,The experiments train on MATH using three backbones and evaluate on 12 math and science reasoning benchmarks, with additional test-time adaptation experiments on unlabeled inputs. The headline result is that SIF’s final checkpoints outperform the best-validation checkpoints of Intuitor and Vigor on all three backbones. The paper also reports reduced late-stage deterioration and more persistent gains during test-time adaptation.

Several experimental observations from the provided text are especially important. First, the paper documents a strong failure case of continued self-certainty optimization: in reported runs on Qwen3-1.7B and Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, self-certainty keeps increasing while MATH validation accuracy falls to zero. That is a direct demonstration that internal reward and correctness can diverge badly. Second, the within-response variance of certainty rises during training, supporting the claim that the mean certainty is an unstable proxy. Third, different certainty bands behave very differently: the highest-certainty band improves quickly at first but degrades later, while intermediate bands are more stable. This directly motivates the multi-window ranked comparison used by SIF.

When reading the full paper, the most important results are not just final benchmark numbers but the training dynamics: batch accuracy, validation accuracy, internal reward, and policy entropy over time. The main claim is about sustained optimization under internal feedback, so those curves matter more than a small gain on a leaderboard. The key ablations should include removing sample/group filtering, collapsing multi-window comparison into a single window, and varying group size or support thresholds.

The excerpt provided here does not include the full result tables, exact training steps, or all model sizes, so precise benchmark-by-benchmark numbers should be checked in the original paper.174:T4a0,Although labeled skim, this is worth reading a bit more carefully if you work on RL for reasoning. Start with the introduction and especially the observation section. The paper’s strongest contribution is that it first establishes the failure mode of mean self-certainty optimization rather than jumping straight to a new method. Figure 2 and the associated tables are likely the most informative parts: they show early gains, late deterioration, entropy collapse, and the decoupling between internal reward and correctness.

In the method section, focus on two ideas: ranked certainty profiles and selective updates. The first explains how the reward is turned from a crude scalar into a comparative signal across multiple certainty levels. The second explains why the method refuses to learn from every sampled response. Without understanding those two design choices, SIF can look like a minor reward-shaping tweak, which would miss the point.

In the experiments, prioritize training curves, certainty-band analysis, ablations, and test-time adaptation. Final benchmark tables matter, but they are not the main reason to read the paper.

Estimated reading time: 30–40 minutes.175:T8ff,方法叫 Shared Residual Distillation，简称 SRD。它建立在 on-policy self-distillation 框架上，但去掉了参考答案和外部 teacher。核心做法不是直接让学生模仿某一条 peer solution，而是比较“不同 peer 作为附加条件时，冻结教师分布相对一个共同参照发生了哪些一致的变化”。

更具体地说，对同一道题 x，当前策略会采样 K 条解题轨迹。训练某一条 student trajectory 的某个前缀时，作者从同题样本里随机选 M 条 peer solution，再额外取一条来自其他题目的 cross-problem solution 作为 control。冻结的初始模型分别在“student prefix + 某条同题 peer”和“student prefix + cross-problem control”条件下给出 next-token 分布。两者之差可以看成该 peer 对教师分布施加的 residual shift。SRD 不直接平均这些 shift，而是做一个很保守的聚合：只保留那些在多个 peer 上方向一致的坐标，并把保留坐标的幅度截到所有支持该方向的 peer 中最小的那个。然后把这个 shared residual 加回冻结模型在 student 原始输入下的分布，形成 teacher target，学生再用 forward KL 去拟合。

这个设计有几个关键点。第一，cross-problem control 的作用是消掉“给模型额外看一段解答文本”带来的通用风格偏移，只保留与当前题目相关的 peer-induced change。没有这个参照，模型可能学到的是 generic solution-format bias，而不是题目局部推理信息。第二，取最小支持幅度而不是平均，是为了抑制错误 peer 带来的过强偏移，属于一种保守的交集式蒸馏。第三，学生训练时只看题目和自己的前缀，不看 peer；peer 只在训练时用于构造 teacher，因此推理时没有额外开销。这一点和 privileged-information distillation 的设定一致。

和 GRPO、RLVR 的区别很清楚：SRD 不需要 reward，也不需要按答案对错给 trajectory 排序。和标准 OPD 的区别在于，teacher 不是外部更强模型；和 OPSD 的区别在于，训练时也没有 reference answer，只利用同题 peer 的共享局部信号。论文真正的新意就在这里：把“多条未经验证解之间的一致残差”当成 dense token-level supervision。176:T7d7,The method is Shared Residual Distillation (SRD), an on-policy self-distillation scheme without privileged reference answers. The key idea is not to imitate any single peer solution. Instead, SRD measures how different same-problem peers consistently shift a frozen model’s token distribution relative to a shared control.

For a problem x, the current policy samples K trajectories. When training on a student-generated prefix, the method selects M same-problem peers and one cross-problem solution as a control. A frozen copy of the initial model predicts next-token distributions under two conditions: the student prefix plus a same-problem peer, and the student prefix plus the cross-problem control. Their difference is a peer-induced residual shift. SRD then aggregates these residuals conservatively: it keeps only coordinates whose direction agrees across peers, and sets the retained magnitude to the smallest supporting magnitude among those peers. This shared residual is added back to the frozen model’s distribution under the original student input, producing a teacher target. The student is trained with forward KL on that target.

Three design choices matter. First, the cross-problem control removes generic distribution shifts caused by simply appending a solution-like text, so the retained residual is more problem-specific. Second, the minimum-supported magnitude acts as a conservative intersection rule, reducing the influence of noisy or wrong peers. Third, peers are used only to construct the teacher during training; the student itself conditions only on the problem and its own prefix, so inference cost does not increase.

Compared with RLVR or GRPO, SRD needs no reward and no answer-level ranking. Compared with standard on-policy distillation, it does not rely on an external stronger teacher. Compared with prior on-policy self-distillation, it does not require reference answers. The novelty is the use of shared peer-induced residuals as dense token-level supervision.177:T56d,The main experiments are on mathematical reasoning with Qwen3-1.7B, 4B, and 8B base models. The headline AIME24–26 avg@12 numbers reported in the paper are substantial: 11.02 to 16.20 for 1.7B, 19.07 to 45.46 for 4B, and 21.39 to 54.44 for 8B. The gains are especially large for 4B and 8B, suggesting that SRD can extract useful local supervision from same-problem samples rather than acting as a mild regularizer. The paper also reports improvements on the Harvard–MIT Mathematics Tournament benchmarks.

On general-capability checks, performance on IFEval and MMLU-Pro is maintained relative to the corresponding base models, which is important because it suggests the reasoning gains are not coming from a narrow trade-off. The ablations highlighted in the abstract indicate that two ingredients matter: the cross-problem residual reference and the conservative magnitude rule. That is consistent with the method’s goal: in the absence of correctness signals, it is safer to learn only the stable overlap among peers than to amplify any single trajectory’s bias.

The provided excerpt does not include full training details such as dataset size, K/M choices, number of updates, or complete ablation tables, so it would be unsafe to invent those specifics. Still, the reported benchmark gains are large enough to make the method notable within label-free reasoning post-training.178:T825,The key move is to formulate the gap between reverse CoT and verified forward CoT as a translation problem rather than a prompting problem.

Let q be the question and a the correct answer. Forward CoT (FCG) samples reasoning from the teacher conditioned only on q. Rejection sampling (RS) keeps only those forward samples whose extracted final answer matches a. Reverse CoT (RCG) instead conditions the teacher on both q and a. The authors argue that the student should ideally learn from the RS distribution, not from raw RCG outputs.

To do this, they build a small paired dataset. For each question, they sample one reverse CoT response x, then sample forward CoTs until they obtain the first accepted response z with the correct final answer. This yields paired examples (x, z). A translator model G_phi is then fine-tuned with teacher forcing to predict z from x.

A crucial design choice is that the translator only receives the reverse CoT text x, not the original question q or answer a. This serves two purposes. First, it matches the paper’s distributional derivation, where the goal is to map source responses to target responses. Second, it blocks a direct question-answer shortcut and forces the model to learn how to rewrite answer-conditioned rationales into outputs closer to accepted forward reasoning.

Once trained, the translator is used at scale: each new question requires one reverse teacher call to produce x and one translator call to produce z-hat, and the student is then trained on (q, z-hat). Compared with RS, which may need many forward teacher calls per accepted sample, this pipeline compresses the expensive part into one cheap teacher sample plus one translation step.

Relative to prior semantic suppression or structural-guidance methods, the difference is conceptual. Those methods still generate under answer access and try to reduce leakage. CoTranslator instead learns an explicit distributional correction from RCG-style outputs toward RS-style outputs. The appendix further provides a distribution-recovery analysis to justify this framing.179:T609,The experiments cover six student models and six math benchmarks, with transfer tests to a new math dataset, a different teacher model, and STEM problems.

The first headline result is quality. For students such as Qwen3-4B-Base, CoTranslator improves average accuracy over semantic suppression by up to 5.82 percentage points. That indicates that merely hiding answer cues is not enough; explicit translation toward the verified forward distribution works better.

The second result is the cost-performance trade-off. The two 4B students retain 95.0% of the average accuracy of rejection sampling while using only 35.9% of its estimated compute. This is the central empirical claim of the paper. RS remains the cleaner target, but it is expensive; CoTranslator uses a small paired set to train a translator and then amortizes that cost over large-scale data generation.

The third result is transfer. Without retraining, the translator generalizes to a new math dataset, a different teacher, and STEM tasks. Average STEM gains are 4.88 points for 4B students and 4.31 points for 8B students. This suggests the translator is learning a reusable transformation from answer-conditioned rationales to more question-grounded ones, rather than memorizing a dataset-specific template.

The paper also includes analysis showing that translated outputs are closer to RS responses and exhibit fewer answer-dependent shortcuts than raw reverse CoTs. Those analyses are important because they explain why the downstream gains appear, not just that they do.17a:T443,This one is worth a careful skim, close to a light read. Start with the formal definitions of FCG, RCG, and RS. The paper only makes sense once the target distribution is clear. Then read the paired-data construction and the translator objective, paying special attention to the decision not to feed q or a into the translator. That is the most consequential design choice in the method.

In the experiments, prioritize three groups of results: the main comparison against RS, RCG, and semantic suppression; the compute-cost comparison; and the transfer results. A 30-40 minute pass is enough to capture the main idea. If you want the deeper layer, read the appendix on distribution recovery and the shortcut analyses.

Two questions are worth carrying while reading. Is the translator learning a superficial style rewrite, or a structural transformation that is genuinely closer to forward reasoning? And how far does the method extend beyond math, especially when answer verification is weak and the reasoning space is less constrained? Those questions define the boundary of the approach.17b:T73d,1) Formalizing aggregation-induced drift as multi-reward hacking
- Consider a primary reward r_p (correctness) and an auxiliary reward r_a (brevity/latency/style).
- Key assumption: auxiliary rewards are more reliably attainable than primary rewards (you can be short/fast without solving the task).
- Study symmetric aggregation rules that treat channels equally and assign positive credit to single-channel success (including auxiliary-only success).
- In a one-step stochastic decision model, prove that under this imbalance, deterministic conditional-mean GRPO dynamics converge to auxiliary-favoring behavior from any initialization, even if the initial policy prefers the primary objective.
- Further characterize when this constitutes reward hacking relative to an unknown true reward.

2) Defense: Trust-Anchored Gating (TAG)
- Two design questions: which channel should be prioritized, and how to enforce that priority.
- Anchor selection via drift: briefly optimize each channel in isolation and pick the channel that induces the least policy drift as the anchor (intuition: exploitable channels cause large shortcut-driven shifts).
- Gated aggregation: break symmetry by construction—auxiliary-only success is scored no better than failing both channels, while joint success remains better than primary-only success.
- Provide a convergence guarantee: with the primary channel as anchor and assuming primary success remains achievable, TAG drives conditional-mean GRPO to the primary-favoring action from any initialization, for any positive gating weight.

3) Why not simple reweighting
- The paper argues and empirically shows that lowering auxiliary weights can delay but not prevent collapse, and that “safe” weights do not transfer across scales. TAG removes the main exploit path by eliminating extra credit for aux-only outcomes.17c:T41c,Empirical validation on Qwen and Llama models (1.7B–30B), across math and program synthesis, with both compatible and incompatible auxiliary rewards:
- Reproduces the characteristic failure: auxiliary success rate approaches 1 and aggregated objective increases, while primary correctness/pass rate collapses; policies exhibit shortcut behaviors (ultra-short guesses for brevity, immediate-exit programs for latency, answer negation to satisfy sign checks, etc.).
- Shows that symmetric multi-reward methods that rebalance channels but remain symmetric (e.g., MO-GRPO, PG-OT) can collapse similarly in their settings.
- TAG substantially mitigates primary-task degradation while retaining auxiliary benefits in most settings.
  - Concrete number reported: on Qwen3-4B with a brevity reward, TAG reaches 0.581 pass@4 (vs 0.220 for additive aggregation) while producing responses 44% shorter than correctness-only training.
- Includes evidence that reducing auxiliary weight only delays collapse and that a weight safe at one scale can fail at another.17d:T769,The core idea is replay-driven decoupling. Rather than forcing the trainer to wait for a newly collected on-policy batch, ReFlow maintains a buffer of recent trajectories and allows optimization to proceed continuously by sampling from that replay pool while rollout workers asynchronously add fresh data. The point is not to import generic off-policy RL wholesale, but to exploit short-horizon sample reuse without letting policy mismatch grow too large.

The design appears to have three layers. First, execution-level decoupling: rollout and training are disaggregated so the learner is no longer tightly gated by fresh generation. This directly reduces long-tail bubbles caused by variable decoding and environment latency. Second, algorithmic support for replay: recently generated samples are reused under staleness-aware controls and correction mechanisms so that replay improves efficiency without drifting too far from the current policy. The paper also claims a theoretical result that replay can reduce gradient variance, which is relevant because LLM RL suffers from noisy rewards and large sequence-level variance. Third, runtime adaptivity: instead of fixing rollout/training resource splits and generation concurrency, ReFlow adjusts them as workload characteristics shift over time.

Relative to standard asynchronous actor-learner systems, the differences are clear. Existing designs usually tolerate only mild stale on-policy data to hide some generation latency. ReFlow goes further and treats replay as the main lever for reducing rollout demand. Existing systems also tend to treat resource allocation as a static tuning problem; ReFlow makes adaptation part of the system design. At the same time, the paper seems careful not to push into fully off-policy RL with very old data. The emphasis is on recent replay, which matches the stability requirements of LLM post-training.17e:T569,From the available full-text portion, the experimental agenda is clear even though the exact tables are missing. First, the paper needs to show end-to-end efficiency gains: less trainer idle time, better GPU utilization, and shorter wall-clock training, especially on multi-turn agentic workloads with heavy latency tails. Second, it needs to establish the quality-efficiency trade-off: compared with synchronous RL, mild asynchronous baselines, and variants without replay or with restricted replay, ReFlow should achieve similar quality with fewer fresh rollouts or better quality under the same time budget. Third, it needs stability and ablation evidence: replay ratio, freshness window, staleness control, and adaptive scheduling should each be tested, and the claimed variance-reduction effect should have empirical support.

First, a Traceable Multi-View Event Bank compiles heterogeneous histories—dialogues, documents, factual records—into source-traceable event units. Second, Evidence-State Transition Modeling casts the memory policy as a finite-horizon MDP. This makes stopping explicit and treats non-writing after retrieval as a first-class decision rather than an implicit threshold. The key design choice is that rewards are conditioned on the current evidence state and trajectory context, so the model evaluates whether an action is appropriate at that point, not whether a text snippet looks good in isolation. The gains are not tied to a single backbone, which makes the result more about the dataset itself than about a narrow model-specific interaction.185:T446,CleaningGridWorld is a 5×5 environment with four dirt cells and one fixed disposal bin. The action set contains four moves, vacuum, and cover. The proxy reward counts cells that no longer look dirty to a cheap sensor, while the true reward counts only real disposal events. Covering dirt and vacuuming it can both improve the proxy signal, but only carrying dirt to the bin improves the true objective. The baseline agent is a compact DQN: a 126-dimensional encoded state, two 128-unit ReLU hidden layers, and six Q-values. Because rewards are sparse, the authors add potential-based reward shaping using Manhattan distance to the current objective, with a continuous potential across the pickup-to-delivery transition. The mitigation is a Lagrangian constrained RL variant with a cost signal targeting the discovered exploit mechanisms. Its main technical point is not the DQN architecture, but the explicit cost construction and the identity connecting proxy reward, true reward, and cost, which yields a deterministic lower bound on true-objective performance in a hard-constrained version.186:T90e,CATCH is an adaptation of Continuous Adversarial Training (CAT). For each prompt x that contains pressure to misstate a proposition, the method constructs two target continuations: y+ is the honest answer consistent with the model’s knowledge or the provided context, and y- is the dishonest answer that complies with the pressure and asserts the opposite. Training then pushes the model toward y+ and away from y-.

This differs from refusal-style safety training in an important way. In harmful-query refusal, the positive target can often be a generic refusal string, so standard supervised or adversarial training has a shared target structure. Honesty does not have that convenience: both the truthful and dishonest continuations are instance-specific, because they depend on the proposition and context. That is one reason plain SFT is a weak baseline here. It can memorize seen prompt patterns, but it does not naturally optimize for robustness to new forms of pressure or strategic settings.

The key mechanism is targeted adversarial training in embedding space. Instead of searching over discrete prompt edits, which is too expensive, the method perturbs token embeddings within an epsilon-bounded region and uses projected signed gradient ascent for K steps to approximately maximize log p_theta(y- | x + delta). This yields a local worst-case prompt perturbation that makes the dishonest continuation more likely. The outer optimization then trains the model to suppress y- and favor y+ under those adversarially perturbed inputs. In effect, the model is not just trained to answer honestly on the original prompt, but to remain honest in a neighborhood of semantically nearby adversarial variants.

The paper also pays attention to capability preservation. CATCH is trained with a utility dataset in addition to honesty targets, and the authors explicitly study how the choice of that utility data affects general performance retention. That is a meaningful detail: if the method only improved honesty by broadly dampening compliance or increasing refusals, it would be much less interesting. Compared with inference-time honesty steering, CATCH aims for a more stable trained behavior. Compared with large-scale honesty SFT, it relies on adversarial objectives to get more transfer from much less data.187:T67d,Several concrete points are clear from the full text provided. First, M_k is used as the teacher to recover M_k′ through on-policy distillation. The student samples trajectories from its current policy, and the teacher provides dense token-level next-token distributions along those trajectories; the KL objective uses stop-gradient teacher logits. This stage repairs the behavioral disruption caused by increasing k. Second, the recovered M_k′ is improved with RLVR, using SAPO to reduce instability from the mismatch between rollout and training policies. Compared with self-distillation using privileged hints, the method does not require hand-designed intermediate signals or ground-truth partial solutions.189:T530,The proposed framework, Beacon, has two components: Safety Signal Recovery (SSR) and Safety-Utility Decoupled Alignment (SUDA). SSR addresses the missing-gradient problem. First, it uses advantage-guided trajectory filtering to retain rollout subsets that still preserve informative relative differences, instead of treating every sampled response equally when the group is already degenerate. Second, when the relative signal fully collapses, it introduces safe reference supervision so that all-unsafe groups do not become gradient-free regions. This is the key design choice: rather than relying purely on GRPO’s relative rewards, the method injects an external safe anchor exactly where relative optimization breaks down. SUDA addresses the safety tax. Harmful and benign prompts are handled differently through category-aware rewards, and KL anchoring is applied primarily on benign prompts. The motivation is straightforward: if the same conservative pressure is imposed everywhere, the model tends to over-refuse. By decoupling harmful-prompt safety optimization from benign-prompt utility preservation, Beacon tries to improve safety without collapsing helpfulness. Two questions are worth keeping in mind while reading: whether safe reference supervision effectively turns the method back into imitation-heavy alignment in hard regions, and whether the same failure persists under richer reward models rather than binary safety rewards.18c:T457,LongForge has an analyzer and a synthesizer. The analyzer reconstructs each QA example into an evidence-assertion reasoning graph. Evidence nodes are verbatim spans from the document. Assertion nodes are the answer sentences. A hyperedge represents a reasoning step where evidence spans and/or previous assertions support one assertion. This design prevents the analyzer from inventing external evidence or adding reasoning chains not present in the answer. Four graph-based metrics are then computed: breadth, the number of distinct evidence spans used; depth, the longest evidence-to-terminal-assertion path after paraphrase contraction; correctness, the fraction of supported reasoning steps; and completeness, the fraction of requested information points answered by supported assertions. The synthesizer uses correctness and completeness as gates, with failure reasons fed back for re-answering. Breadth and depth are measured and later controlled through dataset mixing rather than optimized directly during generation, which reduces the risk of producing answers that look multi-step only on the surface.18d:T885,方法名是 TreeOPSD，核心由两步组成。

第一步是 tree-aware credit construction。作者利用多轮交互天然存在的前缀分叉结构：对同一个历史前缀，采样多个后续 continuation，形成 rollout tree。这样可以把“某个 turn 之后的选择是否有帮助”与此前历史解耦。然后在树上做 recursive backup，把叶子节点的终局 verifier reward 回传成各个 turn 的 backed-up credit。这里的关键不是简单把终局 reward 平均分摊到所有 token，而是利用共享前缀下不同分支的结果差异，得到更细粒度的 turn-level 相对信用。

第二步是 posterior self-distillation。作者不是直接拿 backed-up credit 做 REINFORCE/PPO 权重，而是相对于冻结的行为策略 π_old，通过一个仿射映射把每个 turn 的 credit 变成一个有界的 teacher distribution。这个 teacher 是“后验”意义上的目标分布：高 credit 的动作概率被抬高，低 credit 的动作概率被压低，但整体仍 anchored 在行为策略上，因此不会失控。随后训练当前策略 π_θ 去最小化与 teacher 的 Forward-KL。作者强调两个性质：1）在 π_θ = π_old 的切点处，这个 distillation objective 的梯度与 tree policy gradient 一致；2）随着当前策略接近 teacher，梯度会自然衰减，到达目标后为零，若超过目标则反向，因而比固定 advantage 权重的多轮 mini-batch 更新更稳定。

文中还给出一个结构性质：由于 credit 到 target distribution 的仿射映射与 tree backup 可交换，父节点目标的匹配在梯度上等价于对子孙节点蒸馏损失的聚合。这一点很重要，因为它说明 turn-level target 不是拍脑袋定义，而是和树上的递归 credit 传播保持一致。

与 PPO 的区别很清楚：PPO 仍是 ratio-weighted policy gradient，加 clipping 抑制过大偏移；TreeOPSD 则把优化对象从“沿某个梯度方向上升”改成“逼近一个冻结 teacher 分布”。与 OPD/OPSD 的区别在于 teacher 不来自外部强模型，也不依赖 privileged context，而是直接由 rollout tree + terminal reward 构造。18e:T417,The paper tackles two coupled problems in long-horizon agentic RL with verifiable rewards. First, when supervision comes only from a terminal verifier reward, intermediate turns receive extremely sparse and noisy credit. Broadcasting one trajectory-level advantage across the whole rollout over-credits irrelevant actions in successful runs and under-credits useful actions in failed ones. Second, when a fixed rollout batch is reused across sequential mini-batch updates, the current policy drifts away from the behavior policy that generated the data, creating policy staleness. Existing methods usually address one side at a time: critics or process reward models provide denser supervision but add training complexity and their own failure modes, while PPO-style importance weighting and clipping control drift without defining a finite target that the optimization can converge to. The paper aims to derive turn-level supervision directly from rollout trees and terminal rewards, then turn the RL update into a posterior distillation problem.18f:T9fa,The method, TreeOPSD, has two main components.

The first is tree-aware credit construction. Multi-turn interaction naturally exposes branching prefixes: from the same history prefix, one can sample multiple alternative continuations, forming a rollout tree. This isolates the effect of decisions made after a given turn while holding the preceding context fixed. Terminal verifier rewards at the leaves are then recursively backed up through the tree to produce turn-level credit. The point is not to spread a final reward uniformly across all tokens, but to exploit outcome differences among sibling branches under a shared prefix to obtain more informative relative credit for each turn.

The second is posterior self-distillation. Instead of plugging the backed-up credit directly into REINFORCE or PPO weights, the method maps turn-level credit through an affine transformation relative to the frozen behavior policy π_old, producing a bounded teacher distribution for each turn. This teacher can be interpreted as a posterior target: actions with higher backed-up credit get their probability increased, lower-credit actions get suppressed, but the target remains anchored to the behavior policy. The current policy π_θ is then trained to minimize a Forward-KL divergence to this teacher.

Two properties are central. First, at the tangent point where π_θ equals π_old, the gradient of the distillation objective recovers the exact tree policy-gradient direction. Second, unlike a fixed collection-time advantage weight, the student-teacher residual shrinks as the student approaches the target, becomes zero at the target, and reverses sign after overshoot. That gives the optimization a finite destination and is the paper’s answer to sequential mini-batch staleness.

The paper also claims a structural result: because the affine map from credit to target distribution commutes with tree backup, matching a backed-up parent target is gradient-equivalent to aggregating descendant distillation losses. This is important because it ties the target construction to the recursive tree credit mechanism rather than treating it as an ad hoc heuristic.

Relative to PPO, the difference is conceptual and practical: PPO remains a ratio-weighted policy-gradient method with clipping, whereas TreeOPSD turns the update into distribution matching against a frozen target. Relative to OPD or OPSD, the teacher is not supplied by an external stronger model or privileged context; it is constructed directly from the rollout tree and terminal rewards.190:T645,From the available full text, the empirical story centers on improved agentic performance across competitive benchmarks and across model scales, plus evidence that the method induces longer interaction chains in a Deep Research setting. The latter matters because it suggests the method is not only improving short-horizon answer selection, but also encouraging sustained exploration and multi-step tool use.

The most important comparisons are likely these. First, against PPO- or GRPO-style advantage-based methods, does TreeOPSD degrade more gracefully as the horizon grows? Second, against critic-based, PRM-based, or teacher-distillation baselines, can it remain competitive without introducing extra learned models or external teachers? Third, under more sequential mini-batch updates per rollout batch, does it remain more stable, which would directly support the stale-policy argument?

If there are ablations, the most informative ones will be those removing tree backup, the affine posterior mapping, or the Forward-KL objective one at a time.191:T431,For a skim, start with the introduction and the main method figure, and separate the paper into two questions: how it assigns turn-level credit, and how it stabilizes optimization under policy drift. If those pieces are clear, the rest of the paper becomes much easier to parse.
